The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(π/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(π/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.
Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three

The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.
Additive Fréchet Regression for Random Objects
Changwon Choi; Wookyeong Song; Hans-Georg Müller; Byeong U. Park

Regression analysis for complex data taking values in a general metric space has gained increasing attention in recent years, particularly in the context of Fréchet regression with Euclidean predictors $\mathbb{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{p}$. However, local Fréchet regression, while more flexible than global Fréchet regression, suffers from the curse of dimensionality for the case of multivariate predictors. To address this issue while maintaining model flexibility, we introduce a framework of additive structured nonparametric regression when responses are situated in a general metric space. Overcoming the challenge of the lack of vector space structure in general metric spaces where the responses reside requires a novel approach that incorporates the additive structure via projection operators. This leads to a unified framework of additive regression for a wide range of response types, including one-dimensional distributions in Wasserstein space, network data represented by graph Laplacians and spherical data equipped with geodesic distances, among others. We establish pointwise and uniform consistency, including convergence rates, for the proposed additive Fréchet regression estimators, using smooth backfitting. The practical utility of this additive model is demonstrated through applications to brain connectivity network analysis using resting-state fMRI data and distributional physical activity data.
A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
Onur Beker; A. René Geist; Michael Posa; Marc Toussaint; Justin Carpentier; Georg Martius

Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.
Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
Emiel Claasen; Mehregan Doroudiani; Claude Duhr; Axel Kleinschmidt; Franca Lippert; Oliver Schlotterer; Yoann Sohnle

The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $Γ(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.
Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
Adrián Casado-Turrión; Paulo B. Ferraz; Mindaugas Karčiauskas; José Jaime Terente Díaz

In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.
Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications

We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.
Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$

In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.
Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
Rami Atar; Leonid Mytnik; Dominic T. Schickentanz

We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.
Stochastic counterpart of Nesterov's method for sampling and provable non-acceleration of samplers with heavy-ball structure

Polyak's heavy-ball method and Nesterov's method are two momentum-based methods that have inspired many optimization techniques used in applied fields, including machine learning. Momentum also provides a connection with sampling, and interestingly, many kinetic Langevin samplers reduce to the heavy-ball recurrence when velocity is eliminated and noise is removed. This observation motivates a natural question: what is the corresponding sampler for Nesterov's method? We propose a sampler whose deterministic part is exactly Nesterov's recurrence, driven by temporally correlated Gaussian noise and requires one new gradient evaluation per step. Noise correlation provides $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ bias for smooth observables. We establish geometric ergodicity for possibly non-convex potentials. For strongly convex potentials with Lipschitz continuous gradients, we obtain contraction rates and show that, up to an additive constant, the energy decays at a rate of order $κ^{-1/2}$, where $κ$ is the condition number. For Gaussian targets, we show that relaxation has square-root dependence on $κ$. We further prove that any sampler based on heavy-ball dynamics with additive noise cannot achieve accelerated convergence uniformly over the class of strongly convex functions. Finally, we compare the proposed sampler with OBABO, BAOAB, HMC, MALA, BPS, and NUTS in numerical experiments and demonstrate the better performance of proposed sampler.
Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Site AI Data Centers in Day-Ahead Markets

AI data centers are among the fastest-growing loads on the power grid, and their flexibility is increasingly sought by grid operators. Using it requires a model that links what an operator controls, namely GPU power caps, job timing and job placement, to the power drawn at each site and the electricity prices it faces. This paper develops such a framework for a multi-site AI data-center fleet. It represents GPU power-cap levels; deferrable jobs with deadlines and inference with response-time headroom; and site facility power, and casts the fleet schedule as a linear program solved on day-ahead prices. A year-long simulation on 2025 California Independent System Operator (CAISO) day-ahead prices in three data-center markets demonstrates the framework. Coordinated scheduling lowers the fleet's energy cost by 6.3% at equal work. Four operating modes, each adding one capability, split this saving into efficient GPU operation that needs no price signal, price response in time, and routing work between sites.
Global regularity in optimal transportation under the A3w condition
Yuanyuan Li; Xianduo Wang; Xu-jia Wang

We prove global $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2,p}$ estimates for potentials in optimal transportation under A3w condition. The cost satisfies condition A3w, and the domains are mutually uniformly $c$-convex with $C^2$ boundaries. We prove global $W^{2,p}$ estimates for positive continuous densities and we obtain global $C^{2,α}$ estimates for positive $C^α$ densities.
On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
Melda Akyazi-Zavadski; Nathanaël Berestycki; Sunil Chhita

The completely packed $O(1)$ loop model can be viewed as an interface representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice. We consider submatching events, which prescribe how these interfaces pair finitely many consecutive boundary points. Romik's rationality conjectures predict that the probabilities of these events on the semi-infinite cylinder are given by specific rational functions, which even become dyadic rationals in the half-plane limit.
 We derive explicit Pfaffian formulae for the probability of $k$ nested arches on the semi-infinite cylinder of circumference $2N$, valid for $k<N$. We deduce that these probabilities are rational functions of $N$ and, by taking the limit $N\to\infty$, that the corresponding half-plane probabilities remain rational. This establishes key aspects of Romik's conjectures.
 Our proof uses identities of Fonseca and Zinn-Justin, derived through the qKZ formalism, which express these probabilities as ratios of enumeration numbers for totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions (TSSCPPs). These plane partitions admit a dimer representation, allowing us to apply Kasteleyn theory. We evaluate the resulting hypergeometric sum using Zeilberger's and Gosper's algorithms and then take the half-plane limit $N\to\infty$. Along the way, we derive a somewhat simplified expression for the inverse Kasteleyn matrix entries (encoding correlations in TSSCPPs) of Ayyer and Chhita, which might be of independent interest.
Optimal Control in Pairs Trading with Negative-Power Utility

We solve a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and utility $U(x)=-x^{-γ}$, $γ>0$. Linearizing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation gives explicit formulas for the value function and the optimal feedback control. A budget inequality and concavity verify optimality over all admissible strategies with nonnegative wealth on every finite horizon, without Novikov's condition. Under the optimal feedback, wealth and consumption admit deterministic upper bounds when the interest rate $r$ is at most the mean-reversion rate $κ$. If $r>κ$, each exceeds any prescribed level with positive probability at every time after the start. If $r>\sqrt{2+γ} κ$, there is an explicit critical horizon at and beyond which expected terminal wealth is infinite, while optimal expected utility is finite. When the critical time falls before maturity, expected wealth at that time is finite exactly when the initial spread is zero. We also show that the suprema of the negative powers of optimal wealth and consumption are integrable on every finite horizon exactly for orders $0<m\le 1+γ$.
Topological notions of Shadowing under Semi-Conjugacy

We study various notions of shadowing and investigate whether they are preserved under semi-conjugacy and inverse limits. In particular, we study Inverse shadowing, $H$-shadowing, Periodic shadowing, Ramsey shadowing, Density shadowing and Ergodic shadowing.
Edge cuts of bounded degree in sparse graphs
Anna Neopryatnaya; Vladimir Verdenko; Vsevolod Voronov

Every simple graph on $n \ge 2$ vertices with at most $2n-2$ edges can be split into two nonempty parts with at most two crossing edges at each vertex. For $d \ge 3$ we bound the minimum number of edges in an n-vertex graph without a d-cut.

For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.
Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
Erik Fink; Jingqian Gou; Niklas Holbach; Ondrej Hulik

We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.
Nematic equilibria on a Möbius strip: topology and extrinsic curvature
Massimo Frittelli; Sébastien Fumeron; Gaetano Napoli

We investigate the equilibrium configurations of a nematic liquid crystal confined in a thin tubular neighbourhood of a Möbius strip. Assuming degenerate tangential anchoring and a director uniform across the thickness, we derive an effective two-dimensional Frank energy that accounts for both the intrinsic and extrinsic curvature of the mid-surface. The non-orientability of the substrate imposes identification conditions that couple the reversal of the local frame to the head-to-tail symmetry of the nematic director. We show that the resulting topological classification depends on the parity of the number of half-twists: the sector index is a winding number for even parity, whereas only its parity is physically meaningful for odd parity, in which case the net director rotation is not quantised. We analyse the narrow-strip limit and solve the full two-dimensional equilibrium problem by finite-element methods. The competition between topological sectors depends on the strip aspect ratio and elastic anisotropy. In particular, for a single half-twist, the preferred sector changes at an aspect ratio of approximately 0.58, while for two half-twists two distinct minima of the same sector exchange their energy ordering near 0.60, without any change of topology. These results reveal how non-orientable topology and extrinsic curvature jointly shape nematic equilibria on curved substrates.
A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation

Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$φ$ formulation compared to gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. The results indicate that edge elements can be used to furnish reasonable results for general loading conditions, whereas penalized $H^1$ elements fail (e.g., converge to an incorrect state) even with mesh refinement.
Pathwise uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with a $3/4$-Hölder diffusion coefficient
Pei-Sen Li; Jie Xiong; Xu Yang

For every $γ\in[3/4,1]$, we prove pathwise uniqueness and strong existence for the stochastic heat equation on $\mathbb{R}$ with space-time white noise, Lipschitz drift, and a diffusion coefficient locally $γ$-Hölder under suitable growth bounds. The result settles the critical case $γ=3/4$ left open by Mueller, Mytnik and Perkins. The proof is based on a newly developed short-time linear comparison method. On each short interval, we compare the difference of two solutions with an auxiliary linear process. An expected weighted $L^1$ bound independent of the noise multiplier, together with a vanishing sum of approximation errors, yields pathwise uniqueness. The method may also apply to other SPDEs admitting analogous linear comparison and stochastic convolution estimates.
Minimization of free energy in a Poisson--Boltzmann problem
Shahid Ali; Klemen Bohinc; Angeles Martinez; Stefano Maset

In this paper, we study a mathematical model in which an ionic solution composed of several types of spherical ions is confined between two uniformly charged parallel planes. The ion concentrations at equilibrium, determined by the interplay between thermal and electrostatic effects, are obtained by minimizing the free energy of the system. The resulting minimization problem is infinite-dimensional, and we prove the existence and uniqueness of its solution by means of a norm-convergence direct method based on the Banach--Saks property of the space in which the problem is posed. The existence proof is technically challenging because the functional to be minimized is not coercive in general. Three illustrative problems are considered and solved numerically.

Two subsets $A,B$ of a finite set $X$ are crossing if $A\cap B$, $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, and $X\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all nonempty. A family is $k$-cross-free if it contains no $k$ pairwise crossing members. We construct such families on $n$ elements of size $(\frac{1}{3}+o(1))kn\log k$, where the asymptotic is taken as $k$ tends to infinity and is uniform over all integers $n\ge k$. This disproves the uniform $O(kn)$ bound conjectured by Karzanov and Lomonosov. Our construction consists of cyclic intervals with at most one point deleted, together with their complements. We also prove an $O(kn\log k)$ upper bound for $k$-cross-free families closed under all cyclic shifts of a fixed cyclic ordering of the ground set.
Anytime-valid inference for time series via self-normalization

We develop a self-normalized approach to constructing asymptotic confidence sequences for a broad class of parameters of stationary time series under weak dependence. Our theory covers nonlinear marginal parameters, including quantiles, expectiles and expected shortfall, as well as autoregressive coefficients. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first use of self-normalization to construct asymptotic confidence sequences for time series. A key advantage is that the construction avoids direct estimation of the long-run variance, which can be particularly challenging for nonlinear parameters under serial dependence. Following an initial burn-in period of length $m$, confidence intervals are released sequentially, with simultaneous coverage over all subsequent times converging to $1-α$ as $m\to\infty$. We propose two sequential self-normalizers with complementary statistical and computational advantages. The forward construction uses only the history of sequential parameter estimates, leading to minimal computational overhead. The three-block construction typically yields narrower confidence sequences and is compatible with the optimal law-of-the-iterated-logarithm width rate. Together, these constructions extend the benefits of self-normalization to sequential inference under dependence. We investigate their finite-sample performance through simulations and illustrate their use in Markov chain Monte Carlo output analysis in the supplementary appendix.
Remark on Kobayashi's conjecture: a volume Schwarz lemma

This remark offers an expository reconstruction of OpenAI's proof of Kobayashi's ampleness conjecture for compact Kähler manifolds, together with new results. We extract a volume Schwarz lemma for extremal discs and derive a pointwise volume comparison: the volume form of a Kähler metric with $\mathrm{Ric}(ω)\ge-ω$ is bounded below by an intrinsic volume form built from the Kähler--Einstein metrics of pseudoconvex domains containing the Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix. As a consequence, if a compact Kähler manifold $X$ has nef canonical bundle and its Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix is bounded at some point, then $X$ is of general type.
Simple Private Noisy SGD is Minimax-Optimal under Population Strong Convexity

Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is at the center of modern machine learning and is known to be statistically minimax-optimal in many regression settings, e.g., for convex Generalized Linear Models (GLMs). Yet, it is unknown whether its simplest differentially private Noisy SGD counterpart fulfills similar favorable guarantees even on strongly convex losses. We resolve this question affirmatively. We upper bound the parameter estimation error for a single pass of Noisy SGD with a fixed stepsize schedule and constant batch sizes on smooth and strongly convex Lipschitz losses over a compact convex domain under Renyi DP. Specialized to strongly convex GLMs, our error bounds match minimax lower bounds we derive based on the Score Attack framework. In particular, this provides the first minimax-optimal rate for Noisy SGD in private logistic regression, avoiding poly-logarithmic terms present in existing results. Our analysis is versatile as it relies on standard convex analysis and establishes the same rates in expectation and with high probability.
Michelle Delcourt; Cicely Henderson; Thomas Lesgourgues; Luke Postle

A seminal result of Hajnal and Szemerédi from 1970 asserts that every graph on $n$ vertices with $q\;|\;n$ and minimum degree at least $\Big(1-\frac{1}{q}\Big)n$ admits a $K_q$-factor (a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ spanning all vertices). There has been sustained interest in extending this result to hypergraph $K_q^r$-factors. For general $q$ and $r$, Lu and Székely in 2007 showed that every large enough, $r$-graph $G$ with $q\mid v(G)$ and $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1- \frac{c}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ admits a $K_q^r$-factor (where $c$ is a constant depending on $r$ but not $q$), and there have been various subsequent improvements to the constant (but not the order) of this bound over the ensuing decades. Meanwhile, results from codegree Turán theory show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1 - \frac{c \cdot \log q}{q^{r-1}} \right)v(G)$ is necessary.
 Surprisingly, our main result shows that the order of this upper bound is not correct and, in fact, the codegree $K_q^r$-factor threshold is much closer to this codegree Turán theory bound. In particular, we show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left( 1-c\cdot \frac{\log^{1-1/(r-1)}q}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ suffices for the existence of a $K_q^r$-factor. Our key contribution is showing the same is true for the fractional threshold. Inspired by the first and fourth author's recent proof of the Nash-Williams' Conjecture, we accomplish this by combining a linear programming framework with ideas from discharging. Additionally, we establish a technical result about finding large independent sets in sparse, non-uniform hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.
Super quantum groups of divided powers à la Lusztig

We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids. Moreover, we prove that our super objects are equipped with a Frobenius-type morphism whose kernel is the Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra of super type, a super analogue of Lusztig's small quantum group, and whose cokernel is the enveloping algebra of the semisimple Lie algebra determined by the Cartan roots of the Nichols algebra. We carry out our construction within the framework of Nichols algebras of diagonal type, specifically, those whose braiding is obtained by specializing at a root of unity. This allows us to consider a divided power integral form inside a large quantum group of De Concini--Kac--Procesi type and then, via specialization, obtain our desired object.
Lyapunov Theory for Output-to-State Stability of Nonlinear Infinite-Dimensional Systems
Qiaoling Chen; Andrii Mironchenko; Fabian Wirth

For a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, we show that output-to-state stability (OSS) is equivalent to the existence of a coercive OSS Lyapunov function in implication form. While establishing this equivalence, we prove that OSS is equivalent to uniform global asymptotic stability modulo output, relate these properties to the vanishing output vanishing state property, and highlight new challenges that do not arise in the nonlinear finite-dimensional or linear infinite-dimensional settings. The results are illustrated by a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system with a nonlinear output map.
Existence and uniqueness for a coagulation-transport equation
Edwin Aguilar Anzures; L. F. López Ríos; Arno Siri-Jégousse

This paper establishes the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear coagulation-transport equations describing the asymptotic dynamics of multispecies coalescent processes. The model captures the multi-scale ancestral lineage decay governed by an autonomous drift field, coupled with a time-inhomogeneous quadratic coagulation term parameterized by the initial population mass. By utilizing the metric structure of probability measures, we demonstrate that any weak solution satisfies a unique mild representation formula dictated by the transport semigroup. This characterization allows us to construct a unified narrative where existence, uniqueness, and moment preservation are proved directly through a contractive fixed-point argument in the space of finite Radon measures.
The Rate of Convergence of Empirical $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein Distances
Pui Kuen Leung; Riku Okada; Samuel Lok-Hei Wong

We study empirical convergence rates for $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distances $D_{p,q}$ for arbitrary real exponents $p>0$ and $q\ge1$. Let $μ$ and $ν$ be probability measures on compact metric spaces $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$, and let $\widehatμ_n$ and $\widehatν_m$ be their empirical measures, constructed from independent i.i.d. samples of sizes $n$ and $m$. If the spaces $\mathcal{X},\,\mathcal{Y}$ are compact subsets of the Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, respectively, we obtain an upper bound of order $(n\wedge m)^{-(p\wedge2)/((d_x\wedge d_y)\vee 2(p\wedge2))}$ on the plug-in error of $D_{p,q}^p(\widehatμ_n,\widehatν_m)$ in expectation, up to a logarithmic factor at the critical dimension $d_x\wedge d_y=2(p\wedge2)$. On Euclidean balls, this rate is sharp up to the logarithmic factor. More generally, we show that the same upper bound holds when one space is a compact subset of a complete, connected $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold and the other has polynomial covering numbers, with $d_x\wedge d_y$ replaced by $d$. Earlier works on $(2,2)$-GW, $(2,1)$-GW and other even-order cases rely on variational representations of GW distances that are specific to their exponents. We instead reduce the plug-in error to an analysis of empirical processes through local duality, which may be of independent interest.
Nondefective lifts of stationary discs and the 2-jet determination problem

We introduce a natural notion of defect for lifts of stationary discs attached to a CR nondegenerate submanifold $M \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ of codimension $d$. We prove that the existence of a nondefective lift of a stationary disc implies that germs of CR automorphisms of $M$ are uniquely determined by their $2$-jet. We emphasize that, in particular, this unifies all previously known results on this question.
Local Clustering Tests and Botnet Localization in Sparse Random Geometric Networks
Luca Di Persio; Gianmarco Bet; Youness Outaleb

We use local clustering to test for botnets in sparse random geometric networks. Under the null hypothesis, the vertices are independent uniform points on a fixed-dimensional torus, with edges determined by a distance threshold. Under the alternative, an unknown set of vertices ignores the geometry and connects independently with the same marginal edge probability. Every prescribed vertex has the same marginal binomial degree law under both hypotheses, so its degree alone carries no information. Triangle closure, however, distinguishes the two models. Under the null, conditional on a degree of at least two, the local clustering coefficient has exact mean $C_d>0$, a known constant that depends only on the dimension. Under the alternative, the corresponding mean is $p_n$ for a bot. For a non-bot, the corresponding mixture mean converges to $C_d$ when the botnet size is $o(n)$. We prove non-asymptotic concentration bounds, an exponential bound on the worst-case risk of a scan test, and exact-support recovery. For every deterministic sequence $1\leq k_n=o(n)$, if $μ_n=(n-1)p_n$ satisfies $μ_n/\log n\to\infty$, the local rule recovers the botnet with probability tending to one, uniformly over all label sets of size $k_n$. The proof combines geometric U-statistics, bounded differences on random neighborhoods, and a stability bound showing that genuine vertices retain their geometric clustering when bots form only a vanishing fraction of their neighbors. The test does not use the latent positions. The theorem assumes that the model parameters are known, although $C_d$ can instead be estimated consistently. In the high-expected-degree regime, the rule also works for a single bot.

We introduce a new class of matrices called conditional Euclidean distance matrices in this paper. These matrices are a generalisation of Euclidean distance matrices. We develop the theory of conditional Euclidean distance matrices and show that these matrices represent the squared Lorentzian distance between points of a Minkowski space. We also highlight the connection of conditional Euclidean distance matrices with the representation of hierarchical data in machine learning and the theory of general relativity in physics.
Spectral asymptotics for vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators
Vincenzo Leone; Marianna Porfido; Abdelaziz Rhandi

We consider vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators $-Δ_{a} +V$ with magnetic potential ${a}\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ and electric potential $V$ given by a symmetric and positive semidefinite $m\times m$ matrix-valued function whose entries belong to $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Assuming that $\|\operatorname{curl} {a}(\cdot)\|\operatorname{Id}_{\mathbb{R}^m} + V$ belongs to a certain matrix reverse Hölder class, we characterize necessary and sufficient conditions under which the spectrum of $-Δ_{a} +V$ is discrete, and study the eigenvalue asymptotics and exponential decay of eigenfunctions.

We survey aspects of nonlinear Fourier series as presented in the 2026 Brouwer lecture by the second author. The fast nonlinear Fourier expansion mentioned in the lecture is further elaborated in joint work with the first author.
A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
Francesco Caporali; Jason M. Altschuler; Boris Hanin

We present a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima in both theory and practice, and establish the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives. Our critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes multiply the classical Polyak rule by $4$ and a mild damping factor. The factor $4$ is critical in that it produces equioscillations around the manifold of minimizers $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order. Damping provably drives convergence to $\mathcal{M}$. CDP thus operates at the edge of stability by adapting its stepsizes to local curvature. Once the loss is small, its projected iterates follow gradient descent on $\log{λ_1(\nabla^2 \mathcal{L})}$ along $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order, paralleling the flatness bias of normalized gradient descent (Arora et al., 2022). Unlike normalized gradient descent, CDP step lengths shrink with the distance to $\mathcal{M}$, enabling convergence to an interpolating solution that locally minimizes sharpness at finite learning rate. We establish our theory for a broad class of non-negative losses with locally quadratic Morse-Bott structure near $\mathcal{M}$, capturing regular interpolation regimes in smooth overparameterized neural networks. Empirically, CDP stepsizes produce a flattening effect similar to that of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM, Foret et al., 2021), reducing sharpness even in settings beyond our theory, including nonlinear teacher-student networks and fine-tuning of pre-trained LLMs.
Matheus C. Bortolan; Piotr Kalita; José Antonio Langa; Rafael O. Moura

We study cycles of heteroclinic connections between equilibria of Lotka--Volterra systems with negative self-interactions. We prove that generalized strict diagonal dominance makes the invasion, connection, and weak graphs acyclic for every intrinsic growth vector. No hyperbolicity assumption is needed, and the associated semiflow is gradient with respect to its equilibria. For the broader class of Volterra--Lyapunov stable matrices, we show that two equilibria are joined by a heteroclinic connection exactly when the species that enter have positive invasion rates at the source and the species that leave have nonpositive invasion rates at the target. We show by examples that the three graphs can differ, that the dominance threshold is sharp, and that generalized dominance is not necessary for acyclicity. We also give a quantitative criterion for cycle exclusion in terms of the symmetric and skew parts of a weighted interaction matrix.
A constructive inverse for the Jordan-von Neuman operator on abelian groups

For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.
Perturbed, suprametric, and interpolative contractions are metric contractions

We show that the fixed point theory of perturbed metric spaces, b-suprametric spaces, and interpolative metric spaces reduces to the metric case. A mapping is a perturbed contraction with constant $λ$ if and only if it is a Banach contraction with constant $λ$ for a metric that dominates the exact metric. Thus the theorem of Jleli and Samet is the Banach contraction principle in a finer metric, and we show that this metric cannot be chosen equivalent to the exact one. We also show that the fixed point theorem claimed for perturbed Kannan mappings is false. A b-suprametric is a logarithmic transform of a b-metric with the same constant, and an interpolative metric is a power of a metric with an explicit exponent, which is optimal for $α= 1/2$. Consequently, contractive conditions of maximum type in these spaces are equivalent to the same conditions in b-metric and metric spaces.
Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices

This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$α$ lattice (FPUT-$α$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion.
 Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation. \
Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics

Data assimilation (DA) in partially observed nonlinear systems requires repeated estimation of both hidden states and their uncertainty. Conventional nonlinear filtering can be computationally expensive and often relies on an explicit dynamical model. In this paper, we develop the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a learned latent space, where the dynamics of the latent states follow a conditional Gaussian structure. This structure allows closed-form DA updates in the latent space, while nonlinear encoder-decoder mappings retain the flexibility needed to represent complex dynamics in physical space. A key feature of Neural CGM is its treatment of uncertainty in DA. The latent posterior mean and covariance are mapped to the physical variables through a Gaussian decoder that combines local moment propagation with learned nonlinear corrections. The resulting physical-space posterior statistics depend on the sequentially updated latent distribution rather than on a separate post-processing estimate. The same statistics enter a Gaussian negative log-likelihood during training, so both the posterior mean and uncertainty affect the learned model. Because Neural CGM learns the dynamical model itself, it can also be used for state forecasting and simulation without explicit knowledge of the governing equations. Numerical experiments on benchmark nonlinear dynamical systems show accurate state estimation and forecasting while substantially reducing online assimilation cost relative to conventional nonlinear DA methods. Neural CGM is therefore suited to repeated state estimation, uncertainty quantification, and prediction from partial observations.
Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras

We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.
Generic arm separation for planar percolation models
Loïc Gassmann; Ioan Manolescu; Maran Mohanarangan

Arm separation is an important technical tool in the study of critical and near-critical planar percolation systems. When combined with RSW estimates, it proves quasi-multiplicativity of arm-event probabilities, links the derivatives of different events and allows the identification of universal arm exponents. We provide a very generic statement of arm separation that applies to arbitrary planar percolation models. Our argument is based on exploring configurations conditioned on the existence of arms in such a way that "exposed" arms are revealed with positive probability. The exploration algorithm is independent of the percolation model and applies to all polychromatic arm events. As an application, we prove a strong arm-separation result for critical planar FK-percolation.
María Agustina Cagliero; Oliver Clarke; Lorenzo De Biase; Angelo El Saliby; Giulia Gaggero; Weijia Wang

Studying parameter-dependent polynomial systems often requires stratifying parameter space according to the algebraic or geometric properties of the specialised systems. Comprehensive Gröbner bases and systems, which provide Gröbner bases valid under every specialisation, either uniformly or on specified regions of parameter space, are classical tools for studying polynomial ideals under specialisation. We introduce ComprehensiveGBs, a Macaulay2 package for computing comprehensive Gröbner bases and systems, either over the full parameter space or under specified parameter conditions. We describe its use and implementation, with examples involving Weierstrass cubics and graphs.
Profile-Anchored Control: Velocity Shaping with Exact Disturbance Rejection and Transient-Free Replanning
Christian Fredrik Sætre; Morten Dinhoff Pedersen

In many motion-control problems, how a target is approached matters as much as whether it is reached: speed and deceleration must stay within actuator, safety or comfort limits despite unknown loads and disturbances. Position-dependent velocity profiles provide a natural way to describe such requirements. We show that the square of such a profile can be used both to plan the motion and to construct the controller that executes it. Our main result, profile-anchored control with exact rejection (PACER), recovers the nominal motion after a finite time under an unknown gain and load, and then allows the profile to be replaced mid-motion without a transient. It combines a static law for scalar second-order systems with a dynamic law for first-order ones, used for disturbance rejection. The static law guarantees uniform global asymptotic stability under an unknown input gain with a known lower bound, and finite-time stability under local homogeneity, while the first-order law gives analogous guarantees under disturbances of bounded rate and provides the exact rejection in PACER. Replanning of a profile under speed, acceleration and jerk limits can be formulated as a convex program. The approach is illustrated on a simulated elevator.
Rigidity of Complete Self-shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension

We prove that a connected complete immersed self-shrinker in Euclidean space whose second fundamental form $h$ satisfies $|h|^2\le1$ is either a linear plane or a complete Riemannian covering of a generalized round cylinder. Neither properness nor polynomial volume growth is assumed. This proves the pinching classification conjectured by Cao and Li %[Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{46} (2013)] in arbitrary codimension. The proof combines a localized maximum principle, a pointwise lower bound for the Bakry--Émery Ricci tensor, a weak Harnack inequality, and the convexity of the shrinker potential at the endpoint.
Degree Lower Bounds for Symmetric Boolean Functions: Breaking the Prime-Gap Barrier

We prove that every nonconstant symmetric Boolean function on $n$ variables has exact real polynomial degree at least $n-O(n^{1/3}(\log n)^{2/3})$. This makes progress toward the conjecture of von zur Gathen and Roche that the degree is always at least $n-3$. The original prime-gap argument of von zur Gathen and Roche yields a degree deficit of $O(n^{0.525})$ using the theorem of Baker, Harman, and Pintz, or $O(n^{0.52})$ using an estimate claimed in a recent preprint. Our $\widetilde{O}(n^{1/3})$ bound on the degree deficit improves upon the $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$ bound obtainable from the prime-gap approach, even assuming the Riemann hypothesis or Legendre's conjecture. Notably, our proof avoids prime-gap estimates entirely.
 The proof combines vanishing binomial moments with the arithmetic of linear recurrences. A quantitative form of the integer Hankel determinant method in the Pólya--Carlson theorem forces the function's values on a central interval of Hamming weights to satisfy a short rational recurrence. A second determinant argument bounds the number of characteristic roots near $-1$. Through the binomial transform, these roots can then be cancelled by a polynomial test of degree below the deficit. An integer annihilator and contour estimates make the test isolate the first failure of the recurrence, yielding a contradiction with the vanishing-moment conditions. If the recurrence agrees with the function on a sufficiently long interval, arithmetic height bounds instead force a bounded period, which is ruled out by a separate polynomial test. Every numbered result in the paper has been formally verified in Lean~4.
Higher cluster-tilting modules for blocks of finite groups

We classify the $d$-representation-finite blocks of finite group algebras over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. The main step is to show that if a block admits a $d$-cluster-tilting module with $d\geq3$, then it splits over the fraction field of the Witt vectors. This excludes generalized quaternion defect groups of order at least $16$.
An operator $b$-positivity conjecture for Jack characters

Goulden and Jackson defined a Jack deformation $a_{μν}^λ(α)$ of the connection coefficients of the symmetric group and conjectured that these were polynomials in $b=α-1$ with nonnegative interger coefficients. This conjecture was extended to the structure constants of (stable) Jack characters by Śniady. We formulate a stronger operator conjecture: the differential operators $Δ_μ(α)$ that multiply by stable Jack characters should have coefficients in ${\mathbb N}[b]$ in the normally ordered Heisenberg basis $p_ID_J$. We provide numerical evidence, as well as theoretical consequences of the conjecture which can be rigorously proved. Namely, we exhibit two families of $α$-shifted symmetric functions whose associated differential operators are ${\mathbb N}[b]$ positive simultaneously on the bases $p_ID_J$ and $Δ_μ(α)$. These operators correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the Jack transition measure and to the Cartan generators of the affine Yangian $Y(\widehat{\mathfrak gl}_1)$.
Tunable Ground-State Entanglement in Fully Connected Quantum Systems: From Logarithmic to Volume-Law Scaling

Entanglement scaling is a central probe of the complexity of quantum many-body ground states, yet once geometric locality is absent, it can depend sensitively on the structure and normalization of interactions. For fully connected Hamiltonians with the natural Kac normalization, nondegenerate gapped ground states are known to obey a logarithmic entanglement bound. Here we ask how the ground-state entanglement changes when this interaction normalization is continuously relaxed away from the Kac scale. We answer this question by constructing an explicit all-to-all bipartite Hamiltonian of $n$ qubits with Fourier pairing amplitudes and pairwise interaction strength proportional to $n^{-κ}$. For sufficiently small fixed coupling, we prove that every pure ground state has entanglement entropy $Θ(n^{2-2κ} \log n)$ for $1/2<κ\leq1$ and $Θ(n)$ at $κ=1/2$. We further show that the ground state is unique and separated from the rest of the spectrum by a system-size-independent gap for $3/4 \leq κ\leq 1$, while weak-coupling analysis and numerical calculations suggest that the gap remains open also for $1/2 \leq κ< 3/4$. Thus, varying only the interaction normalization yields a controlled hierarchy from logarithmic scaling at the natural Kac normalization $κ=1$ to increasingly strong subextensive entanglement and ultimately to a volume law, showing that even an arbitrarily weak relaxation of this normalization precludes a universal logarithmic entanglement bound.
Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic

We show that for every field $K$ of positive characteristic there exists an algebraic matroid $M$ over $K$ such that the dual matroid $M^*$ is not algebraic over any field. Our conceptual proof relies on the theory of matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups. As an application, we deduce that the classes of supports of realizable volume polynomials and of realizable covolume polynomials differ in positive characteristic.
Nondegeneracy and uniqueness of ground states of the Schrödinger equation with Neumann conditions in a weakly nonlocal regime
Serena Dipierro; María Medina; Enrico Valdinoci

We consider the nonlocal Schrödinger equation driven by a fractional Laplacian of order~$2s$, with~$s$ close to~$1$. Differently from the existing literature, which focused on either global problems in the whole of~$\R^n$ or Dirichlet conditions, we study here the case of nonlocal Neumann conditions in the halfspace.
 Moreover, we prove that ground states are nondegenerate, i.e. the only solutions of the linearized equation are linear combinations of the tangential derivatives of the ground state.
 Consequently, the ground state is unique, up to tangential translations and a change of sign.
Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
Yuchen Zhou; Lili Zheng; Yuxin Chen; Gen Li

Flow matching is a versatile framework for generative modeling that transports a source distribution to a target data distribution. A key advantage is its flexibility in the choice of source distribution, such as heavy-tailed and multimodal sources. Yet finite-step sampling guarantees for non-Gaussian sources remain limited. We establish a nonasymptotic convergence theory for Euler discretization of flow matching with linear interpolation. Suppose the source distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ has an everywhere positive, continuously differentiable density, finite total variance $\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}$, and an $L$-Lipschitz score. Using the population velocity field and a suitable time grid, this sampler achieves total variation error at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ iterations, provided the target distribution satisfies a mild second-moment condition. These assumptions cover, among many examples, source distributions such as multivariate Student's $t$ distributions with more than two degrees of freedom and finite Gaussian mixtures with shared covariance, while accommodating target distributions with neither a smooth density nor bounded support.
Semi-global Convergence and Finite-Sample Error Bounds for Model Predictive Path Integral Control

We investigate the global optimisation behaviour of Model Predictive Path Integral Control (MPPI) in the low-temperature setting. For objective functions with a unique global minimum and under weak additional assumptions, allowing non-convexity and non-smoothness, we establish semi-global convergence of the mean-field or population level MPPI iteration to this global optimum. We also establish finite-sample results that show that with high probability the MPPI iteration comes close to the global optimum and provide sample complexity results. Under slightly stronger assumptions, we make these results more quantitative and provide concrete bounds on the inverse temperature and number of samples. Finally, we illustrate the results on the classic LQR problem.
First Neumann eigenfunctions on piecewise smooth Jordan domains with convex corners
Santiago Pineda Montoya; Edisson Gallego González; Jaiberth Porras Barrera; Johan H. Rúa Muñoz

We prove that every nonzero eigenfunction of the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded planar Jordan domain whose boundary consists of finitely many smooth arcs meeting at interior angles strictly between $0$ and $π$ has nonvanishing gradient in the interior; hence its extrema are attained only on the boundary. The eigenvalue may be multiple and the domain need not be convex; every convex polygon is included. The method adapts a recent Green-kernel approach for smooth domains.
Harish-Chandra isomorphism over arbitrary base rings

Let $G$ be a split connected reductive group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}$, and let $R$ be any commutative ring. We prove that Harish-Chandra projection induces a natural, strict filtered isomorphism $U_R(\mathfrak{g}_R)^{G_R} \simeq \operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathfrak{h}_R)^{W,\bullet}$, whereas the corresponding Chevalley restriction need not be surjective even over a field.
Curvature Integrability in Twinor Theory: An Ambitwistor Approach to the Twinor Googly Problem

The twinor analogue of the googly problem is addressed through an ambitwistor structure defined by null autoparallels, retaining both chiralities, sources and torsion without requiring chiral null surfaces. Under the stated quotient, evaluation and descent assumptions, holomorphic affine sections reconstruct the twinor field equation $DY=J$. Correspondence-space cohomology realizes the contracted chiral and ladder equations, including the ladder's soldering coupling and mass-normalization source. For a prescribed non-normal conformal connection, infinity-twistor parallelism recovers the energy--momentum equation, supplemented by independent spin-current equations. These constructions give a conditional auxiliary formulation; constitutive sources and gravitational prescriptions remain dynamical input.
Hook histories and a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual canonical Grothendieck functions

We establish a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for power-sum multiplication in the dual canonical stable Grothendieck basis. The coefficients admit a closed boundary product formula and a signed combinatorial description by hook histories. We determine their exact support and prove an exact divisibility law for off-diagonal coefficients governed by the edge-connected components of the indexing skew diagram. We also obtain a hook expansion of power sums, an explicit binomial reduction to the dual stable rule, and a Grassmannian $K$-homological interpretation of the one-parameter specialization. Finally, we deduce complementary rules for power-sum multiplication in the canonical basis and the corresponding lowering operation in the dual canonical basis.
Stefano Tinelli; Francisco Lázaro; Francisco García Herrero

A key challenge in fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) is that the syndrome extraction circuits are themselves faulty. Such circuit-level noise is commonly described by a detector error model (DEM). In Stim and in almost all related works, DEMs are binary: every non-binary circuit error (e.g., CNOT gate), is decomposed into independent binary error mechanisms. In this work, we introduce non-binary DEMs, in which each fault location of the syndrome extraction circuit is modeled by one random variable over its original alphabet, e.g., the 16 two-qubit Pauli errors after a CNOT gate. We also propose a split-merge-regroup transformation that builds a compact non-binary DEM from any Clifford circuit by merging the error components that flip the same detectors and observables. Non-binary DEMs represent any Pauli channel exactly, whereas binary DEMs are exact only for channels that factorize into independent binary parts. When the channels factorize, we prove that binary and non-binary DEMs are equivalent under degenerate quantum maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) decoding, but not under quantum MAP decoding. Although the variables are non-binary, belief propagation (BP) still exchanges a single scalar message per edge. Our numerical results with surface, color and bivariate bicycle codes show that non-binary DEMs have two main advantages. First, their Tanner graphs have four to five times fewer edges, which is advantageous for hardware implementations. Second, their performance under BP, with and without OSD post-processing, is better than that of their binary counterparts, and BP with OSD runs up to $9.4\times$ faster in a CPU.
Twinor Theory in the Newton--Hooke Limit: A Nonrelativistic Schrödinger Equation for Arbitrary Spin

The Newton--Hooke limit of the massive twinor field equations is derived at fixed particle mass and fixed cosmological acceleration per unit displacement. On a static torsion-free background, removal of the rest energy separates the leading spin amplitude from a finite sequence of auxiliary spinors. For every positive integer rank $2s$, a regular limit of exact solutions satisfies a first-order hierarchy. Its lowest two equations give a necessary Schrödinger equation for the leading amplitude, with a curvature term from the ordered spatial derivatives and a source determined by two projections of the relativistic source. The higher equations impose additional conditions. On the homogeneous Newton--Hooke background with trivial internal connection and nonzero cosmological acceleration parameter, vanishing of all limiting contracted sources forces the leading amplitude to vanish for $s\geq\tfrac32$. A separate reduction of the scalar wave equation gives the spin-zero case.
Optimal Preemption: Guaranteeing Information Freshness in Mean Age and Beyond
Aimin Li; Yiğit İnce; Elif Uysal

Once a status update enters service, age-optimal policies must wait for it, even when heavy-tailed delays inflate the Age of Information (AoI). We develop a framework in which the sender may preempt the update in service and sample a fresh one, under general service-time distributions and explicit action costs. Our framework covers sources that generate updates at will as well as random update arrivals. Under nondecreasing age costs, we prove that, with preemption, a finite mean delay suffices for a finite average age even under infinite delay variance. We show the optimality of constant service-age thresholds from prior work for exponential service, and exhibit numerically that for general delays the optimal preemption rule depends on both the AoI and the elapsed service time. Under an action-cost budget, we further minimize the Value at Risk (VaR), which bounds the AoI except for a prescribed fraction of time, and the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR), the mean AoI over that fraction. We reduce both to the same optimality equations without enlarging the state space. Under Pareto and log-normal delays, our algorithm TAILOR keeps the average cost bounded as delay variance grows, while optimal non-preemptive sampling diverges. With optimal preemption, a more variable network can allow fresher data than a steadier one of equal mean delay.
Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections

Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions.
 In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.
Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes

We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows:
 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar interactions exists at all orders, represented by a finite number of effective even forms. 3. The higher-derivative contact-term sector can be constructed from a finite set of basic tensor structures using polynomials in derivative symbols.
 We introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity considerations.
Elliptic analogues of KP and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions

We develop a tau-function framework for soliton solutions on elliptic backgrounds associated with the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (KP) hierarchy and its B-type counterpart (BKP). Starting from discrete KP (dKP) and discrete BKP (dBKP) equations of elliptic type, we construct Casorati and Gram determinant tau functions for the elliptic dKP through Darboux and binary Darboux transformations, and elliptic Pfaffian tau functions for dBKP through the Moutard transformation. Moreover, the higher-order discrete KP and BKP hierarchies together with their tau functions are constructed via Pfaffian identities. Then, through Miwa transformations, the continuous elliptic KP, modified KP, and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions are provided. Suitable constraints on spectral parameters or wave numbers yield reductions to the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV), focusing and defocusing modified Korteweg--de Vries (mKdV), and Sawada--Kotera (SK) equations, together with their solutions on elliptic backgrounds. We also construct KP line-soliton solutions and obtain lump solutions for the KP-I equation. For selected determinant families, we establish sufficient conditions for real-valuedness and global nonsingularity. The resulting framework provides a common approach to elliptic tau functions, their discrete and continuous bilinear identities, and the construction of solutions through reductions.
When Suspicion Adds Up: A Stochastic Framework for Optimizing Honeypot-Based Insider-Threat Detection
Saharnaz Mehrani; Lujia Zhan; Mohsen Emadikhiav; Payman Dehghanian

Insider threats pose security risks when employees or other trusted users misuse their access to organizational systems. Detecting these threats is difficult because harmful activity can resemble routine behavior. Honeypots, or decoy resources monitored for suspicious interactions, can provide evidence of potentially malicious activity. We develop a decision framework that models evidence accumulation through honeypot interactions using a continuous-time Markov chain and jointly selects honeypot counts and monitoring horizons to minimize expected losses from malicious activity and false detections. For thresholds of two and three interactions, we derive closed-form true- and false-detection probabilities and expected detection times conditional on detection within the monitoring horizon. We characterize boundary cases and establish stochastic-ordering results. Our numerical results highlight the value of the proposed framework across different settings.
Yun Li; Yahui Qu; Benedek Valkó; Bálint Virág

We prove that the pair correlation function of $\operatorname{Sine}_β$ extends holomorphically in $β$ to $\Reβ>0$ at every fixed nonzero separation. Our proof combines a random walk representation of the stochastic sine phase moments, stretched-exponential Fourier decay obtained by coupling, and weighted energy estimates for complex $β$.
How Should Candidates Be Weighted under Open-List Proportional Representation? Harmonic Weights and Dirichlet Order Statistics

Candidates in open-list proportional representation systems are not equally prominent, and measurements that involve aggregation over candidates therefore require some form of weighting. We address the question of how those weights should be chosen. Since weights based on realized preference votes are unavailable in advance and endogenous to the electoral outcome, we seek a priori weights that depend on list position alone, and derive them as expected ordered vote shares under a probabilistic model of the division of the list vote among candidates. The natural starting point -- the uniform distribution on the simplex -- is unrealistic, as it prescribes the same degree of concentration of the vote for every list, and under it the leading candidates become more alike as lists lengthen. The other members of the symmetric Dirichlet family require a concentration parameter, which is unknown and which there is no reason to expect to be constant across countries, parties, and elections. Accordingly, we treat that parameter as random. We prove that under a scale-invariant prior restricted to lists with at least two effective candidates, the expected share of the $k$-th candidate decays as $1/k$, and we show that over the leading positions of a long list, up to one hundred of them, the resulting weights are within 1.4 to 3.4 percent, in total variation, of the harmonic weights $(k H_n)^{-1}$, where $H_n$ is the $n$-th harmonic number. No fixed value of the parameter yields similar weights. Moreover, under the uniform distribution itself, harmonic weights are exactly the normalized expected margins between consecutive candidates.
Polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces and the polyanalytic $q$-Bargmann transform
Irfan Ali; Uwe Kähler; Michael Ruzhansky

We study polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces from an operator-theoretic point of view. We compute the formal adjoint $A^*$ of the Jackson derivative $A=\overline{R}_{q}$ on the polynomials in $z,\overline{z}$ inside $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ and we show that, up to unimodular factors, a twist by the grading operator is the only modification of $A$ diagonal in the grading for which a deformed canonical relation $aa^*-λa^*a=I$ holds. The resulting second-order $q$-difference operator $a^*a$ is essentially self-adjoint on the polynomials and $q$-complex Hermite polynomials span its eigenspaces. These eigenspaces give the orthogonal decomposition of $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ into true polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces. We determine the disk on which each of them is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and we factor the corresponding unitary $q$-Bargmann transforms through powers of $a^*$.
Equality in the clique bound for critical graphs

A graph is $k$-critical if its chromatic number is $k$ and every proper subgraph is $(k-1)$-colorable. Gao and Ma (2023) proved that every $n$-vertex $k$-critical graph with $n > k \ge 4$ contains at most $n - k + 3$ cliques of size $k - 1$, and asked which graphs attain this bound. We answer this question by showing that equality holds if and only if $n - k + 3$ is odd and the graph is isomorphic to the join of a complete graph on $k - 3$ vertices and a cycle of length $n - k + 3$. More generally, for $n>k\ge3$, we determine when the size of a nonempty family of distinct $(k-1)$-cliques in an $n$-vertex $k$-critical graph attains the upper bound $s-k+3$, where $s$ is the number of vertices covered by the family. Equality holds if and only if the graph is such a join (with the complete part empty when $k = 3$) and the family consists of all its $(k-1)$-cliques.
The distortion of finitely generated subgroups in hyperbolic groups

We show that the range of distortion functions of finitely generated subgroups of hyperbolic groups is essentially as broad as the range of time-complexity functions $T(n)$ of Turing machines. More precisely, we show that for each such $T(n) \geq n$ for which $T(n)^3$ is superadditive, there is a hyperbolic group $G$ with a finitely generated normal subgroup $N$ such that $\text{Dist}_N^G(n) \simeq 2^{T(n)^3}$. Our approach is to estimate the distortion of the kernels in Wise's HNN version of the Rips construction, and then to look at what these estimates yield when the $S$-machine groups of Sapir, Birget, and Rips are the inputs to the construction.
Signed QoI Gaps for Goal-Oriented Error Estimation: Reliability and Sharpness from the Same First-Order System Residuals

There are two common ways to estimate the error in a quantity of interest (QoI). The product of primal and adjoint error estimators gives a reliable but pessimistic bound. The dual-weighted residual method gives a sharp signed estimate from a more accurate approximation of the adjoint solution. We write the primal and adjoint problems as first-order systems and obtain both a reliable bound and a sharp estimate from the same residuals. The first paper of this series (arXiv:2607.23850) uses two consistent evaluators of a quantity of interest, one built from the potentials and one in which the gradients are expressed through the fluxes. We show that they differ exactly by the $A^{-1}$ inner product of the primal and adjoint constitutive residuals, and we call this difference the signed QoI gap. The identity holds for arbitrary primal and adjoint approximations. In our numerical experiments, the signed QoI gap is of the size of the larger of the errors of the two evaluators, while the product of the estimators exceeds this error by factors of up to several hundred. We therefore use the least-squares estimators to refine the mesh and the signed QoI gap to decide when to stop. We also introduce a third evaluator, built from the fluxes alone, which restores the reaction term. The resulting reaction-restored QoI gap estimates the error when reaction dominates. With the non-intrusive least-squares flux recovery, we can apply the method to any discretization that produces a conforming potential, including finite difference and finite volume schemes.
The envelope property for unibranch projective varieties (with an appendix on the singular Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture)
Yanbo Fang; Jiyuan Han; Mingchen Xia

We prove the envelope property for every real numerical class on an integral unibranch projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field based on the recent work of Lyuhui Wu. Together with Boucksom-Jonsson's converse, this characterizes unibranchness by the plurisubharmonic envelope property. The Appendix applies the result to the uniform Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture for projective varieties with klt singularities.
A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus
Mario Krenn; Moritz Firsching; George Tsoukalas; Rishikesh Gajjala; Xuemei Gu; Swarat Chaudhuri

Photonic GHZ states generated with probabilistic pair sources can be described by edge-coloured, complex-weighted graphs. In this representation, conditioning on an event with one photon in every detector turns the output amplitudes into coherent sums over perfect matchings, and generating an \(N\)-photon \(D\)-dimensional GHZ state is equivalent to constructing a monochromatic quantum graph. Here, we prove that no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for any even \(N\ge4\) when \(D\ge N\). The proof, discovered through AI-assisted formal proof search in Lean using AlphaProof Nexus, constructs a weighted sum \(\mathcal F\) of amplitudes whose coefficients factor vertex by vertex. Summing over the colours at one fixed vertex reduces the problem to an \((N-1)\times N\) matrix of effective edge weights. For the graph amplitudes \(ω\) and GHZ target \(Δ\), the row--column imbalance yields \(\mathcal F(ω)=0\) but \(\mathcal F(Δ)\neq0\), contradicting the required equality \(ω=Δ\). Finally, we give a physical interpretation of the AI-discovered mathematical proof.
Hamiltonian Potential Optimization for Partially Observed Stochastic Optimal Control
Christian Bayer; Saifeddine Ben Naamia; Erik von Schwerin; Raul Tempone

We develop a Hamiltonian potential optimization method for partially observed stochastic optimal control with continuous-time state dynamics and discrete-time noisy observations, including controlled sensing. Rather than solving the infinite-dimensional belief-space Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, we optimize over parametrized potentials depending on the state variable and the available observation history. The associated Hamiltonian minimizers induce admissible continuous controls and, when observations are controlled, sensing decisions. An extended Hamiltonian incorporating a cost multiplier provides a common representation of the induced belief dynamics and running and observation costs. This construction yields a finite-dimensional optimization problem, with gradients computed by a forward simulation and a backward discrete adjoint sweep. The numerical implementation uses Gaussian beliefs represented by conditional means and covariances. For nonsmooth Hamiltonians arising from switching controls, we introduce smooth Hamiltonian approximations to enable gradient-based optimization. To assess the resulting policies, we develop belief-space information relaxation lower bounds. A separate optimization of the dual test functional provides a lower bound which, paired with the admissible policy cost, yields an a posteriori primal-dual diagnostic. Numerical experiments investigate scalar and multidimensional linear-quadratic-Gaussian problems, controlled sensing with and without control bounds, a nonquadratic obstacle penalty, and Hamiltonian smoothing for a discontinuous control selector.
Closed $G_2$-structures with fixed metric: compactness and almost-abelian fibres

We study the space of closed $G_2$-structures inducing a prescribed Riemannian metric and orientation. On a compact seven-manifold, with a fixed Riemannian metric and orientation, we prove that the space of compatible closed $G_2$ structures inducing a prescribed spin-structure is homeomorphic to a real projective algebraic set defined by homogeneous quadratic equations in the kernel of the corresponding Dirac operator. The defining quadrics give a local analytic obstruction map and a Łojasiewicz estimate that bounds the distance to the closed locus in terms of $\|d\varphi\|_{L^2}$. We also prove smooth compactness when the prescribed metrics converge smoothly, and strong $H^1$ compactness for sequences of compatible $G_2$-structures $\varphi_{j}$ satisfying $\|d\varphi_j\|_{L^2}\to 0$. In the invariant setting, the fixed-metric fibre of any seven-dimensional almost-abelian metric Lie algebra has at most four connected components, each a compact homogeneous space. We determine these spaces spectrally when the defining endomorphism is normal, and show that for a non-normal endomorphism the fibre is empty, one circle, or two circles.
