Fulong Ye; Bofeng Huo; Yuxiang Liu; Ligong Wang

A graph $G$ is $F$-free if it does not contain $F$ as a subgraph. Let $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ denote the set of $n$-vertex $F$-free outerplanar graphs with maximum spectral radius. Define $S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t)$ as the starlike tree obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint paths of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one endpoint of each path, and $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$ as the graph obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one vertex from each cycle. When $l_1=l_2=\cdots=l_t=l$, we abbreviate these graphs as $S(t\cdot l)$ and $C_{t\cdot l}$, respectively. Previous results determined $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(t\cdot l))$ for $t\ge4$ [Graphs Combin. 42 (2026) 80] and for $t=3$, in each case for sufficiently large $n$. For $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$, the corresponding extremal graphs are known for $t=2$ and sufficiently large $n$. The sets $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{t\cdot l})$ were also determined for sufficiently large $n$ [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114673]. In this paper, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t))$ for sufficiently large $n$ when the branch lengths are not all equal. Our result for $t\ge4$ also includes equal branch lengths. As applications, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t})$ for arbitrary cycle lengths and sufficiently large $n$. We also determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ for certain linear forests $F=\bigcup_{i=1}^tP_{l_i}$ and sufficiently large $n$. Finally, we apply our main theorems to obtain the known results on outerplanar graphs forbidding matchings or theta graphs for sufficiently large $n$.
A sharp bounded bijection for tight cylindric partitions

Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. The inverse preserves the profile and entry bound. We identify every partition missed at the next deficit. A prefix test decides whether any cylinder lies outside this sector and, if so, identifies the unique one of least deficit. This explains the leading coefficient gap in Warnaar's $Q_{n,c}$. We also determine the first correction to the vertex terms of the published bounded determinant.
On quasi-triangular Hopf algebras of square-free dimensions
Jiacheng Bao; Zhiqiang Yu; Ying Zheng

Let $H$ be a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra of sqaure-free dimension over $\mathbb{C}$. In this note, we show that $H$ is semisimple and cocommutative. Equivalently, a braided finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ of square-free Frobenius--Perron dimension with a fiber functor is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.

Given a symmetric matrix $A \in [-1,1]^{n \times n}$, we estimate the probability that a random principal submatrix, obtained by taking each index independently with probability $p$, is positive semidefinite. As a corollary, we show that $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ indices chosen uniformly at random suffice for testing positive semidefiniteness with squared Frobenius distance threshold $\varepsilon n^2$, thus nearly matching the lower bound of Bakshi, Chepurko, and Jayaram (``Testing Positive Semi-Definiteness via Random Submatrices'', FOCS 2020). The key ingredient is a dense model lemma for positive semidefinite matrices, proved using the hyperplane separation theorem and a contraction inequality for Rademacher random variables.
Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
Michael Goldman; Lukas Koch; Dario Trevisan

We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calderón--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a deterministic large-scale regularity theory for optimal transport with $p$-costs, based on a harmonic approximation by a non-linear elliptic equation of $p$-Laplacian type, with tail bounds on local matching costs.
Intent-Defined Radio: A Goal-Native Architecture for Next-Generation Wireless Networks
Wencheng Yan; Binrui Xu; Yihao Shen; Zhiyuan Jiang; Sheng Zhou

Wireless systems are becoming harder to operate because service goals are increasingly expressed in outcome-oriented terms, while radio platforms still expose mainly low-level configurations and protocol-specific controls. This mismatch makes it difficult to translate latency, reliability, throughput, and continuity requirements into coherent radio behavior. This article argues for Intent-Defined Radio (IDR) as a new system abstraction for next-generation wireless networks. Rather than treating the radio stack as a fixed mechanism set to be manually engineered and then tuned, IDR connects explicit service goals to executable radio behavior within a constrained design space by leveraging the capacity of large language models (LLMs). We position IDR relative to programmable radio, intent-based networking, and learning-based protocol design. We also present two simulation studies using Intent2MAC to illustrate the design loop, demonstrating executable MAC synthesis and offline refinement guided by evaluation feedback. The results show improved service satisfaction at a throughput cost and improved remote-control performance when random contention is replaced by distributed urgency-based arbitration. We finally discuss the open challenges in intent specification, evidence, hardware execution, interoperability, and lifecycle cost, and outline a staged path toward deployment.
Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons

We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of Dimakis--Fredrickson--Yae to the boundary and allowing compactly supported changes of marking, we obtain every point of the normalized period domain. It follows from the ALG Torelli theorem that every ALG gravitational instanton with cone parameter $1/3$, $1/4$ or $1/6$ is isometric, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, to one of these moduli spaces with its Hitchin metric.
Sharp box-dimension bounds for fractional integrals under unequal Hölder and anti-Hölder exponents

Let $0<h\le H<1$ and $0<σ<1$. Graph box dimensions are studied for fractional integrals of functions satisfying an $h$-Holder upper bound on increments and an $H$-anti-H lder lower bound on oscillation on a nondegenerate subinterval. For the Riemann--Liouville integral, the following inequalities hold: \[ \begin{aligned} \max\{1,2-H-σH/h\} &\le\lbdim\G(I_{0+}^σf,[0,1])\\ &\le\ubdim\G(I_{0+}^σf,[0,1]) \le\max\{1,2-h-σ\}. \end{aligned} \] The lower bound is obtained by balancing the truncation error of a Marchaud inverse against the oscillation of the input. For each $(h,H)$, a single sparse tent construction attains it for all $σ\in(0,1)$. The same bounds and their optimality are established for Hadamard integrals on compact intervals bounded away from zero and for left- and right-sided Liouville--Weyl integrals under explicit weighted tail conditions. Zero-mean periodic Weyl integrals with conditionally convergent tails are treated separately. For Hadamard integrals the bounds are transferred by a bi-Lipschitz logarithmic change of variables. For Weyl integrals the transfer relies on invariance of graph box dimensions under continuous perturbations of bounded variation. Local hypotheses and point-dependent anti-Hölder constants are also treated. The exact linear dimension law is recovered for equal exponents, whereas unequal exponents allow a strictly greater loss of graph dimension.
Nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with singular viscosity
Guanghan Zhao; Jingyu Li; Xiaowen Li; Changchun Liu; Ming Mei

We study the nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional isentropic Navier--Stokes system with fast diffusion and singular viscosity. The waves connect a positive left state to zero specific volume at the right far field, where the density becomes unbounded and the viscous coefficient is singular. Under a vanishing--stress condition, we first establish the existence and uniqueness, up to a shift, of a monotone profile with an algebraic right tail. We then prove global existence and convergence to the profile for sufficiently small perturbations in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main difficulties stem from the singular nonlinear viscous term. We note that the existing approach for treating scalar conservation law with singular viscosity can not be applied to Navier--Stokes equations. We propose some new technique: after introducing an effective velocity and using an anti--derivative method, we establish unusual interactive--energy--estimates and thereby the expected energy estimates for velocity by coupling the two perturbation equations; furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary functional to eliminate uncontrollable terms. The artful weighted--energy estimates play a crucial role for treating singularity.
Herz-type Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces with general weights

In this paper, we introduce a new family of function spaces of generalized smoothness that encompasses the classical Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces, their weighted counterparts, as well as Herz-type Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We provide a characterization of these spaces via the $\varphi$-transform in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth, and establish the corresponding Sobolev embeddings. Furthermore, we obtain smooth atomic and molecular decompositions for these spaces. Our approach relies on several new maximal inequalities.
Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7

Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers.
 Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Diţă's family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.
Linear dependence and tameness for homogeneous nilpotent-Jacobian maps in dimension four

Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $H\in K[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]^4$ be homogeneous of positive degree. We prove that the components of $H$ are linearly dependent over $K$ whenever $JH$ is nilpotent, extending the known quadratic and cubic results to every positive homogeneous degree. This fills the gap regarding homogeneous linear dependence in four dimensions. The proof combines the nilpotent flag with the geometry of the geometric generic affine fibers and the projective image surface. Line fibers are treated by homogeneous quasi-translations. For nonlinear fibers, three successive invariants constrain the directions at infinity, reducing the nonplanar image to a developable surface or a smooth quadric. Boundary, ruling, and trace identities exclude both alternatives. We further prove that $X+H$ is one-stably tame in every degree and tame in four variables through degree five.
Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons

We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperkähler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.
Collineations of the diamond lattice in a Hilbert space

Let $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ be non-trivial closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$ such that $\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}=\{0\}$ and $\mathscr{M}+\mathscr{N}$ is dense in $\mathscr{H}$. We characterize when there exists an invertible operator on $\mathscr{H}$ which maps $\mathscr{M}$ onto $\mathscr{N}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ onto $\mathscr{M}$. We prove that such an operator exists if and only if $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ have a common algebraic complement. This happens if and only if either neither of the operators $(I-P)Q$ and $(I-Q)P$ is compact, or $P-Q$ is compact and $\dim(\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}^\perp)=\dim(\mathscr{M}^\perp\cap\mathscr{N})$, where $P$ and $Q$ are the orthogonal projections onto $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$. Moreover, the operator can be chosen to be an involution. Consequently, the group of collineations of the diamond lattice $\{\{0\},\mathscr{M},\mathscr{N},\mathscr{H}\}$ which fix $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ is always complemented in the group of all its collineations.
Subfactor symmetries of real Hadamard matrices

Every Hadamard matrix gives rise to a {\it spin model commuting square} and a hyperfinite subfactor with finite Jones index. The standard invariant of this subfactor is comprised of quantum symmetries of the subfactor which can be viewed as ``non-invertible'' symmetries of the Hadamard matrix. We show that if the Hadamard matrix is real and has order greater than four and congruent to four modulo eight, the standard invariant is minimal, i.e. it consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Consequently, both principal graphs of the subfactor are $A_\infty$. In particular, this holds for every Paley type II Hadamard matrix. The proof uses a congruence for products of four rows and Jones's annular decomposition. More generally, we show that if an irreducible subfactor of finite index greater than four has bounded annular multiplicities along an infinite subsequence of degrees, then its principal graph is $A_\infty$.
Finitely supported mapping classes on infinite-type surfaces

We study the topological closure of the group of mapping classes group with finite-type support on an infinite-type surface. Since every such mapping class fixes each end which is not a puncture, we have that the closure is contained in the pointwise stabilizer of infinite-type ends. A natural question is therefore when this inclusion is an equality, and if it is not, what must be added to obtain the full stabilizer. We prove that finitely supported mapping classes are dense in the stabilizer precisely when there is at most one end accumulated by genus and at most one end accumulated by punctures. We show that if we remove either of these conditions, we need to add puncture and/or handle shifts to topologically generate the stabilizer.
Uniqueness and non-uniqueness of smooth solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}$
Zipeng Chen; Song Liu; Zhaoyang Yin

We study the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb T^d$ with $d\ge2$. For every $2<q\le\infty$ and every smooth mean-zero background solution $U$, we construct two distinct mild solutions with the same initial datum arbitrarily close to $U(0)$ in $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$, both belonging to $C([0,T];\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)) \cap C^\infty((0,T]\times\mathbb T^d)$. The time $T>0$ depends on the background solution but is independent of the prescribed tolerance for the initial data. This gives non-uniqueness for arbitrarily small initial data and density of non-unique initial data in the mean-zero divergence-free subspace of $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $2<q<\infty$. We also prove uniqueness in the same solution class for $1\le q\le2$, establishing the sharp threshold $q=2$ in this Besov scale. The uniqueness result extends to $\dot B^{-1+d/p}_{p,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $1\le p<\infty$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, under the same continuity and smoothness assumptions.
Operator generated topologies and the Krein property

Let $X$ be a Banach space and $Z\subseteq X^*$ a subspace separating the points of $X$. We say that $Z$ has the Krein property if the $σ(X,Z)$-closed convex hull of every norm-bounded $σ(X,Z)$-compact set is $σ(X,Z)$-compact. We show that this property passes from $Z$ to every subspace between $Z$ and its sequential weak$^*$ closure in $X^*$, and that the closed convex hulls do not change. In particular, it passes to the smallest $V^*$-invariant space $Z[V]\supseteq Z$ whenever the operator $V$ is a pointwise $σ(X,Z)$-limit of a sequence of $σ(X,Z)$-continuous operators; for nets this fails in general and holds under a double limit condition. As a source of spaces with the Krein property we show that the Mackey topologies $μ(X,Z)$ and $μ(Z,X)$ are complete if the identity of $X$ is suitably approximated by a sequence of operators whose adjoints map $X^*$ into $Z$; in particular, $μ(E^\odot,E)$ and $μ(E,E^\odot)$ are complete for every $C_0$-semigroup on a Banach space $E$ with sun dual $E^\odot$. The results are applied to the history space $\mathrm{BUC}(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ of delay equations with infinite delay, where every space of bounded measures containing $L^1(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ has the Krein property.
Criteria for memory-induced blow-up in distributed delay differential equations

This paper investigates the conditions under which solutions to distributed delay differential equations describing memory accumulation and forgetting blow up in finite time. It provides criteria for memory-induced blow-up, which means finite-time blow-up of the delayed equation while the corresponding non-delayed equation, obtained in a certain limit, has global solutions. In the author's previous work, memory-induced blow-up was shown for specific nonlinearities by means of Poincaré-type compactification, but a general theory was not established. Here, the two-dimensional ODE system derived by the linear chain trick is rewritten as an orbit equation, and a comparison theorem and an Osgood-type integral condition are applied to obtain a blow-up criterion based on the existence of a subsolution. This characterizes the nonlinearities for which memory-induced blow-up occurs. This paper also gives a necessary condition in a special case, a global existence condition based on a supersolution, and a systematic method for constructing subsolutions for separable nonlinearities. These results recover the author's previous results and are illustrated through several examples.
Unbounded Gaps Between Matrix Monotonicity and Frobenius Radial Convexity

We show that the gap between matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity can be arbitrarily large. For every integer $m\ge 2$, we construct rational functions that are matrix monotone of order $m$ but not of order $m+1$, and Frobenius radially convex of order $2m-1$ but not of order $2m$. Thus, the difference between their exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders is $m-1$, which can be arbitrarily large. As a consequence, for every $n\ge 3$, Frobenius radial convexity of order $n$ does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order, either increasing or decreasing.
Markov processes with jump kernels blowing up at the boundary of $C^{1, η}$ open sets
Soobin Cho; Panki Kim; Renming Song; Zoran Vondraček

We study the boundary behavior of nonnegative harmonic functions for a class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes in $C^{1,η}$ open sets $D\subset\mathbb R^d$. The jump kernels are allowed to blow up at the boundary of $D$ and the processes may have a critical killing potential. We identify the exact boundary decay exponent $p$, characterized by the coefficient of the critical killing potential. We establish a boundary Harnack principle which yields the comparability of $f(x)/δ_D(x)^p$ for nonnegative harmonic functions that vanish continuously on a portion of the boundary. The key ingredient of the proof combines estimates of the exact decay rate for the survival probability of the killed process with a modified box method and uses a regularized distance function to handle the limited boundary regularity.
k-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most one
Zihao Geng; Ji-Ming Guo; Jongyook Park

The problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most $1$ was posed by Hoffman and first studied by Cvetković in 1982. In this paper, all $k$-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most $1$ are characterized. We determine all equality cases and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $1$. For each fixed $k\geq2$, we also determine the $k$-trees attaining the largest second largest eigenvalue below $1$ and the smallest above $1$. Finally, we determine all minimal forbidden induced subgraphs among $k$-trees with $k\geq 1$, each of which has second largest eigenvalue greater than $1$, but deleting any vertex gives a graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$.
Depth of Powers of Cover Ideals of Path Ideals
Nguyen Thu Hang; Truong Thi Hien; Thanh Vu

Let $ J_t(P_n) = (x_1, \ldots, x_t) \cap \cdots \cap (x_{n-t+1}, \ldots, x_n) $ be the cover ideal of the $t$-path ideal of a path graph inside the polynomial ring $ S = K[x_1, \ldots, x_n] $ over a field $K$. For every $ n \ge t \ge 2 $ and $s \ge 2$, we prove that \[ \operatorname{depth} \left ( S/J_t(P_n)^s \right ) = q(s+1) + \left\lfloor \frac{r-1}{t} \right\rfloor, \] where $ n = q(ts + 1) + r $ with $ 1 \le r \le ts + 1 $. Our proof shows that all powers of $J_t(P_n)$ have linear quotients in increasing lexicographic order and explicitly describes the corresponding colon ideals.
Adaptive Tests of Pricing Restrictions with Observed and Latent Factors
Anlin Liu; Guowei Yan; Zhaojun Wang

This paper develops a high-dimensional test for asset pricing models with observed and latent factors. The null hypothesis allows the intercepts from an observed-factor regression to be nonzero, provided that they lie in the latent factor loading space. We estimate the pricing errors in three steps: regress returns on the observed factors, extract latent factors from the lagged covariance structure of the regression residuals, and regress returns on both observed and estimated latent factors. The intercept from the final regression serves as the estimated pricing error. We construct Sum and Max tests based on the estimated pricing errors to detect diffuse and concentrated alternatives, respectively, and combine them using a Cauchy procedure. Under suitable regularity conditions, we establish the joint null distribution of the component statistics, their asymptotic independence, and their power against alternative hypotheses. We also propose a residual bootstrap and establish its first-order validity. Simulation studies examine the finite-sample performance of the tests under different pricing-error patterns and factor-number choices. An application to S\&P 500 stocks illustrates the use of the proposed framework in evaluating an observed-factor pricing model after latent-factor adjustment.
A new second-moment method for spectral measures of inhomogeneous non-Hermitian random matrices

We develop a second-moment method for the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of non-Hermitian random matrices $X_N=(\sqrt{s_{ij}}ξ_{ij})$ with a deterministic variance profile $S_N=(s_{ij})$. When the entries are independent and centered, the second moment of $\det(zI-X_N)$ is the permanent $\mathrm{per}(S_N+|z|^2I)$ of a diagonal shift of $S_N$, and the method approximates $\log|\det(zI-X_N)|$ by half its logarithm. This condition holds for every law with a bounded density on $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. We also allow the two entries $X_{ij}$ and $X_{ji}$ of each reciprocal pair to be correlated, with a nondegenerate joint law that has a finite mixed fourth moment. If the pairs and the diagonal entries also have bounded densities on their real linear supports, we prove an elliptic law for every symmetric doubly stochastic profile whose largest entry tends to zero. For i.i.d. $ξ_{ij}$ as above and general profiles with vanishing largest entry and bounded average row sum, we show that the ESD is asymptotically close to the Brown measure of the matrix $(\sqrt{s_{ij}}c_{ij})$ of free circular elements. The ESD converges weakly in probability if and only if $N^{-1}\log\mathrm{per}(S_N+qI)$ converges for every $q>0$, and these limits determine the radial distribution of the limit. Distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1
Zihao Geng; Qian-Qian Chen; Ji-Ming Guo

The gem is obtained by joining a vertex to every vertex of a path on four vertices. A distance-hereditary split graph is a split graph containing no induced gem. In this paper, we characterize all connected distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1 and determine the multiplicity of the eigenvalue 1. Our result extends previous results on threshold graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1.

States with identical protected observations can admit different future interventions. Each transition specifies its successor, response increment, required initial reserve and net consumption. Composing these records in execution order distinguishes protocols with equal net consumption and different initial reserve requirements. At a fixed state, a weighted Gram operator determines the linear response ellipsoid and a quotient identifies directions attainable only through cooperation between blocks. Nonlinear systems with identical complete affine data can have incomparable finite-budget response sets. In regular charts, the first correction to quadratic minimum cost is a covariant cubic form involving the third derivative of cost and the Hessians of protection and response. At singular gates, sequential feasibility depends on the peak reserve along the path. A history-weighted operator detects responses outside the old channel's range closure. Controlled congruence characterizes exact reductions of deterministic labelled dynamics, and a two-cut value identity separates the effect of paid verification from that of subsequent action selection.
 On Qwen2.5-7B Base, two projected policies preserved 2,048 reference top tokens under a per-position KL ceiling of $2\times10^{-5}$. Over 200 arrivals they recovered 391 of 396 initial rejections. Each yielded over 1,200 times the held-out cross-entropy reduction of historical-channel-only AdamW. Under an expanded 2,560-position contract, fixed continuation and neutral renewal began on the same protected logit fiber in distinct structural strata. Both admitted all 200 subsequent writes. Fixed continuation yielded 1.74 times the held-out loss reduction per unit squared write cost. Renewal had a smaller KL excess on the first candidate tested at every arrival and used fewer full verification scans.
Infinitely Many Plasma Echo Cascades and Sobolev Norm Divergence at the Gevrey-3 Threshold

We construct a global solution to the confined Vlasov--Poisson system near a fixed homogeneous Penrose-stable equilibrium that exhibits infinite-time growth driven by nonlinear plasma echoes. For every sufficiently small \(ε>0\), the initial perturbation has size \(O(ε)\) in a Gevrey-3 norm with radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\). The corresponding solution is real and neutral, and the full distribution remains nonnegative. Its kinetic profile scatters in a lower Sobolev topology, while the spatial density and electric field decay. Nevertheless, the kinetic profile satisfies
 \[ \lim_{t\to\infty}\|f(t)\|_{H^{1000}_{z,v}}=\infty. \]
 The construction combines infinitely many well-separated echo cascades within a single global nonlinear solution. Each cascade generates a high-frequency output that persists under the subsequent evolution, and the accumulated outputs produce divergence in a fixed Sobolev norm. Thus, unlike finite-time echo amplification, the instability persists to arbitrarily large times despite scattering and macroscopic Landau damping. The construction identifies an instability mechanism at the critical amplitude-dependent Gevrey-3 radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\), where cumulative echo amplification balances the initial Fourier decay.
Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
Mengxiao Gao; Elly K. H. Hung; Yuchen Wu; Yi Yu

Estimating the score function of a distribution plays a central role in statistics and machine learning, with applications in distribution estimation, sampling, and score-based generative modeling. However, learning scores from sensitive data raises privacy concerns. These concerns are particularly pronounced in score-based generative modeling, where trained models may memorize individual training examples and expose sensitive information through membership inference and data extraction attacks.
 Although non-private score estimation has been extensively studied, the statistical limits of its private counterpart remain less understood. In this work, we study score estimation under $(α,β)$-differential privacy for $d$-dimensional sub-Gaussian distributions with locally $γ$-Hölder-continuous scores. We develop a sampling-based private score estimator using quadratic B-splines and the exponential mechanism, and we implement our proposal through projected Langevin Monte Carlo with runtime polynomial in the sample size $n$. The proposed estimator satisfies $(α,β)$-differential privacy, and achieves expected density-weighted squared error $\mbox{polylog}(n) \max(n^{-2γ/(d+2γ+2)},\,(nα)^{-2γ/(d+γ+1)})$. We also establish a nearly matching private minimax lower bound, thereby characterizing the privacy-accuracy trade-off for score estimation. As an application, we construct a differentially private diffusion model whose privacy guarantee is independent of the number of denoising steps. We show that, with an appropriate discretization scheme, the resulting diffusion model attains nearly minimax optimal expected total variation error among all private distribution estimators. We validate our theoretical findings through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
On the Smallest Cayley Table Fill That Uniquely Determines a Group

The article investigates the minimal number of cells in a Cayley table that must be filled in order to uniquely determine a group. An exact result is obtained for groups of orders \(2\)--\(23\), and an upper bound is given for an arbitrary order.
Computing Optimal Non-stationary Policies for the Probabilistic Reach-Avoid Problems
Saber Omidi; Momotaz Begum; Marek Petrik; Se Young Yoon

We develop and analyze an algorithm for computing optimal non-stationary policies for probabilistic reach-avoid problems. The objective in probabilistic reach-avoid problems is to maximize the probability of reaching a goal without visiting predefined avoid states. Prior work has focused on computing optimal stationary reach-avoid policies. Stationary policies use the same action distribution whenever a given state is visited. This paper shows that stationary reach-avoid policies may be suboptimal and non-stationary policies may outperform them in reach probability by a margin arbitrarily close to one. To compute optimal non-stationary policies, we reduce the reach-avoid problem to a constrained average-reward Markov decision problem and propose an algorithm to compute lottery-based policies from a standard linear program formulation. We prove that the lottery-based policies are optimal and show that they are simple to compute, analyze, interpret, and implement. The numerical experiments confirm that the lottery-based policies can outperform state-of-the-art stationary policies even in complex domains.
Ryutaro Misawa; Masanori Sawa; Filip Špiranec

For every strength, we prove the existence of rational designs on spheres, orthogonal and unitary groups, real and complex Grassmannians, and ellipsoids that are defined by positive-definite quadratic forms with rational coefficients and have a rational point. This answers Bannai's Problem for these spaces, solves the problem of Cui--Xia--Xiang on rational spherical $4$-designs on the unit circle, and proves Xiang's conjecture in the stronger form of existence in every dimension. To this end, we introduce the $(G,\mathcal{S})$-Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem for an abelian group $G$ and a finite set of characters $\mathcal{S}$ and develop its existence and minimality theory. We also prove a general theorem transforming integer-weighted rational designs into equi-weighted designs on distinct rational points. On the unit circle $\mathbb{S}^1$, we determine the minimum sizes of rational spherical designs of strengths $4,5,6,7$ and show that they are respectively $2304,4608,9216,9216$. We also show that the minimum size of a rational spherical $5$-design on $\mathbb{S}^2$ is $192$. We further apply our framework to prove a conjecture of Thuswaldner--Ziegler on sums of distinct units and to answer Mahabaduge's problem on convex equilateral lattice polygons affirmatively.
When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?

Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.
Critical edges and endpoint sparse dominations for the lacunary spherical maximal operator

We study sparse bounds for the lacunary spherical maximal operator in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. Lacey in 2019 established $(r,s)$-sparse bounds in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(\frac{d}{d+1},\frac{d}{d+1})$ in the $(1/r,1/s)$-plane. We extend these bounds to the two open critical edges, answering a question of Roos and Seeger. At their common vertex, we also obtain a sparse bound with a logarithmic modification in the first average.
 The main ingredient in our argument is a local estimate based on the local density of the input level sets, which replaces the modulus of continuity estimate used in Lacey's proof.

For a perfect matching $M$ on $[2n]$, let $P_M$ be the interval order on its edges and let $\operatorname{Open}(M)$ be the set of smaller endpoints of its edges. For an opening set $O$ that occurs for some matching, put $S_O=\sum_{\operatorname{Open}(M)=O}X_{\operatorname{Inc}(P_M)}$ and $H_O=ωS_O$. We give explicit Schur and power-sum expansions of $H_O$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and prove that $H_O$ is $h$-positive (equivalently, $S_O$ is $e$-positive). The Schur coefficients count standard tableaux of staggered skew shapes with prescribed entries in the left cells of distinguished dominoes. The Schur expansion follows from a Jacobi--Trudi sign-reversing involution on arrays with prescribed opener positions. For every partition $μ$ of $n$, a coefficient-transfer formula expresses $[h_μ]H_O$ as a positive scalar multiple of an elementary coefficient of the chromatic symmetric function of a clique blow-up of a path. This graph is a unit interval graph, so Hikita's theorem gives nonnegativity. The power-sum coefficients admit a cycle-type autocorrelation formula in terms of the restricted permutations from the Ferrers threshold model and an interpretation by alternating permutations with prescribed valley values and record partitions; we also obtain explicit threshold formulas. Further results include descent-set refinements, formulas for selected $h$-coefficients, and a rim-hook cancellation for the coefficient of $h_n$. These results refine the global matching identity of Amdeberhan, Shareshian, and Stanley.
Stein degree on birational log Calabi-Yau fibrations

We prove uniform bounds for the Stein degrees of boundary divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations of Fano type over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero. The main ingredient is the birational case for which we provide two approaches.
A Note on Spherical Images of Convex Hypersurfaces

A theorem of Wu states that the closure of the image of the Gauss map of an open convex hypersurface is geodesically convex, although the image itself may not be. We show that the general version of this theorem follows from a short proof for smooth hypersurfaces due to do Carmo and Lawson. We also show that all closed, geodesically convex subsets of spheres are attained as spherical images of convex hypersurfaces and give examples of convex surfaces whose spherical images cannot be attained as spherical images of smooth surfaces.
Separated solutions for a critical competitive system with sublinear coupling in domains with shrinking holes
Zijuan Gao; Qing Guo; Chengxiang Zhang

We construct nonnegative, fully nontrivial separated solutions for the critical competitive system of two coupled elliptic equations with a sublinear competitive coupling, in a bounded domain with two shrinking holes, for $N\ge5$ and every fixed $β<0$; each component concentrates at one of the holes and vanishes near the other. The coupling is not $C^1$ at the origin, so a direct Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction is unavailable, and the reduction has to be closed in a Lebesgue space although the matching requires $L^\infty$ control. We therefore solve a nonlinear outer problem by minimization, derive the dead-core property, solve the two scalar inner problems by a nonlinear contraction, match the inner and outer solutions, and close the scale and position equations by a Brouwer degree argument. This gives a Coron-type construction in the high-dimensional sublinear-coupling regime.
Andrzej Derdzinski; Sinhwi Kim; JeongHyeong Park

We call a Riemannian metric on a four-manifold, as well as the underlying conformal structure, conformally even/odd if its self-dual and anti-self- dual Weyl tensors acting on bivectors have, at each point, equal/opposite spectra. The term mixed parity refers to the simultaneous occurrence of both of these conditions, an obvious example being the conformally flat case. After listing various known classes of conformally even metrics, we construct examples of conformally odd ones which are not of mixed parity, as well as some metrics of mixed parity that are not conformally flat. The former examples are provided by left-invariant metrics on Lie groups, and realize uncountably many local conformal-equivalence types. The latter also include some arising from Lie groups, as well as certain 1+3 Riemannian products that are not locally conformally homogeneous.
Convex splitting by binary quantum hypothesis testing

How many independent quantum systems does it take to hide one system that is correlated with a reference? An observer can measure all the systems together with the reference to detect the correlation. We turn any such measurement into binary tests on a single system and the reference. For each test we bound the probability of declaring a signal when an independent pair was prepared. Averaging the largest signal acceptance probabilities allowed by these bounds controls the normalized trace distance in the convex-split lemma. A second bound gives a sufficient number of systems by minimizing the hypothesis-testing relative entropy over the state of the reference. Both bounds hold for density operators on separable Hilbert spaces. Comparing two distributions for the location of the hidden system gives one-shot bounds for private communication and one-way secret key distillation, including the public information available to an eavesdropper. For a fixed finite-alphabet model with separable quantum outputs and positive information advantage and variances, we recover the known Gaussian corrections to the attainable number of private or key bits from $n$ independent repetitions and bound the remaining loss by $\log_2 n+O(1)$ at fixed errors. The position-based key distillation protocol attains this bound with $O(n)$ public bits.
Note on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers II
Invariance of Property (T) for Étale Groupoids
Xiangqi Qiang; Rui Liu; Chengjun Hou

We study topological Property (T) for locally compact Hausdorff étale groupoids under pullbacks, amplifications, and Morita equivalencen. We show that Kazhdan pairs for the regular representation family pull back along Haar system-preserving homomorphisms, and for general representation families we identify a constant-vector compatibility condition as the additional hypothesis needed. We also show that Property (T) for the regular representation family passes from a groupoid to its transformation groupoid with the same Kazhdan constant; under a natural restriction condition on representation families, the same holds for general families. Finally, we prove that Property (T) is invariant under ampliation for ample groupoids with compact unit spaces, both for all representations and for the regular representation family. Hence topological Property (T) is Morita invariant for ample Hausdorff étale groupoids with compact unit spaces, and likewise for the regular representation family.
Characterizations and Algebraic, Perturbation, and Topological Properties of $θ(H)$

Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $θ(H)$ be the class of bounded operators whose restrictions to every nonzero closed reducing subspace attain their numerical radii. We characterize this property by eigenvalues of suitable self-adjoint parts. For normal operators, membership in $θ(H)$ is equivalent to pure point spectrum and reverse well-ordering of the moduli of eigenvalues. Without normality assumptions, we prove stability under finite orthogonal direct sums using graph subspaces of closed, possibly unbounded, intertwining operators. We give a compact-perturbation criterion in terms of the essential numerical radius and show that an operator remains in $θ(H)$ under every compact perturbation if and only if it is compact. Finally, $θ(H)$ is norm-dense in $\mathcal B(H)$ and is norm closed if and only if $H$ is finite-dimensional.
Twisted enveloping algebras for permutation orbifolds

We formulate a topological formal calculus for continuous distributions with values in linearly topologized spaces.
 We apply it here to construct permutation-twisted fields directly from products and branch specializations.
 For a vertex operator algebra $V$, the key structural observation is that modes of tensors with at most one non-vacuum factor topologically generate the permutation-twisted enveloping algebra.
 Combining this observation with the calculus and $Δ_N$, we obtain
 an explicit isomorphism $\mathscr{U}_σ(V^{\otimes N})\cong\mathscr{U}(V)$
 for an $N$-cycle $σ$, with grading and canonical filtrations rescaled by $N$.
 For arbitrary permutations, the cycle factors are rescaled before taking their degreewise completed tensor product.
Improved Constants in the Kautz-Singleton Construction for Probabilistic Group Testing

We consider the probabilistic nonadaptive group testing problem, in which a uniformly random defective set of size $d$ is to be identified among $N$ items using a binary test matrix. For the explicit Kautz--Singleton construction, it is known that order-optimal scaling $T=Θ(d\log N)$ for high-probability recovery can be achieved in the regime $d=Ω(\log^2 N)$. However, the leading constant in this scaling remains uncharacterized even for standard low-complexity decoders. In this work, we revisit the probabilistic analysis of this construction and improve the leading constant for the COMP decoder, as well as establishing the same bound for the DD decoder. Our approach relies on a sharper analysis of the number of distinct roots associated with the defective items, yielding tighter bounds on the decoding error probability. In particular, we show that both COMP and DD achieve vanishing average error probability with $T\le (1/\ln 2+\varepsilon)d\log N$ tests for any $\varepsilon>0$, in the admissible regime $N=q^k$ for some prime power $q = Θ(d)$ and integer $k \ge 2$. For COMP, this leading constant matches that of the random near-constant column weight design, whereas for DD, a gap remains except in the sparse regime $d = N^{o(1)}$.
On the Type E case of the Brown Wemyss realization conjecture

We consider the remaining Type E case of the Brown-Wemyss numerical realization conjecture. The noncommutative splitting lemma and the Type A and D classifications of Brown and Wemyss leave two-generator cyclic potentials with cubic part $x^3$. For these remaining potentials, we construct geometric realizations under the hypothesis of radical growth dimension at most one. The construction combines marked ADE deformations and cyclic coordinate changes for lengths three, four, and six with a filtered finiteness argument in length five. Under the numerical growth hypothesis, cubic lower bounds exclude the other branches for every choice of formal tail. The resulting contractions have a regular source and a complete local cDV target. Finite-dimensional algebras are realized by threefold flops, and the sole growth-one algebra in this residual case is $\operatorname{Jac}(x^3+xy^3)$, for which we give a divisor-to-curve contraction.
DeoPC: Data-Enabled Output-Feedback Predictive Control for State Regulation
Jingyuan Li; Dawei Shi; Ling Shi

Constrained regulation of the internal state of an unknown linear system is challenging when only input-output measurements are available online. In this work, we develop a data-enabled output-feedback predictive control (DeoPC) framework for constrained state regulation using input-output data. Specifically, a data-driven state estimate is constructed from past input-output data via a subspace-based singular value decomposition. Based on this state representation, we formulate a predictive controller that directly penalizes the state and control effort while enforcing the system constraints. Under persistent excitation and initialization conditions, we establish recursive feasibility and closed-loop stability of DeoPC in both noise-free and bounded-noise settings. In addition, we show that DeoPC can be calibrated to the physical state coordinates using a few offline state measurements, or treated as a model predictive control tuning problem when no state measurements are available. The effectiveness of DeoPC is demonstrated through simulations on an unstable batch reactor system.
Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
Yin Liu; Shanshan Zhao; Didong Li

Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development. However, limited attention has been devoted to synthetic time-to-event data, which are central to clinical trials and survival analysis. In particular, theoretical guarantees for the distributional fidelity of synthetic survival data remain largely unexplored. More importantly, even when a generator achieves distributional fidelity, it remains unclear whether the downstream statistical analysis is reliable. To address these gaps, we propose a general two-stage generative framework for survival data (TSGSurv) that jointly generates observed times and covariates conditional on event status, and establish its distributional convergence rate. Focusing on the widely used Cox proportional hazards model, we establish conditions under which generator fidelity guarantees consistency of model coefficient estimates. We further characterize the limitations of naive inference based on synthetic data, and develop a variance correction and a distribution calibration procedure to recover valid inference of original data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed generative and inferential framework with extensive simulations and two real data applications.
Dimension-Free Buffer Bounds for Compressed-Momentum Error Feedback

Analyses of error feedback bound the memory buffer through a compressor contraction constant -- $r/p$ for the best rank-$r$ approximation of a $p$-dimensional spectrum -- which survives into the rate. We show it need not appear at all. When the compressed momentum is re-injected into the pre-compression accumulator, the previous compressed momentum $β_1 M_{t-1}$ is an admissible competitor in the projection, and the buffer obeys $\|E_t\|_F \le (1-β_1)\|G_t\|_F + γ\|E_{t-1}\|_F$, free of the dimensions $m,n$ and of the rank $r$. The argument uses only that the compressor is a metric projection onto a closed cone, so it covers top-$k$ selection as well as truncated SVD, holds for every selection from the projection set with no condition on singular-value crossings, and in its trajectory-tracking form assumes nothing about the gradients. In the two-stage template of the standard analyses it replaces a Stage-2 constant of order $p^2/r^2$ by one of order $1$, against $Θ(p/r)$ for the sharpest contraction-based bounds. Transferring the full rate costs a leakage term, which we bound by the step-weighted gradient mass $\sum_{u\le t}η_u\|G_u\|_F$ and show tight up to a factor $\sqrt{2}$; the price is an additive $O(\log^2 T)$ floor, not a slower rate. On BERT fine-tuning at rank ratio $32/768$ the feedback decay costs under $0.008$ validation $F_1$.
A Faà di Bruno Convolution Identity in Parafermion Operator Products

We give a detailed combinatorial proof of a Faà di Bruno convolution identity used in parafermion operator-product calculations. The identity establishes the cancellation of potentially more singular terms and shows that the leading contribution combines the polynomial indices additively. The proof, originating in the author's doctoral thesis, provides a general derivation of an identity stated in earlier parafermion literature.
Total acyclicity of Q-shaped diagrams and N-stable categories

We study total acyclicity of $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective modules. We prove that an acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagram $P$ of projective $A$-modules is totally acyclic if and only if the associated module $K_q(P)$, or equivalently $C_q(P)$, is Gorenstein projective for every $q\in \Q$. We also establish Frobenius structures on the categories of acyclic and totally acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective $A$-modules and introduce the associated defect category. Using adjunctions between $\Q$-shaped diagrams and chain complexes, we compare this category with the classical projective defect category and show that their vanishing is equivalent under a mild condition on the Serre functor of $\Q$. Finally, we apply our results to $N$-complexes and extend the $N$-stable equivalence of Brightbill and Miemietz beyond the Gorenstein setting, obtaining a triangle equivalence between the homotopy category of totally $N$-acyclic complexes of projective $A$-modules and the $N$-stable category of Gorenstein projective $A$-modules.
Note on the random triadic process II

For a fixed integer $r\geqslant 3$, the random $r$-generalized triadic process starts from a minimum weakly $K_r$-saturated graph, namely the complete $(r-1)$-partite graph $K_{1^{r-2},n-r+2}$ with $r-2$ singleton parts and one part of size $n-r+2$. At each step of the process a new edge $\boldsymbol{e}$ is added with probability $p$, provided there exists a copy of $B_{r-2}$ in $K_n$ for which $\boldsymbol{e}$ is its spine and the only edge that has not yet been added to the current graph, where $B_{r-2}$ denotes a triangular book graph consisting of $r-2$ triangles sharing a single common edge known as the spine of the book. When $r=3$, this is the random triadic process. Korándi et al. proved a sharp threshold probability ${p}= \frac 12n^{ - \frac 12}$ for the propagation of the random triadic process.Tian and Yang complemented those results by considering the final size of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when ${p}=o( n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ α(3-r)} n)$ for any fixed constant $α> \frac 12$.In this note, we further consider the sharp threshold probability $\tilde{p}_r$ for the propagation of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when $r\geqslant 4$. We prove that $\frac 12 n^{- \frac 12}<\tilde{p}_r\leqslant c\, n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ \frac 12} n$ for some positive constant $c$, and conjecture that $\tilde{p}_r= c_r\, n^{ - \frac 12}$, where $c_r= \frac 12(r-2)!^{ \frac{1}{2r-4}}\bigl( \frac{2r-5}{r-2}\bigr)^{ \frac{2r-5}{2r-4}}$.
An explicit domain-preserving projected Milstein scheme with strong order one for stochastic systems
Xingwei Hu; Yaozhong Hu; Aiguo Xiao

A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants. To accommodate more general domain constraints, we consider stochastic systems on bounded or unbounded open convex polyhedral domains, where coefficients may exhibit boundary singularities and polynomial growth. Under local regularity, growth and boundary assumptions, we establish well-posedness and integrability estimates for the exact solution. Then we construct an explicit projected Milstein scheme that preserves the domain by applying a Euclidean projection onto a step-size-dependent interior set after each Milstein update. For systems driven by multidimensional commutative noise, we prove strong order-one convergence for the maximum grid error in Lp, for suitable p > 1 and sufficiently small step sizes under additional weighted regularity and stability conditions. The proof combines these integrability estimates with local Milstein consistency, localization and weighted stability, without requiring a priori step-size-uniform moment or boundary inverse-moment bounds for the numerical approximation. Applications to constrained stochastic models and numerical experiments illustrate the observed first-order convergence behavior.
Blow-up suppression for the Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system by Taylor--Couette flow outside a disk

Taylor--Couette devices have been investigated for enzymatic reactions and cell culture, where cylinder rotation provides a means of controlling mixing and mass transfer (Schrimpf et al., AIChE J., 2021). Motivated by these applications, this paper studies blow-up suppression in the two-dimensional Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system outside the unit disk. We prove that sufficiently strong Taylor--Couette flow yields a unique global strong solution whose density and concentration are uniformly bounded in time, without smallness assumptions on the initial cell mass or the fixed initial velocity perturbation. The main difficulty is that the angular shear tends to zero at infinity, so decay estimates on bounded regions do not directly control the full solution. To overcome this difficulty, radially weighted energy estimates exploit the radial velocity to control the density and vorticity at large radii. Combining these bounds with linear decay estimates and an energy comparison with the radial chemotaxis solution yields convergence of the density in $L^2$ to the radial solution with angularly averaged initial density, uniformly on fixed finite time intervals away from $t=0$ as the rotation amplitude tends to infinity. The decay of the radial solution then makes the full density small in $L^2$ at a finite time. An energy estimate preserves this smallness and gives global continuation.
A decoupled structure-preserving scheme for pressure-driven multispecies tumor growth

We propose an Onsager-based scheme for an $m$-species pressure-driven reaction--cross-diffusion system with a common homeostatic pressure. The scheme uses a modified scalar energy structure to update the total density, followed by compatible updates of the individual species. The global nonlinear problem remains scalar, and the species densities sum exactly to the updated total density. We establish unique solvability and show that the scheme preserves species nonnegativity, the pressure bound and total-mass monotonicity and satisfies a discrete energy dissipation law without a time-step restriction. We further develop a predictor--corrector extension to improve temporal accuracy while retaining these structural properties. Numerical experiments verify the accuracy and structure-preserving properties of the proposed schemes and demonstrate their computational efficiency.
A Uniform Positive Lower Bound for the Analyticity Radius of KdV on the Real Line

We show that, for the Korteweg--de Vries equation on the real line with real-valued initial data in an $L^2$-based analytic class, the radius of spatial analyticity of the solution has a fixed positive lower bound for all time. This improves the previous quantitative lower bounds, which tend to zero as $|t|\to\infty$. The proof uses a positive measure representation of the Hamiltonian multipliers to sum the KdV Hamiltonians into an exactly conserved energy that controls the analytic norm.
Covering Location Optimization at GPU Speed

Large-scale covering location optimization often involves NP-hard combinatorial problems that pose substantial computational challenges in urban facility planning. This paper proposes a GPU-accelerated parallel search framework for the maximal covering location problem, combining device-resident multi-trajectory exploration with lightweight CPU-side coordination. Exploiting the structure of one-swap moves, exact incremental gains are evaluated through sparse coverage representations and tiled CUDA kernels. A hierarchical reduction identifies the best exchange without materializing the full swap-gain matrix, while GPU-resident destroy-and-repair and elite-guided restarts balance intensification and diversification. Computational experiments on nine real-world urban configurations demonstrate consistent improvements over GRASP, achieving a mean relative gap of 0.029\% against published best-known solutions (BKS) and reaching BKS in 50 of 90 independent runs. On the largest urban benchmark, Kings, with 7,730 candidate locations and a budget of 50 facilities, the proposed method reaches BKS in all ten runs using a consumer-grade NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti GPU, requiring only 45.2 seconds on average to obtain its final incumbent, compared with 99.5 seconds reported for AILS-PR in a high-performance computing cluster environment. The source code and benchmark reproduction scripts are publicly available at https://github.com/Yuntian-Zhang/GPU4CO
Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models

Combining fine-tuned models by composing their parameter updates has become a standard alternative to multi-task training. We formalize composability as a property of a collection of task vectors and prove that the excess loss of the merged model is controlled by an interference functional of the cross-task curvature overlap and the signed alignment of the updates. In the quadratic regime this functional equals the excess loss, giving a criterion that is necessary as well as sufficient and that measures the angle between task vectors in the curvature metric rather than the Euclidean one. Fine-tuning under a curvature-guided regularizer -- constructed from curvature statistics of the kind memory-efficient optimizers maintain -- keeps displacement in the base curvature metric below a ceiling set by the penalty coefficient at every iterate, at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ non-convex rate. Under a single Loewner comparison between the base statistic and the task curvatures, this control converts into a ceiling on the interference functional, inversely proportional to the penalty coefficient, so that the curvature term of the bound is controlled during training. A first-order term, present because regularized solutions are not stationary for the task loss, is not reduced in the same way. Experiments on an exact non-quadratic model confirm the budget and the ceiling, show the first-order term dominating for strong penalties, and find the curvature-guided penalty slightly better than an isotropic one. In a three-seed transformer study the functional is rank-correlated with merging degradation, but no more strongly than the Euclidean displacement norm.
Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy

Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; if the $d$-fold cyclic cover of $X$ along the map is formal, the same holds at every $d$-th root of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime $p$. Each condition amounts to the vanishing of certain Massey products along the class of the map; together they say that the rational cochains of every finite cyclic cover along the map, and the mod-$p$ cochains of $X$, are formal as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. For the complement of a central hyperplane arrangement, with its Milnor fibration, Alexander formality holds exactly when the numbers of hyperplanes in its irreducible factors have no common divisor greater than 1; so the complement of an irreducible arrangement of two or more hyperplanes is never Alexander formal, although it is formal.
 On the side of covers, we show that a CDGA graded by an abelian group, over a field of characteristic zero in which the characters of the group separate its points, is formal if and only if it is formal as a graded CDGA. Consequently, the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$; the converse fails, through a Jordan block at an eigenvalue of infinite order, which no finite cover detects. Modulo $p$, eigenvalues of $p$-power order collide with 1, producing Jordan blocks that strong formality allows. The two conditions are incomparable; all four resulting classes contain arrangement complements.
Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules

We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation. Every polynomial relation of degree at most $d$ is detected modulo $t^{d+1}$. For $d\ge1$ this bound is sharp for each elliptic curve.
 A rational quasi-period row gives a Galois-stable Tate line. Together with an algebraic holomorphic period ratio it forces potential splitting, which identifies the exact ordinary CM obstruction. We compute the full Tate matrix. For ordinary non-CM curves with $p\ge5$, the standard quasi-period row is rational precisely at a zero of Katz's $E_{2,p}$. Away from the zeros the two full ratios are algebraically independent. At the zeros, a nonzero quasi-period and the normalized holomorphic ratio have algebraically independent images in $\mathbb C_p$. The complex question that motivates these results, the analogue for Drinfeld modules, and a conditional arithmetic consequence for Katz values complete the comparison.
Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, II. Operator-Theoretic Tools

This is the second part of a two-part work on semiclassical Weyl laws and Connes' integration formulas for spectral triples. It establishes three operator-theoretic results, which are used in Part I but are of independent interest. The first is a factorization formula for the fractional commutators $[|D|^{-α},a]$, which is obtained by means of double operator integrals. The second is an enhancement, for arbitrary unital spectral triples, of a lemma of Connes-Sukochev-Zanin on the differences $(a^{1/2}|D|^{-α}a^{1/2})^s-|D|^{-αs}a^s$, together with a holomorphic version of it. The third is a Tauberian theorem showing that zeta function and heat trace conditions of the type sought by Connes imply Weyl laws for the operators $aD^2a$, where $a$ ranges over positive invertible elements of the algebra. Along the way, we obtain a version for spectral triples of the Tauberian theorem of McDonald-Sukochev-Zanin without any extra regularity assumption or restriction on the degree of summability. This paper can be read largely independently of Part I.

We prove convexity in the affine orbit of entropies associated to Gauss curvature flow for sub-affine powers. This allows the construction of an affine boosted Gauss curvature flow, which keeps the evolving hypersurface at the affine minimizer of the Gaussian entropy. The modified flow has bounded isoperimetric ratio, and after rescaling it converges along a sequence of times to self-similar solutions of the Gauss curvature flow. The construction also proves existence of new self-similar solutions to Gauss curvature flow in the sub-affine regime.
A GPU Interior-Point Solver with Macro-Element Condensation for Equilibrium-Based Plasticity

Equilibrium-based conic formulations of elastoplasticity and limit analysis provide statically admissible stress fields but generate large Newton systems whose sparse factorization limits three-dimensional computations. This work develops and analyzes a macro-element condensation tailored to the Newton systems arising from primal--dual interior-point methods. Exploiting four-tetrahedron macro-elements, the method eliminates stress directions and macro-internal traction-continuity multipliers, yielding reduced systems that can be solved using positive-definite factorizations, with estimated reductions of approximately \(4\times\) in dimension and structural nonzeros relative to stress-only elimination. The validity of this elimination is established through global and macro-local nonsingularity conditions. Local nonsingularity is independent of the yield criterion in elastoplasticity, whereas in limit analysis it holds directly for Rankine and is ensured for von Mises through trace-bound augmentation. Numerical results show that, relative to stress-only elimination, the proposed condensation achieves CPU speedups of up to approximately \(2\times\) and reduces peak linear-solver memory by up to \(66.5\%\). We further develop a CUDA Fortran implementation that exploits uniform macro-local blocks through batched routines and uses cuDSS for the reduced sparse solve. This implementation achieves speedups of up to \(13.5\times\) over its CPU counterpart and up to \(87.5\times\) over MOSEK, while successfully solving the largest tested 3D problems that exceed the device-memory capacity of the GPU solver CuClarabel. For elastoplasticity, we also propose a preconditioned conjugate-gradient solver that reduces device-memory requirements relative to the direct GPU solver, at the expense of increased solution time.
Strong chromatic index of graphs with Ore-degree at most nine
Xiaoxue Hu; Jiangxu Kong; Yu Xue

The strong chromatic index $χ_s^{\prime}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of colors in an edgecoloring in which distinct edges at distance at most two in the line graph receive different colors. Let $θ(G)=\max _{x y \in E(G)}\left(d_G(x)+d_G(y)\right)$ denote the maximum edge weight, also called the Ore-degree, of $G$. We prove that every finite loopless multigraph $G$ with $θ(G) \leq 9$ satisfies $χ_s^{\prime}(G) \leq 28$. For simple graphs, this improves the direct greedy bound from 32 to 28. In particular, it verifies the Erdős-Nešetřil conjecture for simple graphs of maximum degree five whose vertices of degree five form an independent set, using one fewer color than the conjectured bound of 29. When $θ(G)=9$, our bound is four colors above the bound of 24 predicted by the Ore-degree conjecture of Chen, Huang, Yu, and Zhou.
Stability analysis and critical thresholds in a nonlocal advection diffusion model of wound healing on bounded domains

Nonlocal advection diffusion models describe how wound healing depends on the strength of cell-cell adhesion and the cell sensing radius. Depending on these parameters, the wound may close completely or remain in a persistent state with a spatially nonuniform cell density. The model combines random cell movement, cell proliferation, and cell-cell adhesion within a finite sensing radius. We first derive the dispersion relation on the whole line and use it to compute the critical sensing radius and the corresponding wavelength. This relation shows that diffusion and cell proliferation stabilize the healed state, while cell-cell adhesion can make it unstable. On a bounded interval, the cell density is fixed at the healthy value on an exterior collar. In this setting, we establish conditions that keep the cell density within a positive bounded range, derive a sufficient condition for nonlinear exponential stability that depends on domain size, and formulate and numerically solve the associated linear spectral problem. The analysis shows how reducing the domain size can stabilize the healed state at parameter values for which the whole line model is linearly unstable. Finally, we compute critical sensing radii and domain sizes numerically and compare the sufficient stability bounds with the transitions observed in wound simulations involving perturbations of finite amplitude.
The Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology: A Methodological Shift from the Perspective of Natural Science and Engineering Practice

Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, fundamentally driven by the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm, rely on setting external objectives and iterative trial-and-error. When confronted with complex nonlinear problems containing noise and conflicting constraints, this paradigm inherently induces statistical smoothing and compromise, yielding black-box models that lack interpretability and out-of-distribution generalization. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology, reconstructing the solving process into four irreversible stages: Deconstruction, Structure, Construction, and Solving. The method suspends a priori presuppositions to strip unit coupling, extracts rigid invariants inherent to the problem, constructs equivalent mappings anchored to these invariants, and executes the mapping directly to generate the solution. Evaluation metrics and experience are relegated to a posteriori verification. Demonstrated through cross-disciplinary practices including number theory, Hamiltonian systems, deep learning, and seismic inversion, this methodology transcends the statistical fitting bottleneck. Structure-Driven and Objective-Driven methodologies are complementary: when structure is sufficient, solutions are directly constructed; when lacking, it degenerates into the OD path.
A proof of Casselman's comparison conjecture

We prove Casselman's comparison conjecture for parabolic subgroups of real linear reductive groups. Let $Q=LU$ be a standard parabolic subgroup of a real linear reductive group $G$, with Levi subgroup $L$ and unipotent radical $U$. For every Casselman--Wallach representation $π$ of $G$ and every $i\geq0$, the natural inclusion $π_K\hookrightarrowπ$ induces a topological $L$-equivariant isomorphism \[
 H_i(\mathfrak u,π_K)^\infty\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 H_i(\mathfrak u,π). \] Put $\mathscr U=\mathcal U(\mathfrak u)$ and $F_k=\mathscr U/I_{\mathfrak u}^k$, where $I_{\mathfrak u}$ is the augmentation ideal. For every $k\geq1$ and $i\geq0$, we establish natural topological $L$-isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty
 \simeq \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π),\
 \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty
 \simeq \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π). \end{aligned} \] We also obtain closedness of $\mathfrak u^kM$ for the (co)chain spaces $M=C_j(\mathfrak u,π),C^j(\mathfrak u,π)$, and for $M=J_a,J_{a-1}/J_a$, where $(J_a)$ is the smooth Bruhat filtration of a principal series representation.
Generalized Covering radii and Deep Holes of a Family of Antiprimitive Narrow-Sense BCH Codes in Even Characteristic
Ketong Ren; Bing Liu; Cuiling Fan; Haode Yan

This paper determines the generalized covering radii, deep holes, and complete coset leader weight distribution of the antiprimitive narrow-sense BCH code of length \(q+1\) and designed distance \(3\) over \(\mathbb{F}_q\), where \(q=2^m\) and \(m\geq 2\). We establish the complete generalized covering-radius hierarchy: the covering radius is \(3\), whereas the \(t\)-th generalized covering radius is \(4\) for every \(t\geq 2\). Using the covering radius, we then derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a received word to be a deep hole by reducing the syndrome representations to conditions involving roots of an associated cubic polynomial. An explicit parametrization yields complete, nonredundant representatives of all deep-hole cosets. Enumerating these representatives gives closed-form expressions for the numbers of deep holes and determines the complete coset leader weight distribution, with distinct formulas according to the parity of \(m\).
Dynamical edge universality and the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
Jiaoyang Huang; Shengjing Xu; Yulei Xu

We prove dynamical edge universality for three families of interacting particle systems for every $β>0$: $β$-Dyson Brownian motion with an analytic potential, weighted $β$-corners processes, and a class of discrete-time Markov chains. Our results apply to general non-equilibrium initial data and show that the Airy$_β$ line ensemble emerges at positive times whenever the limiting density has a regular square-root edge.
 More precisely, after centering at the moving deterministic edge and rescaling space and time on the $n^{-2/3}$ and $n^{-1/3}$ scales, respectively, the trajectories of the top $k$ particles converge jointly in distribution to the top $k$ curves of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble, for every fixed $k$, in the topology of uniform convergence on compact time intervals.
 The proof combines dynamical loop equations with characteristic-flow estimates to establish local laws near the moving edge and upper bounds on the extremal particle. We then identify the stochastic evolution of every subsequential limit of the rescaled Stieltjes transform and establish convergence through the pole-evolution characterization of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble.
Rigidity and Non-Rigidity of Disk Pseudo-Rotations below $C^2$

For every $0<β\le1$, we prove $C^0$-rigidity of area-preserving $C^{1,β}$ disk pseudo-rotations with non-Brjuno rotation number. At the $C^1$ endpoint, every non-Brjuno rotation number of zero exponential type admits non-rigid examples. We also obtain a different rigidity result when the rotation number has positive exponential type: the boundary restriction of every $C^1$ pseudo-rotation is rigid and topologically conjugate to a rotation. We show that this boundary conclusion fails in the bi-Lipschitz class by constructing non-rigid examples for every rotation number of finite positive exponential type. The proof of rigidity is based on a finite-information closing theorem under Hölder regularity. For the construction of counterexamples, we use disjoint supports instead of a summable perturbation scheme.

In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $π$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $γ$ and Feigenbaum's constant $δ$ that use each of the digits $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $π$, $γ$ and $δ$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$.
