The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the published records; for $π$ with the digits 1-9 the optimal error is $2.81\cdot 10^{-14}$. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.
A complete intersection theorem for sets of bounded size

Let \(1\le t\le k\le n\) and \(2k<n+t\). We prove that a largest \(t\)-intersecting family of subsets of \([n]\) of size at most \(k\) is obtained by taking all such subsets that contain at least \(t+r\) points of a fixed \((t+2r)\)-element set, for some \(0\le r\le\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{2}\right\rfloor\). This settles a conjecture of Ahlswede, Bey, Engel and Khachatrian from 2002.
On the regularity of stationary solutions to free boundary problems

In this note, we improve the regularity of Hölder continuous stationary solutions with respect to inner variations which are harmonic outside their zero set. We obtain a $\sqrt{\log}$-Lipschitz estimate for a class of solutions allowing a generalized phase variable and including the two-phase problem. In the case of the one-phase problem, we can improve to Lipschitz regularity. In particular, we show that the initial Lipschitz assumption in the class of variational solutions considered by Kriventsov and Weiss can be replaced by any positive Hölder exponent
Semiclassical Averaging and Temporal Fluctuations of Quantum Dark Solitons in the Lieb-Liniger Model
Kota Kaneko; Kohei Motegi; Jun Sato

We study the time evolution of quantum dark-soliton states of the Lieb--Liniger model, introduced by Sato--Kanamoto--Kaminishi--Deguchi as equal-weight superpositions of one-hole yrast states, and their relation to Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) solitons. We consider a simultaneous weak-coupling and large-system limit in which the repulsive coupling constant $c$ tends to zero and the particle number $N$ and ring circumference $L$ tend to infinity, with the mean density $\bar n=N/L$ and scaled circumference $Λ=L\sqrt{c\bar n}$ fixed. We conjecture that, in this limit, the normalized quantum density and its evolution at fixed scaled time $τ=c\bar n t$ are described by a canonical-momentum average of normalized periodic one-soliton GP densities, each evolving at its own velocity. We explicitly parametrize the GP family by canonical momentum and provide numerical evidence for this correspondence. The different velocities explain the spreading of the averaged density notch despite shape preservation by individual solitons. In the infinite-line limit, we derive an analytic expression for the initial averaged profile, establish an inverse-fifth-power decay of its density deficit with distance from the soliton center, and express the Fourier transform of its deviation from the background as a series of Bickley--Naylor functions $\operatorname{Ki}_3$. Following the spreading of the initial notch, we investigate temporal density fluctuations of the quantum dark solitons and propose a relation between long-time mode variances and second moments of GP Fourier coefficients, supported by numerical comparisons of individual mode variances and the total variance. Yrast transition frequencies distinguish the initial dephasing time scale from the longer scale associated with finite-time averaging of fluctuations.
A Nonadaptive Sparse Fourier Transform in Every Dimension

Let $G=(\mathbb{Z}/2^a\mathbb{Z})^d$, of order $N=2^{ad}$. Given point-query access to any complex signal $X$ with Fourier transform $\hat{X}$ over $G$, we provide a randomized algorithm that constructs a $k$-sparse estimate $\widetilde{X}$ via non-adaptive queries such that, with large probability, $\|\widetilde{X}-\hat{X}\|_2^2 \leq C \cdot \|H_k(\hat{X})-\hat{X}\|_2^2$, for an absolute constant $C>0$, where $H_k(\cdot)$ denotes the best $k$-sparse approximation. The constant $C$ can be improved to any desired $1+\varepsilon$ by either supplying a constant-factor estimate on the $k$-sparse tail norm or allowing an arbitrarily small additive error term $δ\|\hat{X}\|_2^2$ on the right-hand side. With a supplied tail estimate, we can also satisfy an $\ell_\infty/\ell_2$ heavy hitters guarantee. For fixed $δ$, the number of samples is $O((k/\varepsilon^2)(\log N)\log(k/\varepsilon))$, and the recovery algorithm requires a polynomial in $(k/\varepsilon)\log N$ exact operations. The algorithm naturally extends to $G=(\mathbb{Z}/b^a\mathbb{Z})^d$ for any fixed integer $b>1$.
Andrés R. Moreno; José L. Ramírez

In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths. Inspired by properties of the Calkin--Wilf tree, we study several parameters of our tree and use them to obtain new results on semi-Fibonacci partitions. We also derive generating functions for partition statistics and determine the average and extremal partition sizes at each level.
Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
Ritwik Chakraborty; Inhyeok Choi; Biswajit Nag

Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.
Gaussian Quasi-Likelihood Estimation for Nonsynchronously Observed Lévy processes

We study parametric inference for a two-dimensional simple Lévy process observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon, where the two components are sampled in a possibly non-synchronous manner. Combining Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimation for Lévy SDEs with the non-synchronous quasi-likelihood methodology, we construct a Gaussian-type quasi-likelihood based on the covariance structure of non-synchronous increments, and we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the resulting estimators. The convergence rates coincide with those in the synchronous setting, while the asymptotic variance depends essentially on the sampling design and becomes more complicated under non-synchronicity. To handle the different moment structure of pure-jump Lévy processes, we introduce an additional convergence assumption and provide tractable sufficient conditions linked to the observation scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators.
Kakutani equivalence of higher rank unipotent abelian actions I
Adam Kanigowski; Philipp Kunde; Kurt Vinhage; Daren Wei

We study Kakutani equivalence of higher-rank abelian unipotent actions. We construct a Kakutani invariant for general $\mathbb{R}^n$-actions and establish a quantitative vanishing criterion. By this criterion, we prove that ergodic abelian horocyclic actions on finite-volume quotients of connected semisimple Lie groups are loosely Kronecker. We also include a proof of the Abramov entropy formula for time changes of Rn-actions, following the strategy developed by Nadler.
Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function III

We extend the denumerant to a weighted denumerant, the sum of a function $μ$ over the solutions in non-negative integers of $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=n$. For the monomial weights $x_1^{α_1}\cdots x_k^{α_k}$, with exponents $α_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$, we prove upper and lower bounds of the kind of those of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689), with an explicit constant and explicit shifts. As an example of application, summing these bounds over all the numbers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ we find, by elementary means, the asymptotic main term of the sums $\sum_{y_1+\cdots+y_k=n}σ_{α_1}(y_1)\cdotsσ_{α_k}(y_k)$ of products of divisor functions, for every $k$ and for real exponents $α_i\neq0$ of either sign.
Variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups
Leonardo Colombo; María Emma Eyrea Irazú; David Martín de Diego; María Daniela Sánchez; Marcela Zuccalli

We develop fixed-step variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups, derive their reduced dynamics, and analyze their long-time behavior by backward error analysis. We derive the continuous Euler-Lagrange equations, energy balance, and Noether conservation laws, and construct time-indexed discrete Lagrangians using retractions, with the midpoint-Cayley scheme treated explicitly. On their regularity domains, the resulting phase-space maps are symplectic. For left-invariant discrete Lagrangians, they reduce to Lie-Poisson maps that preserve coadjoint orbits and, when $G$ is connected, every Casimir function. A variational error analysis establishes second-order accuracy of the midpoint-Cayley method. We also construct an exactly symplectic, projectable extension on $T^*(\mathbb R\times G)$ whose formal modified Hamiltonian is affine in the momentum conjugate to time and admits symmetry reduction. Under uniform analyticity, coefficient bounds, and domain-containment assumptions, optimal truncation yields exponentially accurate interpolation and near-conservation of the modified extended Hamiltonian over exponentially long intervals. For a connected attitude network on $SO(3)^N$ with damping and uniformly positive, non-increasing coupling weights, we prove local asymptotic stability of the static consensus set for the continuous dynamics and exact preservation of total spatial momentum by the discrete scheme. Numerical experiments on the network and on a time-dependent rigid body on $SO(3)$ illustrate second-order convergence and the extended energy balance.
Painlevé transcendents in the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions

This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying benchmarks in the ARCH competition.
Saksham Aggarwal; James Nichols; Katharine Turner

Persistence diagrams are widely used in topological data analysis to summarize topological and geometric structure in data. We study nonparametric regression where inputs are persistence diagrams and outputs are real-valued. Using kernel-based local averaging estimators defined directly over diagram space with Wasserstein distance, we establish consistency and derive bounds on the rate of convergence under suitable assumptions in the $L^2$-theory. We also present computational experiments that demonstrate strong performance of the proposed estimator, particularly in low data regimes.

A Piatetski-Shapiro prime is a prime number that can be written as $\lfloor m^c \rfloor$ for some positive integer $m$ and non-integer $c>1$. Li and Pan showed the results for small gaps between consecutive Piatetski-Shapiro primes for $1<c<9/8$. On the other hand, Deshouillers, Drmota, and Müllner showed the large gaps between Piatetski-Shapiro primes although they did not mention it explicitly whenever there are infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes with exponent $c$ using binomial expansion. In this article, we use a different method from theirs, and we obtain the explicit exponent that appears in their paper.
Pointwise Minmax Representations for Total Variation Denoising on Graphs

Total variation denoising (TVD) is a fundamental method in image denoising, signal processing, and nonparametric regression. We establish exact pointwise minmax/maxmin representations for TVD on arbitrary finite graphs, extending recent one-dimensional results. Under squared loss, fitted values are expressed through corrected local averages over nested connected vertex sets. The correction is a signed boundary count: edges leaving the inner set contribute +1 if they remain within the outer set and -1 otherwise. To the best of our knowledge, this representation is new even for two-dimensional TVD. We show that Brunk's classical minmax formulas for isotonic regression on every finite directed acyclic graph arise as special cases of our graph TVD representation. The exact reduction proceeds through asymmetric TVD and nearly isotonic regression, which coincides with isotonic regression above a finite penalty threshold. We further extend the representations to arbitrary finite separable convex losses, assuming coercivity of the full objective, but without requiring differentiability or strict convexity. For nonunique solutions, the possible fitted values at each coordinate form a compact interval. Its lower and upper endpoints admit maxmin and minmax representations, respectively, through scalar local optimization problems and are attained simultaneously at all coordinates by two extremal solutions. This yields exact representations for quantile TVD on arbitrary graphs and unifies TVD, nearly isotonic regression, and isotonic regression within a single pointwise framework for general separable convex losses.
Interacting framework for the free magnetic dynamics

This is the second paper of a program aimed at a rigorous many--body theory of continuum fermions in a uniform magnetic field, built on the asymptotic quasi--local structure that the magnetic coherent--state frame induces on the CAR algebra. Here we study the free dynamics. We show that a Bogoliubov dynamics preserves the local structure exactly if and only if it is generated by a function of the Landau Hamiltonian. For this class we compute the hopping coefficients in closed form, prove that the Lieb--Robinson velocity vanishes, and determine when the almost--local algebra lies in the domain of the generator. For the Landau Hamiltonian the dynamics turns out to be periodic. We then describe the ground states and the KMS states at every temperature, prove their ergodicity under magnetic translations, and recover the KMS states at positive temperature as thermodynamic limits of local Gibbs states. Finally, we relate the exact hopping operator to the Hofstadter model. These results confirm that the frame--induced local structure is a consistent setting for the perturbed and interacting magnetic dynamics to be studied next.
Exceptional zeros for $\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Yoshida lifts
Armando Gutierrez Terradillos; Lois Omil-Pazos; Óscar Rivero

The aim of this article is to study an exceptional zero phenomenon for the $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\mathrm{GSp}_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ in the critical regions (F) and (D). We construct improved $p$-adic $L$-functions by replacing the $p$-depleted Eisenstein family with its $p$-ordinary counterpart. Under a local compatibility hypothesis at the ramified places and classical control for the families, we show that their poles detect exactly the Yoshida lifts whose smaller constituent is dual to the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representation. The proof compares their residues with distinguished automorphic periods, extending the coherent period formula to the case where one modular form has weight zero. An explicit Euler-factor identity relates each improved function to the usual $p$-adic $L$-function. At these Yoshida points, the vanishing factor cancels the pole, and the resulting value is expressed through the distinguished period and the logarithmic derivative of the ordinary elliptic root. We also discuss the expected factorization along Yoshida families into Hida--Rankin $p$-adic $L$-functions.
Preservation of big diagonal for automorphisms of Hilbert schemes

If $X$ is a smooth projective surface that is not K3 or abelian surface, we show that any automorphism of the Hilbert scheme of points $X^{[n]}$ preserves the big diagonal. This generalizes several previous works, and gives a complete description of automorphisms of $X^{[n]}$ when $X$ is not K3 or abelian surface. We also obtain a Torelli-type theorem: a smooth projective surface $X$ can be recovered from $X^{[n]}$ unless $X$ is a K3 surface. Further, for each integer $n\geq 2$, we construct automorphisms of $A^{[n]}$ not preserving the big diagonal for an abelian surface $A$.
Moduli of continuity preserved by the Hilbert Transform

It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as Hölder continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-Hölder and the log-Hölder moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~\cite{ALSZ21} that for compactly supported $t$-log-Hölder continuous functions ($t>1$) their Hilbert transforms are at least $(t-1)$-log-Hölder continuous. A similar result holds for weak-Hölder continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.
DS3M: Deep structured state space models for nonlinear system identification on modern hardware

Neural state-space identification learns dynamical models from measured inputs and outputs. SUBNET combines this task with an encoder that estimates initial states from short measurement histories. Its continuous-time version requires many successive neural-network evaluations during numerical integration, resulting in slow training speed which is a major limitation for practical use cases. We propose deep structured state space models (DS3M), which combine compact nonlinear dynamical components in parallel and in series. Custom GPU kernels implemented with Triton reduce the launch and memory overhead of their sequential evaluation. We explain this construction, describe a port-Hamiltonian variant, and present various benchmark comparisons of accuracy and training time.
On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k$
Alan Filipin; Yasutsugu Fujita; Ana Jurasić

We study a class of Diophantine problems arising from triangular analogues of classical Diophantine tuples. A set of positive integers is called a triangular $D(n)$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $n$, is a triangular number. In this paper, we investigate the extensibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs of the form $\{n,2n\}$, where $n = 2k^2 + \varepsilon k$, with $k$ an odd positive integer and $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}$ such that $4k + \varepsilon$ is prime. We prove that for all $(k,\varepsilon)$ in a finite explicitly determined set, the pair $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple. The obtained results give further evidence for a general non-extensibility phenomenon, which we formulate as a conjecture.
Integer Programming Strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box Problem
Tim Kunt; Thorsten Koch; Hyejun Park

We present a selection of Integer Programming (IP) strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box problem, which asks for the longest induced path in the $d$-dimensional hypercube. Current records are based on sophisticated, exhaustive searches, with optimality proven only for instances up to dimension 8, motivating our study of IP formulations. We address symmetries and potential strengthenings. With the smallest open instance having as few as 512 binary decision variables, the proposed IPs offer a challenging and intriguing combinatorial problem. In addition, we extend the problem to higher-dimensional grid graphs and provide solutions for unexplored and unsolved instances.
Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations

Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of André's $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Frăţilă's formulation of $p$-adic periods. The formulation naturally produces deformation series of the resulting periods and Frobenius difference equations satisfied by these series. We then explain how the formulation brings the resulting $v$-adic periods within the scope of Chen's $v$-adic ABP criterion and of difference Galois theory, and gives us a strategy to study the transcendence degrees of $v$-adic periods through their deformation series. We show that certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms can be expressed in terms of André's $v$-adic periods. Applying the strategy to these examples, we obtain algebraic independence results for certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms; more precisely, the transcendence degree of the field generated by a suitable collection of special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms is one less than the transcendence degree of the field generated by the corresponding special values of $\infty$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms together with the Carlitz period.
Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture

Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. We further show that the $(1,1)$ entry of the resolvent of a nilpotent $T_m(u)$ is $λ^{-1} \pm λ^{-3} \pm λ^{-7} \pm \dots \pm λ^{-(2^K - 1)}$, with signs that determine $u$. The proof of the main theorem has been formalised in Lean~4.
Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function II

We apply the elementary arithmetic argument of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689) to binomial coefficients, and obtain upper and lower bounds for Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ that sharpen those of Agnarsson. The lower bound is a sum of binomial coefficients; it holds along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ without assuming that a solution exists, and it is greater than the polynomial lower bound of the first paper. In the upper bound the shift of Agnarsson's binomial coefficient is reduced.
A fast iterative solver for lopsided Sylvester matrix equations

A generalization of the factored alternating direction implicit algorithm is introduced that makes use of type $(p, q)$ Zolotarev rational functions to apply unequal numbers of left and right shifts. Convergence properties of the algorithm are discussed, as well as a method for computing shift parameters. Several applications are highlighted where the generalized method is useful, including in the solving of a collection of shifted linear systems, for discretizations that involve left and right operators that are not equally amenable to inversion, and for Sylvester matrix equations with differently-sized, differently-structured, or differently-conditioned coefficient matrices.
A note on Turán densities of daisies and hypergraph products

The Turán density of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is defined as $π(\mathcal{H})=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})/\binom{n}{r}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal H)$ denotes the largest number of edges in an $\mathcal H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $r\geq s\geq2$ and $t\geq s$, an $(r,s,t)$-daisy $\mathcal D_r(s,t)$ is the $r$-uniform hypergraph consisting of all unions of a fixed $(r-s)$-set with the $s$-subsets of a disjoint $t$-set. We show that for every fixed $s\geq3$, \[ \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty}π(\mathcal D_r(s,t))=1-O_s(t^{-(s-1)}) \] as $t\rightarrow\infty$. This bound is best possible up to the implicit constant by a classical result of de Caen, and it answers, in a stronger form, a question of Ellis, Ivan and Leader, who asked for the case $s=3$. Moreover, we show a related result for matroid basis hypergraphs. We also consider Turán densities of hypergraph products, of which daisies are a special case. The product of two hypergraphs on disjoint vertex sets consists of all unions of an edge of the first with an edge of the second. For the product $\mathcal H^d$ of $d$ disjoint copies of a fixed $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ that is not $r$-partite, we show that $1-π(\mathcal H^d) \rightarrow 0$ exponentially fast as $d\rightarrow\infty$, and we determine the exponential rate in terms of the minimum number of edges in a homomorphic image of $\mathcal H$. This answers a question of Bollobás, Leader and Malvenuto up to a polynomial factor in $d$, and we further address a related question of theirs for products of two different hypergraphs.
Interior and global $W^{2,1}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation

In this paper, we prove that for $3\leq k\leq n-1$, continuous $k$-convex solutions of the $k$-Hessian equation with density bounded above and below by positive constants belong to $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$. This regularity holds globally on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex domains when both the boundary and the boundary values are of class $C^{1,1}$.

Many problems in statistics, combinatorics, econometrics, and other fields are expressible in terms of the upper probability of all copulas. We formally study this capacity, which we call the upper copula capacity, as a mathematical object. In particular, we examine the capacity of given sets and integration with respect to this capacity. For two-dimensional convex sets, the upper copula capacity equals the smaller of the two coordinate projection lengths. We also give an exact formula for the capacity of lower-tail events for positively weighted sums in any dimension and characterize when the upper Choquet integral equals the supremum of expectations over all copulas. Various problems in different fields can be formulated via the upper-copula capacity, and we discuss how known and new results connect to offer new perspectives on these problems.

We introduce a random Dirac operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^2)$ that we call $1d$ Stochastic Dirac Operator and which is indexed by two parameters $κ_0,κ$. In two companion articles, we show that this operator arises generically as the small disorder limit of one-dimensional random Schrödinger operators, thus revealing a universal behavior. In the present paper, we provide a detailed construction of this singular operator, and investigate its spectral properties. In particular, we show that its spectrum is either absolutely continuous when $κ= 0$, or pure point when $κ>0$. In the latter case, we show that the shape of the eigenfunctions is given by the exponential of a two sided Brownian motion with drift, in connection with a result of Rifkind and Virág. Finally, we establish a delicate convergence result of the sequence of eigenvalues / eigenfunctions from the finite-volume operator to the infinite-volume one.
Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons

We prove that complete expanding Kähler-Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in Stein manifolds, and hence pseudoconvexity of bounded domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete Kähler-Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.
The Bolker condition and overdetermined FBI transforms

We study real analytic canonical relations satisfying the Bolker condition and show that, in the FBI representation, they can be described by phases of overdetermined FBI transforms. As an application, we give a simplified proof of an analytic regularity result for generalized Radon transforms due to Mazzucchelli-Salo-Tzou.
The geometry and classification of positive frames
Shankhadeep Mondal; Deguang Han; David Larson; Ursula M. Molter

We investigate the geometric and operator-theoretic structure of positive frames and their duals in finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, with particular emphasis on positive linear dependence, redundancy, and convex geometry. Building on the classical theory of positive spanning sets, we characterize equivalence classes of positive frames through the kernels of their synthesis operators and obtain parametrizations in terms of the relative interior of a standard simplex and suitable subsets of Grassmannians. We establish that every redundant frame admits a positive dual, regardless of whether the original frame is positive, and provide an explicit construction through a rank-one perturbation of the canonical dual. Furthermore, we investigate the affine and topological structure of positive dual frames, proving their relative openness in the space of all duals and the absence of extreme points. We characterize dual frames satisfying prescribed positive relations and derive criteria for the existence of positive-basis duals. We also examine semi-positive frames and their boundary behavior, together with connections between positive spanning, balancedness, and finite group representations. Finally, we study the convex geometry of nonnegative relation spaces and establish a directional characterization of positive-spanning robustness under arbitrary vector erasures. These results provide a unified geometric framework for understanding positive frames, their dual systems, and the role of redundancy in constrained reconstruction.
Extinction conditions for a two-sex branching process with random mating and overlapping generations
Nikita V. Gordeev; Manuel Mota; Elena B. Yarovaya

We propose a modification of the bisexual branching process with random mating and overlapping generations. Unlike the model of Molina and Mota \cite{Molina2024}, our modification introduces probabilistic age-dependent survival that depends on the state of the population. Our modification preserves the general properties of the original process. We establish two sufficient conditions characterizing the subcritical and supercritical regimes of the process, i.e., extinction of the population with probability one and survival of the population with positive probability.The results are illustrated with numerical simulations of the process performed in Python.
On generalizations of the Cohen structure theorem

The Cohen structure theorem is an important tool in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry. Recent work of Caviglia, Goswami, and Mesiti addresses the related question of which unital rings admit a maximal ideal for which the natural projection admits a section; for such rings, they prove a structure theorem in terms of semidirect products of rings. In this paper, we extract the underlying mechanism of their structure theorem to address when unital rings admit a nonzero proper ideal whose associated projection map has this property. We also address other settings involving ideals with conditions which are determined by ring theoretic properties of the corresponding quotient.
Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
Jeremy Miller; Urshita Pal; Peter Patzt

We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.
A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties

We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.
The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121

We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus. At $p = 17$ and $43$ one Hecke block of the Mordell-Weil group has logarithm divisible by $p^2$ but $p$-adic height of valuation one, and a comparison of valuations in the quadratic Chabauty identity then shows that each CM point is the only rational point in its residue disc, with no computation of the local height at $p$, no basis of the Mordell-Weil group and no equations for the curve. The inputs come from expansions of differentials at CM points and from a formula we prove for intersection numbers of CM divisors of coprime fundamental discriminants under Hecke operators on $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(\ell^e)$ (Theorem 1.3).
Iterative constructions of semifields 2-dimensional over a nucleus
Lukas Kölsch; Paolo Santonastaso; Yue Zhou

The construction of finite semifields dates back to Dickson's work in 1906. To the best of our knowledge, only two iterative constructions were previously known: those of Hiramine, Matsumoto and Oyama in 1987, and of Kantor and Williams in 2004. The latter yields, for suitable even orders, superpolynomially many pairwise non-isotopic semifields. In this paper, we use skew-polynomial rings to give a new iterative construction of finite semifields. This construction produces large families of pairwise non-isotopic semifields, each of which is $2$-dimensional over one of its nuclei. In particular, we show that this construction method yields semifields not contained in any family of semifields known so far.
On a critical nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K$-wise interaction: the cooperative case
Haining Fan; Lorenzo Giaretto; Nicola Soave

We study least energy fully non-trivial solutions of a nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K\ge3$ components and $K$-wise interaction, in the Sobolev critical regime. We consider bounded domains with Brezis--Nirenberg-type assumptions, and the associated homogeneous problem in $\mathbb R^N$. For every positive coupling, we prove the existence of a nonnegative ground state and identify a strictly positive threshold separating semi-trivial ground states from fully non-trivial ones. When the linear coefficients coincide, a finite-dimensional reduction gives an exact formula for the ground state energy and a characterization of all nonnegative ground states. In particular, above the threshold all ground states are synchronized; for sufficiently strong cooperation, their amplitude vector is unique and has an explicit asymptotic behavior. We also establish existence results for positive synchronized solutions beyond the ground state regime. For sufficiently weak cooperation, we obtain least energy positive solutions in the critical ternary case $N=K=3$, by minimizing on the component-wise Nehari set and ruling out critical concentration. The analysis includes the endpoint interaction exponent $q=1$, where the energy functional is not differentiable.
An Explicit Three-Dimensional Dispersing Billiard with Finite Horizon

We construct an explicit three-dimensional periodic Lorentz gas whose quotient by the period lattice \(2\Z^3\) has 38 spherical scatterers with rational centers and four rational radii. The scatterers are strictly separated, so the associated dispersing billiard has no corners or cusps. We prove finite horizon by establishing a common blocking margin for every rational direction. A projected-lattice estimate for the face-centered cubic core leaves nine exceptional directions, handled by a finite line-space covering certificate. Simultaneous rational approximation transfers this margin to every direction and yields an explicit upper horizon bound. All finite calculations use exact arithmetic, with verification data and algorithms included. The positive separation and blocking margins also ensure stability under sufficiently small independent perturbations of the centers and radii.

We present a formally verified Rust implementation of a first-order semidefinite programming solver, a nontrivial piece of numerical software. We wrote the solver by hand and then directed Claude to generate the entire verification in Verus, an automated theorem prover for Rust programs. We discuss the algorithm underlying the solver, its implementation in Rust, and our pragmatic approach to proving it correct in Verus.
Geometric control of diffusive relaxation: spectral design, transport bounds and transverse mode isolation

Geometric confinement changes both thermal relaxation and heat throughput, but these effects need not be governed by the same conduction path. We establish a distinction between serial and parallel geometries for passive, homogeneous Fourier conductors at fixed material properties, volume and length. For a reduced variable-area conductor, two logarithmic shape harmonics independently tune two selected Bloch-rate pairs, and exact local transport level sets permit spectral redistribution at fixed effective diffusivity. A nonperturbative weighted Poincaré bound, however, requires the effective axial diffusivity to vanish if the first positive insulated rate tends to zero at fixed length. This obstruction is avoided by continuous parallel paths with weak transverse exchange. Capacity-weighted networks identify the exchange mechanism, and a three-dimensional product domain provides an exact bulk realization. Its axial conductance remains $κV/L^2$, while exactly one positive insulated rate vanishes and the next approaches a positive limit set by axial, chamber and neck diffusion. The slow rate is asymptotically the transverse neck conductance times the sum of inverse chamber capacities. Spectral projection estimates translate this separation into a preparation- and readout-dependent observation window. The result is metastable retention of a temperature contrast under insulated conditions, not a second equilibrium state. It identifies when geometrical control of internal equilibration can be separated from macroscopic heat transport.
Convexity is overrated: Shortest paths on 4-polytopes are hard to compute

We prove that computing geodesic distance on the boundary of a rational convex $4$-polytope is NP-hard. We then construct rational $4$-polytopes with two rational points joined by exponentially many shortest paths of equal rational length, disproving several conjectures along the way. For the same problem, we also prove SQRTSUM-hardness under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. By a separate argument, we show that the square of the geodesic distance between distinct rational boundary points of a rational convex polytope is a totally positive multiquadratic number.
The low-degree sample complexity of clustering Gaussian mixtures with more groups than dimensions

We study the computational limits of clustering $n$ observations drawn from a mixture of $K$ isotropic Gaussian distributions in $\mathbb R^d$, when the number $K$ of groups is much larger than the dimension $d$. In this regime, distance-based and spectral procedures require a squared separation $Δ^2$ of order $\sqrt d$. In contrast, tensor-based procedures cluster at a polylogarithmic separation but need a sample size that is a large polynomial of $dK$, and the low-degree lower bounds known for random centers only show that $n$ must exceed $dK^2$. Focusing on normally distributed centers, we characterize the minimal separation for clustering with low-degree polynomials in the regime $K>d$, through a low-degree lower bound and a matching upper bound, up to subpolynomial factors. In particular, for $K=d^{p/2}$ with $p> 2$ a real number, we show that a sample size of the order of $K^3 d^{(\lceil p\rceil-p)/2}$ is required to recover the clustering with subpolynomial separation, and that it suffices when $p$ is not an integer.
On the ring of bounded functions on the character variety

Let $\mathfrak{X}$ denote the character variety associated to the group $(o_L, +)$, where $o_L$ is the ring of integers in a finite extension $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$. $\mathfrak{X}$ is a rigid analytic variety parametrizing locally $L$-analytic characters. Let $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)$ denote the global sections bounded by $1$. In this paper we prove that $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)= o_L[[o_L]]$, answering the question posed in [AB24].
Small-Gain Analysis of Robust Event-Triggered Extremum Seeking for Scalar Maps
Victor Hugo Pereira Rodrigues; Tiago Roux Oliveira; Miroslav Krstic; Zhong-Ping Jiang

We study a sample-and-hold implementation of gradient extremum seeking for a scalar quadratic map in which the control signal is refreshed only when an event occurs. The event generator acts on the demodulated gradient signal as it is actually measured, rather than on its averaged version, and contains a strictly positive offset, following the small-gain philosophy for robust event-triggered control. Rather than invoking averaging theorems, we work directly with the exact dynamics of the parameter estimation error. In the scalar setting, the demodulated gradient has an explicit sinusoidal structure, which is exploited through a change of variables that absorbs the zero-mean oscillatory perturbation, together with a quadratic Lyapunov function and the persistence of excitation of the probing signal. For a sufficiently fast dither, the estimation error is shown to decay exponentially to a residual neighborhood of the origin whose size is quantified by the dither amplitude and frequency, and by the relative threshold and the offset of the event generator. All constants, including the input-to-state stability gain of the extremum seeking loop, the admissible dither frequency and the positive lower bound on the time between two consecutive events, are given in closed form, so that Zeno behavior is excluded. A simulation example illustrates the results.
Self-adjoint skew quartics, symplectic monodromy, and zeta functions

For an odd prime power $P$, let $A_H(P)$ be the number of $a\in\F_{P^H}$ for which the self-adjoint skew quartic $t^4+t^3+at^2+t+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{P^H}[t;σ]$, with $σ(c)=c^P$. We determine $A_H(3)$ for every $H\ge1$ and prove that its minimal constant-coefficient recurrence has order $24$. Local ramification gives the degrees of the Steinberg and regular cuspidal Frobenius polynomials. Duality and finitely many exact counts determine both polynomials. For $P=p^f$ with $p\nmid f$, we construct an explicit genus-$P(P+1)/2$ flag curve whose zeta numerator is the Steinberg Frobenius polynomial. At $P=3$ this identifies the degree-$12$ factor computed above with the zeta numerator of a genus-$6$ curve. For general $P$ the flag curve and the regular cuspidal factors give a rational expression for the counting series. We evaluate the linear coefficients of the two factors by an elliptic-curve point count and express their quadratic coefficients through a single finite-field character sum.
Samuel B. Hopkins; Yiding Hua; Sidhanth Mohanty; Amit Rajaraman; David Steurer

We study community detection in the sparse two-community stochastic block model when an adversary may corrupt a small constant fraction of the edges of the observed graph. For every choice of parameters above the Kesten-Stigum threshold and every $\varepsilon > 0$, we give a nearly-linear-time algorithm which estimates the communities with accuracy within $\varepsilon$ of the information-theoretically optimal accuracy, while tolerating a small constant fraction of adversarially corrupted edges. Previously, efficient algorithms with optimal accuracy were known only in the absence of corruptions, while robust algorithms either achieved only weak recovery or approached optimal accuracy only in the limit of large signal-to-noise ratio. Our algorithm is simple: approximate the second eigenvector of the nonbacktracking matrix, using a semidefinite program to cope with the corruptions, and use it to initialize belief propagation. Along the way, we show that in the absence of corruptions, belief propagation initialized at this eigenvector achieves optimal accuracy, resolving an open problem of Zdeborová in the two-community case. The proof of this fact is short and independent of our robustness results--its key ingredient is a local characterization of the second eigenvector of the nonbacktracking matrix in terms of constant-depth nonbacktracking walks.
Nodal Knotted Finite-Energy Spatiotemporally Localized Scalar Wave Solutions

Significant amount of information is available in wave optics about monochromatic paraxial beams characterized by nodal knots, the latter being threads of complete darkness (lines of zero intensity) tied into knots. Also, well -known are finite-energy spatiotemporally localized vector-valued wave solutions characterized by knotted to-pologies. Unfortunately, except for solutions to the Schrödinger-like equation describing anomalous dispersion, no scalar-valued spatiotemporally localized waves with analogous knotted topological structures are known to date. It is the goal in this article to fill in this gap by deriving finite-energy spatiotemporally localized scalar-valued wave solutions characterized specifically by Hopf and trefoil nodal knot topologies. This will extend to spatiotemporally localized pulsed fields the diverse important applications of mono-chromatic light beams, having nontrivial topological structures, in trapping and guiding particles, image processing and optical communications; also, in applications to biology and medicine.
José Angel Alejandro-Soto; Paulo T. Araujo; Ruy Fabila-Monroy; Sergio Gerardo Gómez-Galicia; Mohamed Hibat-Allah; Md Moshiur Rahman Raj; Mahmud Ashraf Shamim; Ana Laura Trujillo-Negrete

Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. We prove that $m(F_k(G))\geq\binom{n-2}{k-1}m(G)$, and that this bound is tight up to a multiplicative factor of $1+O(k/n)$; in the case when $k=c \cdot n$ for some constant $0 < c < 1$, we provide an example where this bound is off by a multiplicative constant factor. We also show bounds for $m(F_k(G))$ for various classes of graphs $G$. Finally, we consider the algorithmic complexity of finding $m(F_k(G))$, showing it to be NP-complete for a constant $k$, and giving evidence that, when the weights take finitely many values, it is not NP-hard for $k\geq n^δ$ for any constant $δ>0$.
Robust BUG dynamical low-rank integrators based on the Euler-Maruyama method for stochastic differential equations. Part I: a closed-moment approach

In this work, we introduce Euler-Maruyama-based Basis-Update & Galerkin (EM-BUG) dynamical low-rank integrators for stochastic differential equations (SDEs). These integrators extend the standard BUG integrator to the Euler-Maruyama scheme by incorporating diffusion directions into the augmented physical basis and exploiting the second moment to update the physical basis independently of the new Brownian increments. This construction avoids the inversion of the reduced second-moment matrix and allows us to derive convergence estimates that are robust with respect to small eigenvalues. We establish preservation of positive semidefiniteness, exactness with respect to Euler-Maruyama at full rank, and second-moment stability. Strong and weak convergence estimates show that the time-discretization accuracy of the underlying Euler-Maruyama scheme is preserved up to the low-rank approximation error. We also derive Monte Carlo error estimates recovering the standard sampling rate up to the time-discretization and low-rank approximation errors. Numerical experiments on linear SDEs with additive and multiplicative noise support these theoretical results and demonstrate accuracy comparable to the standard BUG integrator.
An α-potential linear approximation for LQ differential games
Balint Varga; Gergely Lorant Kiss; Andreas Schwung

Feedback Nash equilibria of infinite-horizon linear-quadratic (LQ) differential games are characterized by coupled algebraic Riccati equations (cAREs), whose numerical solution generally relies on iterative algorithms and can be highly sensitive to their initialization. Motivated by the $α$-potential-game framework, this letter proposes an $α$-potential linear approximation for constructing a systematic, game-dependent initialization. For an N-player LQ game, a reference potential game is constructed. Its equilibrium requires solving only one standard algebraic Riccati equation. The original cAREs are subsequently linearized around this reference solution, yielding a coupled linear system whose solution provides player-specific corrections and hence an approximate feedback Nash equilibrium. The resulting approximation is used to initialize three standard cARE solvers. Numerical experiments on $10^4$ randomly generated two-player games show that the proposed initialization reduces the mean number of iterations. Further experiments for $N=2,\ldots,13$ show that the reduction in iteration count persists as the number of players increases.
A refinement of Szemerédi's distinct-distance bound for points in general position

We prove that every collinear triple free set of $n\ge4$ points in the Euclidean plane determines at least $\lfloor n/3\rfloor+1$ distinct distances. This refines the classical bound $\lceil(n-1)/3\rceil$ of Szemerédi that is based on counting isosceles triangles. The refinement is based on treating the diameters separately: they only appear on the convex hull, so for them, we can use the planar diameter theorem and Altman's theorem on distances in convex polygons.
Accelerating Diffusion Maps on a Quantum Computer: Spectral Filtering and Galerkin PDE Solvers

Diffusion maps generalize principal component analysis (PCA) to nonlinear manifolds, enabling spectral dimensionality reduction, geometric data analysis, and elliptic PDE approximation on point clouds. For large datasets of size $N$, however, classical matrix operations incur prohibitive $\operatorname{poly}(N)$ scaling, even when extracting low-dimensional spectral features or targeted scalar observables. We introduce a quantum algorithmic framework that bypasses explicit graph-Laplacian assembly by exploiting the symmetric factorization $G = A^T A$ directly at the block-encoding level. Combining Gaussian moment dilation, Laplace-weighted linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT), we implement spectral filters of $A$ to estimate heat-semigroup overlaps, regularized inverse queries, and energy responses, as well as to prepare spectral Galerkin solution states. A common-state construction further allows the block-encoding queries to be used across multiple scalar observables. Under polylogarithmic-cost block-encoding access to $A$ and state-preparation oracles, our heat-overlap algorithm achieves $O(\operatorname{polylog} N)$ gate complexity at fixed normalized precision, confidence, and spectral scale. Ideal statevector simulations validate our discrete circuit constructions, while a matched approximate-counting benchmark demonstrates the quadratic precision advantage of coherent amplitude estimation for energy readout.
Detection and Recovery of Core--Periphery Structure in Random Geometric Graphs

Core--periphery (CP) structure, characterized by a dense core of interconnected nodes linked to sparsely connected peripheral nodes, is a prevalent feature of many real-world networks. We propose a core--periphery random geometric graph (CP-RGG) model in which vertices are independently and uniformly distributed on the unit cube \([0,1]^m\), and each vertex is designated as a core node with probability \(p_n\). Two vertices are connected if their Euclidean distance falls below a type-dependent threshold, governed by three distinct radii for core--core, core--periphery, and periphery--periphery pairs. We investigate the information-theoretic limits for both the detection and recovery of the core in the CP-RGG. For detection in the non-degenerate regime, we prove that the total variation distance between the CP-RGG and a null RGG without CP structure converges to one if and only if the expected number of core nodes tends to infinity. For recovery, we demonstrate that almost exact recovery is achievable if and only if the expected degree tends to infinity. Finally, we establish limits for exact recovery. In the one-dimensional sparse regime (\(m=1\)), we obtain a sharp threshold when the core--core and core--periphery radii coincide. For \(m\ge2\), when the core has polynomial size and the core--periphery radius exceeds twice the periphery--periphery radius, we prove that the exact recovery threshold is sharp up to constant factors, scaling on the order of \(\log n\).
New lower bounds for six small hypergraph Ramsey numbers

Let $R(k,l;t)$ denote the least $n$ such that every colouring of the $t$-subsets of an $n$-set with two colours has $k$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the first colour, or $l$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the second. We give explicit colourings proving $R(4,5;3)\ge 38$, $R(4,6;3)\ge 71$, $R(5,5;3)\ge 99$, $R(5,6;4)\ge 201$, $R(6,6;4)\ge 601$ and $R(6,6;5)\ge 84$. The first three improve the bounds 35, 63 and 88 listed in Radziszowski's dynamic survey. The last three improve the listed bounds 67, 133 and 72, and for the two 4-uniform numbers also the values 159 and 317 of a recent data deposit. The colourings of 3-subsets are invariant under groups of affine maps $x\mapsto ax+b$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, for $n=37$, 69 and 97, in the last two cases with one further fixed point. Those of 4-subsets live on the projective line over $\mathbb{F}_q$, for $q=199$ and $q=599$, and are invariant under $\mathrm{PSL}(2,q)$ or $\mathrm{PGL}(2,q)$, so each is given by a table of $q$ entries. For 5-subsets we show that, for every prime $q\ge 5$, invariance under $\mathrm{PGL}(2,q)$ forces six points all of whose 5-subsets have the same colour; our colouring is invariant under all affine maps of $\mathbb{Z}_{83}$. By known constructions the bounds give $R(5,5,5;3)\ge 9605$ and $R_k(5;3)\ge 98^{2^{k-2}}+1$, and $R(6,7;4)\ge 2001$, $R(7,7;4)\ge 12001$ and $R(8,8;4)\ge 588001$. The colourings, and programs that verify them, accompany the paper as ancillary files.
Labeled Chip-Firing on Ordered Directed Graphs
Ryota Inagaki; Tanya Khovanova; Austin Luo

We study labeled chip-firing on rooted directed graphs where for each vertex $v$, the children of $v$ are linearly ordered. When a vertex fires, the selected chips are sent to its children in increasing order. We show that homomorphisms preserving these child choices transport legal firing sequences. We then consider the directed lattice $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$ and ask which chips can reach a given vertex. We give a recurrence for the smallest reachable label when sufficiently many chips are present and show that consecutive pairing attains this minimum. Finally, we determine the largest reachable label by symmetry and prove that the reachable labels form an interval when the number of initial chips is sufficiently large.
The Scaled Dirichlet Distribution: Lauricella Representations and Estimation

We derive explicit expressions for the mixed moments of the scaled Dirichlet distribution in terms of the Lauricella hypergeometric function of type $D$. The relationship with Carlson's multivariate $R$-function is stated, and the convergence conditions required for the series derivation are made explicit. The general expressions yield means, second moments and covariances, with Gauss and Appell hypergeometric representations in the bivariate and trivariate cases. Method-of-moments and maximum-likelihood formulations are presented, together with simulation summaries and an illustrative comparison of scaled Dirichlet and ordinary Dirichlet fits to compositional futures-return data.
A Modified Quasi-Newton Method for Unconstrained Optimization with Nonpositive Curvature Detection and Structured Complexity
Farhad Rahbarnia; Dominique Monnet; Dominique Orban

We consider the convergence, worst-case complexity, and implementation of R2N, a modified quasi-Newton method for large-scale unconstrained smooth optimization. At each iteration, we compute a step that approximately minimizes the sum of a quadratic model of the objective with an adaptive quadratic regularization, and that results in sufficient decrease. The objective is only assumed to be $C^1$, although second derivatives may be used if they are available. The implementation features a broad range of step-computation strategies, from sparse factorization to matrix-free Krylov methods, that satisfy global convergence requirements. When detected, directions of nonpositive curvature are exploited. Our analysis allows unbounded model Hessians, provided they satisfy a mild growth condition. We derive a worst-case evaluation complexity bound that separates the progress made along positive- and nonpositive-curvature directions. By forcing the regularization parameter to vanish near isolated local minimizers, we obtain superlinear local convergence. The implementation specializes naturally to nonlinear least-squares problems. We provide a modular Julia implementation, and use it in a numerical study on the CUTEst test set that assesses the treatment of nonpositive curvature, the subproblem solver, the update of the regularization parameter, and direct versus iterative subproblem solves. An Armijo-Goldstein line search along nonpositive-curvature directions, MINRES-QLP as subproblem solver, and a regularization parameter driven to zero near a solution form our recommended configuration. With exact second derivatives, R2N is competitive with a trust-region method, solving slightly more problems with fewer objective and gradient evaluations. With convex models, the trust-region method performs as well or better.
A Generalized Lefschetz Degree with applications to Fixed Point Theory

We introduce and study a class of spaces, named Lefschetz admissible, where the identity maps on compacts can be approximated by certain maps with values in Lefschetz spaces in a suitable sense. For maps defined on these spaces, we introduce a generalized Lefschetz degree obtained as the set of accumulation points of usual Lefschetz degrees for the approximant maps in a certain compactification. We show that when the degree is nonempty, fixed point results hold. We consider both the situation of spaces embedded in topological vector spaces (TVSs) as global and as neighborhood retracts. As two consequences, we obtain a generalization of a fixed point result due to Browder, and a no-retraction criterion for compact subsets of locally convex TVSs.
Antipodal Parity and Second-Chaos Regge Curvature on Random Hyperplane Arrangements

Limit theorems are proved for the signed Regge curvature of independent oriented hyperplanes in Euclidean space under the piecewise-flat metric induced by unit linear ramps on their positive half-spaces. Provided each hyperplane law is invariant under orientation reversal, the curvature has zero mean and zero first Hoeffding component at every finite sample size. In particular, it is uncorrelated with all square-integrable unoriented functionals. For isotropic Gaussian normals on bounded windows, the rescaled curvature is approximated in mean square by a degenerate U-statistic and converges to a second-chaos series diagonalised on odd spherical harmonics. In the plane, the global cone-angle deficit admits a closed-form limit law universal up to scale under finite fourth moments.
Learning Integer Winding Evolution Times in Quantum Phase Estimation

Learning a Hamiltonian evolution time in Quantum Phase Estimation that produces phase distributions with low Shannon entropy circumvents the fundamental limit of digitization error of phase, independent of the number of phase qubits of accuracy. By introducing an optimization loop to minimize the Shannon entropy of measured eigenvalues produced by a QPE quantum circuit, minimum eigenvalue computation accuracy is greatly improved, which we show numerically on quantum magnet models. This technique works because standard QPE has a natural correspondence between entropy of the phase distribution and the analog accuracy of the minimum eigenvalue phase. This introduces for the first time a type of parameter learning to QPE, which makes near term practicality of QPE for fundamental sciences more feasible by using shorter depth QPE circuits.
Algebraically elliptic resolutions in a family of determinantal quartic threefolds
Alexander Dvorsky; Shulim Kaliman; Mikhail Zaidenberg

We construct a family of determinantal irrational quartic threefolds in $\mathbf{P}^4$ for which the blow-up of the sixteen nodes and two distinguished small projective resolutions are algebraically elliptic in the sense of Gromov.
Rank and Rel in Strata of Abelian Differentials

We prove that every invariant subvariety M in a genus g stratum H(k_1,...,k_n) of Abelian differentials satisfies rank(M) <= rel(M) + 1 + sum_i (k_i - 1). In particular, every invariant subvariety with rel zero in a principal stratum is a Teichmüller curve. Combined with work of Eskin, Filip and Wright, this implies that each principal stratum contains only finitely many nonarithmetic Teichmüller curves. If rank(M) < g, we also show that rank(M) + rel(M) <= g - 1 + n/2.
A Computational and Experimental Framework for Fourier Optics in Python

Simulation of the propagation of light is useful for the design and dimensioning of optical systems. In this paper, we present the basics of propagation simulation using Fourier optics and practical implementation in Python, with a particular emphasis on dimensions. We first verify that our numerical wave-optics simulations maintain correct physical spatial scaling. Next, we benchmark numerical propagation against closed-form analytical formulas for Gaussian beams, lens focusing effects, and grating diffraction. We then show how those simulations can be used to generate diffractive optical elements such as Fresnel zone plates, and we bridge the gap between numerical simulations and experiments by collecting data and recovering phase information using a phase retrieval algorithm.
A Density Bound for Muñiz's List Reversal

Muñiz described the problem of reversing a list of positive integers under the following rules: given a list of distinct positive integers, at each step, one can combine two adjacent entries into their sum or break an entry into two entries with the same sum, under the constraints that after each step the list must contain distinct entries no larger than the original largest entry. The question of what lists are and are not reversible under these rules is studied and an asymptotic upper bound on the density of an irreversible list is established.
Compact Slack-Free Penalty Functions for Inequality Constraints in Higher-Order Unconstrained Binary Optimization

Inequality constraints in higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) are commonly handled using slack variables or by enumerating infeasible assignments, which respectively enlarge the search space or produce penalties whose size grows with the number of forbidden values. We construct exact slack-free penalty functions for upper- and lower-bound constraints on binary-encoded integers. Each function is constructed hierarchically from the threshold bits through a recursive addition-and-multiplication rule, and its correctness for arbitrary bit widths and representable thresholds is proved by mathematical induction. Equivalent explicit finite sum-product representations are also derived, enabling direct analysis of product-term count and polynomial degree. Interval constraints are obtained by adding the lower- and upper-bound penalties, while exclusion constraints are obtained by multiplying them. Compared with the trivial enumerative construction, the proposed method reduces the worst-case product-term count from linear to logarithmic in the representable range. Except at one non-vacuous boundary threshold for each bound, it also reduces both product-term count and degree. The resulting single-bound penalties have minimum positive value 1 and maximum value at most the bit width, which may simplify penalty-weight selection. The same construction also extends exactly to fixed-scale fractional variables through appropriate scaling of the integer thresholds.
Gabe Cunningham; Claudio Alexandre Piedade; Philippe Tranchida

A hypertope is a thin, residually connected incidence geometry. For each pair of types $\{i,j\}$, the residues of that type must be polygons, and if all residues of that type are the same type of polygon, then we can record this information in a diagram $D$. Given such a diagram, we prove a lower bound on the number of chambers of a hypertope with that diagram. A hypertope that achieves this bound is called \emph{tight}. We prove that a hypertope is tight if and only if its diagram $D$ is a forest and, for every pair of types $\{i,j\}$ that is not an edge of $D$, every $i$-element is incident to every $j$-element. This generalizes a previously known result about abstract polytopes. Finally, we describe a combinatorial method and an algebraic method for constructing tight hypertopes.
Structure and Complexity of Perfect Functional Representations
Serhat Emre Coban; Yanina Y. Shkel; Emre Telatar

For given random variables $(X,Y)$, functional representation lemma states that there exists a random variable $Z$ and a deterministic function $g$ such that $Y = g(X,Z)$, and $X$ is independent of $Z$. In other words, $Z$ captures all the information about $Y$ not contained in $X$. We refer to $Z$ as a `perfect functional representation' if it satisfies $I(Y;Z) = H(Y|X)$. We show that the existence of perfect representation depends solely on the conditional distribution $p_{Y|X}$ and define the corresponding conditional distributions as perfectly representable. We provide a necessary and sufficient condition for $p_{Y|X}$ to be perfectly representable. Moreover, we cast the problem of checking perfect representability as a linear program, give an algorithm whose complexity is polynomial in $|\mathcal Y|$ and exponential in $|\mathcal X|$, and prove that deciding perfect representability is NP-complete for rational input matrices encoded in binary.
When Is an OIRI-Algebra a Banach Lattice? Structure Theorems and Counterexamples

This paper investigates the exact conditions under which a relatively uniformly complete semiprime $f$-algebra whose order ideals are ring ideals (an OIRI-algebra) admits a norm turning it into a Banach lattice or an AM-space. While recent literature claimed that this equivalence holds automatically in the presence of a weak order unit, we construct a concrete counterexample within a relatively uniformly complete vector lattice showing that this assertion fails in general. By analyzing the canonical embedding $ψ:A\rightarrow Orth(A)$, we prove that the equivalence between being an OIRI-algebra, admitting an AM-space or Banach lattice norm and satisfying $Orth(A)=$ $Stab(A)$ $=Z(A$) holds under the assumption that $ψ\left( A\right) $ is relatively uniformly closed in $Orth(A)$ (alongside a characterization via finite elements in the unitization $A^{\sharp}$). We also deduce immediate consequences for unital $f$-algebras and generalize our main theorem to non-semiprime $f$-algebras via the quotient modulo the nilpotent radical $N(A)$.
The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
Pablo Araya; Luis Fredes; Avelio Sepúlveda

We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that, under mild regularity assumptions, the rerooting-invariant families of laws satisfying this Markov property are exactly the Boltzmann decorated metric maps. We also prove a strong Markov property and show that the random submaps inducing a Markovian decomposition are exactly the stopping maps for a suitable filtration. Finally, we obtain analogous results for classical decorated planar maps.
On Hölder Equicontinuity of the Integrated Density of States for Random Schrödinger Operators on $\mathbb{Z}^d$

We study a random Schrödinger operator $H_λ= H_0 + λV$ on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ consisting of a translation invariant hopping matrix $H_0$ and a random potential $V$, given by independently distributed single site potentials with absolutely continuous distributions. Assuming a regularity assumption for the hopping matrix $H_0$, we show Hölder continuity of the integrated density of states of $H_λ$ up to exponents $2/3$, independently of the disorder strength $λ$.
The Partial Trace Functor on Soergel Bimodules in Type $\mathbb{B}$

We write down some observations about the partial trace functor between the categories of Soergel bimodules of type $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$ and $\mathbb{B}_n$ for future reference. In particular, we observe that, like in type $\mathbb{A}$, the partial trace sends Soergel bimodules to a semi-infinite $q$-graded sum of Soergel bimodules.
Globally $F$-regular varieties are rationally chain connected
Eric Jovinelly; Brian Lehmann; Eric Riedl

We prove that projective globally $F$-regular varieties are rationally chain connected. We deduce this from a study of the positivity of their tangent bundles and their purely inseparable covers. Although some globally $F$-regular varieties admit non-vanishing pluridifferential forms, we show that each admits a unique purely inseparable crepant cover that does not have this pathology. These covers carry very free curves, which can be degenerated to chains of rational curves through general pairs of points.
Certified Discovery of Quantum Phase Diagrams
Yuanxi Liu; John Preskill; Hsin-Yuan Huang

Can a machine provably discover new quantum phases of matter? We show that the answer is yes under physically motivated assumptions. For any smooth family of geometrically local Hamiltonians, we construct an efficient quantum algorithm that outputs the phase diagram to prescribed accuracy and provides a verifiable certificate for every transition it reports. The algorithm takes as input only a classical description of the family together with unverified preparations of reference ground states; no order parameter, symmetry-breaking pattern, or training data are supplied. It succeeds provided that at least one preparation is correct in each gapped region of parameter space. The algorithm explores parameter space by quasi-adiabatically or adiabatically transporting each reference state, detecting the approach of a phase boundary by tapping the transported state with a frequency-filtered local probe: excitations created by the probe witness the closing of the energy gap. We prove that the gap closing for continuous phase transitions can always be detected using the frequency-filtered gradient of the Hamiltonian. The gap-detecting measurement is gentle, so when the ground state is unique a single reusable copy of each reference ground state supports the full exploration (for degenerate ground states, polynomially many copies suffice). The quantum algorithm runs in polynomial time at inverse-polynomial gap resolution. We also give a classical algorithm that runs in quasipolynomial time at constant gap resolution. Numerical experiments demonstrate how our algorithm accurately determines the phase structure of several model quantum systems.
Functional Estimation under Local Differential Privacy: General Lower Bounds and Applications to Entropy and Power Sums

We study the estimation of functionals of discrete distributions under local differential privacy (LDP). Even for well-studied examples like Shannon entropy and power sums, the existing bounds left open how the minimax risk scales with the alphabet size, the sample size, and the privacy parameter. To understand these dependences, we establish two general minimax lower bounds for the broader class of additive functionals. The first lower bound links the difficulty of estimating a functional to how well it can be approximated by polynomials of a given degree. The second complements the first by capturing how sensitive the functional is to small changes in the underlying distribution. To illustrate the effectiveness of these two bounds, we apply them to the estimation of Shannon entropy and power sums. In both cases, they close the existing polynomial gaps and, perhaps surprisingly, show that simple plug-in type estimators already achieve the optimal polynomial rates.

In this work, we are interested in the decomposition of trilinear forms. We associate this decomposition with the decomposition into irreducible subspaces of the group algebra associated with the symmetric group. We have a correspondence between a ternary form and a symmetric trilinear form, in the same way that we have the correspondence between a quadratic form and a symmetric quadratic form. We are then interested in the decomposition of ternary forms into a sum of cubes of linear forms and as an application we find the Tartaglia formulae on the expression of the roots of equations of degree 3.
Monomial singularities of maps in low codimension and their deformations
R. Giménez Conejero; M. E. Rodrigues Hernandes

We study complex analytic map germs whose coordinate functions are monomials up to a change of coordinates. Motivated by recent normal form results of Rodrigues Hernandes and Ruas for $\mathcal{A}$-finite monomial maps in the range $p\ge 2n$, we address the remaining gap $p<2n$, solving an open problem posed in their work in the range $n<p<2n$. Our main results show that a monomial map germ $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^p,0)$ with $p < 2n$ and $(n,p) \neq (1,1)$ is $\mathcal{A}$-finite if and only if it is $\mathcal{A}$-equivalent to an $\mathcal{A}$-stable germ. For $n = p = 1$ we also obtain the family of simple singularities of type $A_k$. Finally, we construct new families of $\mathcal{A}$-finite (generally non-monomial) map germs starting from monomial ones.
On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem for $\mathbb Z_n^3$

The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)$ is the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $\mathbb Z_n^r$ contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero. In this paper, we prove that $$\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^3)=9n+o(n)$$ for odd $n$. For every fixed $r\ge 4$, we also show that $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)\le\bigl(\binom{2r-1}{r}+1\bigr)n+o_r(n).$ Our approach combines Alon--Dubiner-type spectral expansion, Zakharov's convex-geometric framework, and restricted-sum ideas developed by Han and Ren.

We give a census of the roughly 10 billion prime, connected, alternating tangles with at most 14 crossings. Along the way, we prove analogs of the Tait conjectures for alternating tangles and observe that aspects of the geometry of alternating tangles are reflected in their diagrams, as is the case with links.
