For example, in the 1960s, Bondareva used linear duality to characterize when the core of a game with transferable utility is nonempty. Scarf later established a core existence theorem for balanced games with non-transferable utility. Shapley derived this result from his KKMS covering theorem, demonstrating how topological covering theorems yield core existence results. In this note we give a new KKM-type covering proof of linear duality. We then extend the argument to inequalities with continuous perturbations. Under some asymptotic growth assumptions on perturbations, we obtain a feasible point and balancing coefficients satisfying complementary slackness, a Lagrangian lower bound, and a Scarf-type feasibility criterion. The latter yields Scarf's theorem for normalized cooperative games with non-transferable utility. Using Musin's 2017 KKM-type theorems with boundary conditions and the author's 2026 results on cover degrees relative to point configurations, we also obtain a complementary slackness theorem for continuous functions on compact connected oriented manifolds with nonempty boundary.
Rigidity for the quadratic Riemann curvature functional in dimensions greater than four

We investigate rigidity properties of critical metrics for the quadratic Riemann curvature functional on Riemannian manifolds of dimension greater than four. This functional is the integral of the squared norm of the Riemann curvature tensor. On noncompact manifolds, criticality is understood with respect to compactly supported variations, without assuming finite total curvature energy. We prove that every complete noncompact critical metric with finite curvature energy is either flat or has strictly negative scalar curvature everywhere. We further show that every complete critical metric with concircular scalar curvature is flat. Here concircularity means that the Hessian of the scalar curvature is pointwise proportional to the metric. Consequently, every complete weakly Einstein critical metric with divergence-free Cotton tensor is flat. The latter two flatness results require neither noncompactness nor finite curvature energy. Finally, we construct a complete nonflat critical metric in dimension five with vanishing Cotton tensor, showing that the concircularity and weakly Einstein assumptions are essential in the respective flatness results.
Rough vector fields with vanishing Lie brackets

We consider two vector fields $X, Y \in W^{1,p}_{loc}(\mathbb R^d) \cap \mathbf L^\infty$ with bounded divergence. If $p \geq 2$, this paper shows that $DX \,Y - DY \, X = 0$ almost everywhere if and only if their Regular Lagrangian Flows commute. If instead $1 \leq p < 2$, we present an example of two divergence free locally Sobolev vector fields in $\mathbb R^2$ with vanishing Lie brackets whose flows do not commute. In the regime $2 \leq p < \infty$ this paper also yields a quantitative commutation result not depending on the Lipschitz constant for vector fields with $[X, Y] \neq 0$, which is new even in the smooth setting.
Target-Clamped Contrastive Learning in Nonlinear Resistive Networks with Monotone Elements
Henk J. van Waarde; Benjamin Scellier; Encho T. Nguyen

In the pursuit of energy-efficient hardware for machine learning, nonlinear resistive networks trained via local learning rules are emerging as promising alternatives to digital neural networks. Learning in these physical systems is often achieved with Equilibrium Propagation (EP), which compares a "free" state to a "nudged" target-driven state to perform gradient descent on an objective defined by an explicit cost function. In contrast, Target-Clamped Contrastive Learning (TCCL) "clamps" output nodes directly to exact target values, performing gradient descent on an implicit contrastive function - an objective whose properties have long remained unknown. Focusing on nonlinear networks composed of resistors with monotonically increasing current-voltage characteristics (such as Ohmic resistors and diodes), our contribution is twofold. First, we establish rigorous convergence guarantees for TCCL. We prove that the contrastive function is convex for nonlinear resistive networks without hidden nodes, and demonstrate that this property does not hold in general for the objective function optimized by EP. For these networks, TCCL converges to a global minimum of the contrastive function under suitable assumptions on the learning rate. In the presence of hidden nodes, the contrastive function is not convex, but we show that TCCL still converges to a stationary point on a subsequence. We also reveal cases where such stationary points are global minimizers of the contrastive function. Second, we characterize the representational capacity of these circuits. We establish a novel function approximation theorem demonstrating that any continuous, monotonically non-decreasing, and shift-equivariant function can be approximated to arbitrary precision, proving that these properties are the sole limitations on the network's computational expressivity.
44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer as orbits under the group of interval shifts
Helga Boyer von Berghof; Daniel C. Mayer

We generate a splitting of the 924 monotonically ascending twelve tone half series H=(H_1,..,H_6) in [0,..,11]^6 in 80 orbits H^G under the additive cyclic group G=Z/12Z of transpositions (interval shifts). By classification according to cardinality and forming the union of the orbits H^G and K^G of a half series H and its complement K, we obtain exactly the 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer, completely independent of symmetry properties, however, fundamentally due to so-called wider-gleiche orbits. This was not clear in previous literature.
Cyclic Self-Dual Codes over Prime-Square Rings and Unimodular Lattices
Minjia Shi; Mengru Yang; Patrick Solé

We present an explicit construction of cyclic Euclidean self-dual codes over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{2}\mathbb{Z}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, and use Construction~A to obtain unimodular lattices with large minimum norms. The construction is based on reciprocal factorizations of $x^n-1$. We explicitly describe the associated residue and torsion codes and analyze the relationship between minimum Euclidean weights and lattice minimum norms. We construct a unimodular lattice of minimum norm~$4$ in dimension~$49$, unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$5$ in dimensions $53$, $55$, $58$, $59$, and~$61$, and extremal unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$6$ in dimensions $69$ and~$71$. Using shadow theory and harmonic theta series, we prove that extremal unimodular lattices do not exist in dimensions $59$ and~$61$. Together with the known upper bounds, these results establish the optimality of the constructed lattices in all eight dimensions. In particular, we determine the previously unknown optimal minimum norms of unimodular lattices in five dimensions: $53$, $55$, $61$, $69$, and~$71$. We further construct unimodular lattices whose minimum norms are exactly one below the corresponding extremal bounds in dimensions $62$, $63$, $65$, $67$, $70$, $89$, $91$, $92$, $93$, and~$94$.
Nearly Tight Almost Sure Convergence Rates for the Last iterate of SGD
Weiming Ou; Andrea Paudice; Xiao Wang

We study the almost sure convergence of the last-iterate optimization error of Stochastic (sub)Gradient Descent (SGD) for convex objectives. For smooth objectives, we establish convergence rates of order $k^{-1/3}$ when a stationary minimizer exists, and $k^{-1/4}$ otherwise, up to polylogarithmic factors, where $k$ denotes the iteration counter. We further show that the latter rate extends to nonsmooth convex objectives. All these rates are achieved by deterministic, anytime stepsize policies. Finally, we establish matching lower bounds showing that the exponents $-1/3$ and $-1/4$ are optimal, up to polylogarithmic factors, for the corresponding problem classes.
Wenhua Qian; Yuze Ren; Wenming Wu

We study surjective $L^p$-isometries on spaces of bounded idempotents in an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. On each fixed positive finite-rank stratum, every surjective $L^p$-isometry, $1\leq p<\infty$, is implemented by a unitary or antiunitary operator, possibly composed with adjunction; no separability is required. The same conclusion holds for the operator norm, viewed as the $L^\infty$-norm. On a separable space, operator-norm isometries of the infinite-rank, infinite-corank sector admit the additional complement operation, as do surjective $L^p$-isometries between individual $L^p$-perturbation classes for $1\leq p<\infty$. For the extended $L^p$-metric on all idempotents, implementations may be chosen independently on finite-distance classes, subject to an explicit compatibility condition for matching infinite-rank classes. The proofs use similarity coordinates and metric blow-ups, followed by tangent-space splittings, nearest projections at the $L^1$ endpoint, or sharp Fredholm-index distance estimates. We also establish uniqueness of standard implementations and use essential-spectral invariants to obtain continuum many perturbation-class isometry types.
Canonical weight-two algebras and strongly generated vertex operator superalgebras

This paper studies vertex operator superalgebras strongly generated by their weight-1, weight-$\frac{3}{2}$ and weight-2 homogeneous subspaces. The presence of a nontrivial weight-1 subspace introduces derivative and quadratic current terms in weight-2. To address this, we use low-weight quasi-primary projections to identify two canonical commutative associative algebras, $\mathcal{A}$ and $A$, within the weight-2 subspace. We demonstrate that the algebraic structures of the generating subspaces are encoded by a quadruple that generalizes Lie--Rinehart algebras and their weak representations. This quadruple yields necessary and sufficient compatibility conditions for constructing an associated Lie superalgebra $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{g},A,U)$. Based on this, we construct a family of universal vertex operator superalgebras $V_{\mathcal{L}}(\ell,0)$ and establish a reconstruction theorem for their simple quotients under certain conditions. If $A$ is finite-dimensional, we prove that its orthogonal idempotent decomposition into local Artinian summands naturally induces a tensor product isomorphism of the corresponding vertex operator superalgebras. In addition, our general construction encompasses many vertex operator superalgebras, such as superconformal algebras and generalized $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ (super)algebras.
Large Deviations and Convexity Transition for the Multidimensional Elephant Random Walk

In this article we establish a weak large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the elephant random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, for every reinforcement parameter $p \in (0,1)$. We identify a qualitative change in the behaviour of the associated rate function between dimension $d=1$ and dimensions $d \geq 2$. In dimension $d=1$, the rate function coincides with the Donsker--Varadhan rate function of the simple symmetric random walk and is independent of the reinforcement parameter $p$. By contrast, in every dimension $d\geq 2$, the rate function differs from that of the simple random walk as soon as $p\neq 1/(2d)$. Finally, we prove that for all $d \geq 2$ the rate function is convex if and only if $p \leq 1/(2d)$. This allows us to identify a critical point in the large-deviation behaviour of the model which occurs strictly before the standard diffusive-to-superdiffusive crossover.
Non-bipartite spectral extremal graphs forbidding a three-chromatic color-critical graph
Bo Dong; Cunxiang Duan; Attila Sali; Ligong Wang

A graph is color-critical if it contains at least one color-critical edge. For every fixed three-chromatic color-critical graph $H$, we determine the maximum spectral radius of an $n$-vertex non-bipartite $H$-free graph and characterize the unique extremal graph for all sufficiently large $n$. The extremal graph belongs to one of three graph families: $J_n(s,t)$, $\mathrm{ST}_2(n-1)$ or $L_n(s,t)$. Explicit conditions on $H$ determine the family and its exact parameters. This paper generalizes the results for books and theta graphs to all three-chromatic color-critical graphs. Furthermore, an three-chromatic example demonstrates that spectral extremal graphs are not necessarily edge-extremal, disproving a conjecture of Fang and Lin [J. Algebraic Combin., 2026].
Central limit theorem for linear eigenvalue statistics of random spatial networks
Christian Hirsch; Kyeongsik Nam; Moritz Otto; Anne Marie Svane

The random connection model provides a flexible framework for spatial networks in which connectivity is determined by both geometry and randomness. Its vertices form a Poisson point process, and pairs are connected independently, conditional on their positions, with distance-dependent probabilities. This generalizes the hard distance threshold of random geometric graphs and accommodates long-range connections. We also consider a weighted extension in which each vertex carries a positive random weight that influences its probability of connecting to other vertices. This combination of spatial structure and heterogeneous connectivity raises the question of whether spectral fluctuations exhibit Gaussian behavior on large scales. We address this question by studying linear eigenvalue statistics $\operatorname{Tr}[f(A_n)]$ of the adjacency matrix $A_n$ of the random connection model in expanding windows $W_n$. For polynomial test functions, we establish a finite limit for the normalized variance and prove a central limit theorem under suitable connection-profile integrability and vertex mark moment assumptions. When the limiting variance is positive, the normalized statistics admit an $O(|W_n|^{-1/2})$ normal-approximation bound in both Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distance. Furthermore, under an exponential moment assumption on the vertex marks, we extend the central limit theorem to a general class of test functions $f$.
A Godunov-type in-cell discontinuous reconstruction shock-capturing method for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
Christophe Berthon; Marie Compain; Carlos Par{é}s; Ernesto Pimentel-Garc{í}a

The present paper is devoted to show the correct convergence of a numerical method based on Godunov and the in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic but never recasts in a conservation form. With ambiguous nonconservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. In a previous work the authors determine the simple waves of the nonconservative system studied here and they are able to construct the solutions of the Riemann problem of interest. These solutions are used to obtain a Godunov-type scheme and it is combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique to obtain the correct convergence to the exact solution even in the presence of shocks.
Second-Order Steady-State Approximation of Heterogeneous Mean-Field Models

Mean-field models provide tractable approximations for large stochastic systems, but second-order steady-state results are largely limited to homogeneous or fixed-dimensional population processes. This paper develops a second-order steady-state approximation for fully heterogeneous mean-field models. Conditioning on the realized agent parameters, we study fixed-dimensional weighted occupancies even though the dimension of the full heterogeneous mean-field system grows linearly with the number of agents $M$. We first establish an $O(M^{-1})$ bound on the mean-field approximation error for stationary expectations of twice continuously differentiable functions of these occupancies. We then characterize the leading term in this error in terms of the stationary mean bias and covariance of the weighted occupancies. A Lyapunov equation for the linearized dynamics yields an approximation to the stationary covariance of the unscaled weighted occupancy with error $O(M^{-3/2})$. Its solution, together with the drift derivatives at equilibrium, also gives an explicit $1/M$ correction to the mean-field prediction of the stationary mean. The corrected mean has error $o(M^{-1})$, which improves to $O(M^{-3/2})$ under a stronger bound on the drift remainder. The resulting covariance and mean-refinement equations have the same structure as the finite-time heterogeneous refined mean-field equations, but our results directly provide steady-state guarantees for weighted occupancies rather than marginal state probabilities of individual agents. The results are illustrated through a heterogeneous power-of-two load-balancing model with buffer size two.
Sharp boundary regularity for planar minimal graphs with analytic Dirichlet data
Camillo De Lellis; Guido De Philippis; Alessio Figalli

We study the boundary behavior of generalized (BV) solutions of the Dirichlet problem for the minimal surface equation over a bounded set \(Ω\). Such a generalized solution is always the graph of a smooth function \(v\) inside \(Ω\), but might carry a vertical part over \(\partialΩ\), which records the gap between the prescribed Dirichlet datum \(g\) and the boundary trace \(h\) attained by \(v\). When \(Ω\) is a bounded real-analytic planar domain and \(g\) is real analytic we prove that \(h\) is Lipschitz, right and left differentiable at every point, of class \(C^1\) on \(\partialΩ\setminusΣ\), and real analytic on \(\{h\neq g\}\setminusΣ\), where \(Σ=\{κ=0\}\) is the zero set of the curvature of \(\partialΩ\). Also, at each point \(p\inΣ\cap\{h\neq g\}\), the two one-sided branches extend real analytically across \(p\). The proof recasts the vertical part near a contact point as a scalar obstacle problem with a possibly degenerate right-hand side, whose model case is \(Δv=H\,\id_{\{v>0\}}\) with \(H\ge0\) a polynomial. These results are optimal: for merely smooth data the trace may be discontinuous, while in the real-analytic case there are examples where corners do occur.
The inverse Littlewood problem for multiplicative functions

We formulate and solve the asymptotic inverse Littlewood problem in the class of multiplicative functions. That is, let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{U}\cup\{0\}$ be a bounded completely multiplicative function satisfying $\sum_{p:f(p)=0}1/p<\infty$. We show that \[ \int_0^1 \left|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)e(αn)\right|\,dα\ll\log x \] for all $x\ge3$ if and only if $f(n)=χ(n)n^{it}$ for some Dirichlet character $χ$ and some $t\in\mathbb{R}$.\\ More generally, we show that there is $\varepsilon_0>0$, depending only on the $\ell^2$-density of $f$ (that is, on $\prod_{p:f(p)=0}(1-1/p)$), such that under the weaker hypothesis \[ \int_0^1 \left|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)e(αn)\right|\,dα \ll x^{\varepsilon_0} \] for all $x\ge3$, there are a Dirichlet character $χ$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that \[ \sum_p\frac{\left|f(p)-χ(p)p^{it}\right|}{p}<\infty. \] We give evidence for the sharpness of such classification, by constructing non-pretentious examples with $L^1$ norm $o(\sqrt{x})$ at every sufficiently large scale, but with ``wild" behavior at the intermediate scales.
AG-BFGS: Foundations for Accelerated Geometry Learning
Regina Carla Sousa; Denis Vargas; Elizabeth Wanner; Joshua Knowles

We introduce an accelerated geometry-learning framework for BFGS that incorporates momentum into the learning of Hessian inverse approximations. We prove that the resulting accelerated updates satisfy explicit stability conditions and preserve positive definiteness within admissible parameter regions. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding non-accelerated schemes while maintaining numerical stability. These results provide the first rigorous theoretical foundation for accelerated quasi-Newton learning and bridge the gap between empirical observations and mathematical guarantees for accelerated second-order methods.
A Euclidean Quasi-Newton Method for Matrix-Manifold Optimization via Almost-Global Coordinates
Ziang Tian; Jiang Hu; Zhigang Yao; Bingjie Li

We study smooth matrix-manifold optimization using objective values and first derivatives. Almost-global coordinates transform the manifold-constrained problem into an unconstrained pullback problem, to which we apply BFGS with a chart-restart strategy and a limited-memory implementation. We establish correspondence of first- and second-order stationary points and minimizers, together with conditional convergence and local q-superlinear convergence. The local rate follows from Euclidean full-memory BFGS theory once the chart is fixed, without the locking condition required by classical transported-gradient Riemannian BFGS analyses. Tests on 15 benchmark problems from Manopt and Pymanopt, with ten instances per problem, show that our limited-memory method solves all 150 cases, whereas Riemannian BFGS and Riemannian steepest descent solve 132 and 117 cases, respectively. On the 115 cases successfully solved by all three methods, our method takes roughly half the time of either baseline, measured by geometric-mean solve time.
A Characterization of Rings Where a Linear Transformation and Its Inverse and Transpose Have the Same Information Exchange

Linear transformations are considered over finite commutative rings. It is shown that the information exchange of an invertible linear transformation and that of its inverse are equal for any ring. It is also shown that the information exchange of any linear transformation and that of its transpose are equal if and only if the ring is Frobenius. Applications are presented to the Discrete Fourier Transform, to the analysis of Vandermonde transformations, and to area-time complexity.
Coupled flows in $G_2$ geometry: preservation, existence and stability

We study coupled flows on compact manifolds with $G_2$ structures that preserve coassociative submanifolds and $G_2$ instantons as the ambient $G_2$ structure evolves. For coassociatives, we give an explicit example on a torus showing that the Laplacian flow of closed $G_2$ structures coupled to mean curvature flow can fail to preserve coassociativity, even arbitrarily close to a flat structure. We circumvent this by adding a Lie derivative to the ambient equation, using an elliptic correction of minimum $L^2$ norm along the submanifold. We prove short-time existence and uniqueness of the corrected coupled flow from coassociative initial data, without any rigidity assumption. We also prove global existence and smooth exponential convergence for coassociative initial pairs sufficiently close to a torsion-free coassociative pair, with the ambient cohomology class fixed. For instantons, we propose a similar corrected coupled system by adding a torsion term and a nonlocal elliptic correction to Yang-Mills flow along prescribed coclosed ambient $4$-forms. We prove short-time existence and uniqueness of the corrected coupled system for connections nearby an acyclic $G_2$ instanton. We obtain global existence and smooth exponential convergence for the coupled corrected connection flow and the modified coflow of coclosed $G_2$ structures with parameter zero, near a torsion-free structure with an acyclic instanton. We prove a new result on the global existence and smooth exponential convergence near a torsion-free $4$-form in a fixed cohomology class for the modified coflow with $c=0$ which is a result of independent interest. We also give continuation criteria for both the coupled systems and construct compact examples with nonzero correction. Finally, for every positive coflow parameter, we exhibit a flat torus with a growing linear mode which shows why $c=0$ is the meaningful one.
Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.
Construction of Ternary Minimal Linear Codes with Dimension $n+r$ Via Index Codes and The Access Structures of Their Dual Codes

Recently, minimal linear codes have been extensively studied due to their applications in secret sharing schemes, secure two-party computations, and so on. Constructing minimal linear codes violating the Ashikhmin-Barg condition and then determining their weight distributions have been interesting in coding theory and cryptography. In this paper, we present a general construction of ternary linear codes of dimension $n+r$, where $n$ and $r$ are positive integers, and derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the resulting codes to be minimal. We first specialize the construction using index codes arising from spreads, with three classes of index codes satisfying the minimality condition, we obtain the parameters and weight enumerators of the corresponding minimal codes, and determine the access structures type of the secret-sharing schemes based on their dual codes. By the index codes from Krawtchouk polynomials, we then give a second specialization of the construction, with a class of index codes satisfying the minimality condition, we obtain the parameters of the resulting minimal codes, and determine the access-structure type of the secret-sharing scheme based on each dual code. Several constructed families of minimal codes violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

We prove that for $n\ge2$ the normalized surface measure is the only rotation-invariant finitely additive probability measure on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb S^n$, and that for $d\ge3$ Lebesgue measure is the only finitely additive measure on the bounded Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ which is invariant under orientation-preserving isometries and normalized on the unit cube. This answers the Borel version of the Ruziewicz problem. On $\mathbb S^n$ it suffices to assume invariance under a finite set of rotations with a spectral gap, and on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under two such sets of rotations about two distinct centres. The main step is a criterion for invariant finitely additive probability measures to vanish on null sets. For a finite nonempty symmetric set of homeomorphisms of a $σ$-compact metrizable space with a quasi-invariant Borel measure $m$ which is finite on compact sets, such as Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$, every invariant finitely additive probability measure on Borel sets vanishes on $m$-null sets if and only if there is $δ>0$ such that every countably additive Borel probability measure supported on an $m$-null Borel set is moved by some generator by at least $δ$ in total variation. Sufficiency is proved by constructing, for every invariant null Borel set, a bounded Borel field on the orbit graph, supported on the set and with divergence at least one there.
Long lived QNM for multiple black holes

We provide a rigorous definition of quasinormal modes (QNM) for the Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetimes with multiple extremal black holes. For certain configurations, the trapped set of the null geodesic flow contains stable (elliptic) orbits. We analyze this phenomenon in the case of two black holes of equal mass and show that it produces QNM converging exponentially fast to the real axis. QNM for black holes have been extensively studied for $\textit{single}$ black holes and this appears to be the first $\textit{mathematical}$ result for the case of multiple black holes.
Action-Dependent Policies for Multi-Agent Linear Quadratic Regulation
Yongjie Liu; Gangshan Jing; Long Wang

The linear quadratic regulation (LQR) problem over a multi-agent system usually requires a distributed feedback gain that is structurally constrained by the network topology, incurring an inevitable suboptimality gap. Existing studies either identify conditions on the system and topology that enable convex relaxation or seek a stationary point via policy gradient algorithms. In this paper, we reduce the suboptimality gap by adopting action-dependent policies (ADPs), where the control input of each agent depends on not only states of neighbor agents, but also control inputs of some other agents. We show that although exhibiting a distributed structure, ADP can enlarge the feasible set of feedback gains and even represent centralized optimal policies under suitable conditions. However, this comes at the price of losing coercivity of the cost function and possible failure of convergence for the projected gradient flow (PGF). To overcome this difficulty, we propose a partially regularized formulation, which guarantees convergence of PGFs, and forges a connection between standard multi-agent LQR and its action-dependent counterpart. Sufficient conditions for local convergence to globally optimal policies under PGFs regardless of regularization are also established. Finally, numerical examples are presented to validate the performance of ADP.
On p-adic asymptotic formulas for slope factors of L-functions of toric exponential sums

Adolphson and Sperber expressed the unique unit root of the $L$-function of a toric exponential sum in terms of $A$-hypergeometric functions, whereas reciprocal zeros and poles of positive slope remain much less understood.We study complete rational factors of arbitrary prescribed slope in families satisfying a chain-level ordinary condition. Our main tool is a new contraction map arising from a twisted block LU factorization of the Frobenius matrix of a nuclear $σ$-module. Its fixed point produces an upper triangularization and the associated slope filtration, while explicit Schur-complement quotients of finite Frobenius iterates approximate the diagonal slope blocks with geometrically decreasing error. At a periodic fiber, successive cancellation in an ordered product of these approximations yields a quotient formed from two finite Frobenius iterates, and the characteristic polynomial of this quotient converges to the complete slope polynomial. Combined with the relative Dwork trace formula, this yields uniform $p$-adic asymptotic formulas for the complete slope factors of the $L$-functions of toric exponential sums. When the relevant slope blocks have rank one, the Schur complements reduce to ratios of leading principal minors and give asymptotic formulas for the individual reciprocal zeros and poles after cancellation.
Turán number of the odd-ballooning of odd prisms
Wenwen Chen; Longfei Fang; Yuke Zhang

The Turán problem for odd-balloonings has been studied for various classes of skeleton graphs, including stars, paths, cycles, trees, bipartite graphs, and certain 3-chromatic graphs. The Turán numbers and extremal graphs for odd prisms have also been determined. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the Turán problem for prescribed odd-balloonings of odd prisms. Let $k\geq1$ be fixed, and let $F^o$ be a prescribed odd-ballooning of the odd prism $C_{2k+1}\square K_2$, in which each edge is replaced by a cycle of prescribed odd length at least five. For all sufficiently large $n$, we prove that $${\rm ex}(n,F^o)=\Big\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\Big\rfloor+(k+1)n-3(k+1)^2.$$ Furthermore, the unique extremal graph is $K_{\,2k+2,\,\lfloor(n-2k-2)/2\rfloor,\,\lceil(n-2k-2)/2\rceil}$. The proof combines the decomposition-family method and Simonovits' structural theorem with local embedding arguments to establish the extremal structure and its uniqueness.
Optimal local gradient estimate for gravity water waves and its application to the Stokes conjecture
Lili Du; Chunlei Yang; Fan Zhang

In 1880, G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol. I] studied a two-dimensional gravity water wave and conjectured that the wave crest forms a symmetric corner of angle 2pi/3 at the stagnation point. The conjecture was first proved by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. Their proofs rely on structural assumptions, including the isolation of stagnation points and the symmetry and monotonicity of the wave profile. In 2011, Varvaruca and Weiss [Acta Math. 206 (2011)] introduced a novel geometric approach and gave a new proof of the conjecture without relying on the structural assumptions mentioned above, under a local gradient bound for the two-dimensional stream function. In this paper, we establish an optimal local gradient estimate for general variational solutions of the free boundary problem. Our approach adapts the Hopf differential method of De Philippis, Hirsch, and Nahon [arXiv:2609.12180v2] to the gravitational setting, and combines it with their abstract approximation theorem to turn the holomorphic approximation of the Hopf differential into the local gradient bounds. An important new observation is that the weighted Cauchy-Beurling correction, combined with vanishing on the lower half plane, supplies the additional height decay needed to obtain the local gradient bounds. As a consequence, we remove the a priori growth hypothesis from the geometric analysis in [Acta Math. 206 (2011)]. For general variational solutions, we establish the Stokes corner or full-density blow-up alternative. Under the stated topological and interface hypotheses, we obtain the Stokes corner and two free boundary branches that are C^1 up to the stagnation point.
An Isogeometric Collocation Solver Based on the Quantized Tensor Train Representation

We introduce an isogeometric collocation framework based on the quan tized tensor train (QTT) representation to solve partial differential equa tions. The proposed method constructs isogeometric collocation operators directly in the QTT format using only a few sampled entries, enabling ef ficient compression and computation. The vectors of the geometry-derived coefficients at the collocation points are represented in the QTT format using the TT-cross approximation. We conduct numerical experiments using the proposed QTT-based isogeometric collocation framework for the convection diffusion-reaction problems in different spatial dimensions and for the Poisson problems on three-dimensional nontrivial geometries, showing significant re ductions in memory usage and computational cost while preserving solution accuracy.
Stability analysis of stochastic differential equations with the Koopman operator
François-Grégoire Bierwart; Gaëtan Louvet; Alexandre Mauroy

This paper investigates the stability of stochastic systems through the lens of the Koopman operator framework. In particular, we establish the connection between the convergence properties of the Koopman semigroup and specific stability properties of the underlying stochastic system. Moreover, we demonstrate that specific Koopman eigenfunctions capture stochastic attractivity properties and we illustrate these results with two numerical examples. This work mirrors existing Koopman operator-based stability results for deterministic systems and extends them to the stochastic framework.
A Geometric Characteristic Long Exact Sequence for Codimension-Two Spin and Pin-plus/minus Bordism

Following Botvinnik--Rosenberg \cite{BotvinnikRosenberg2023}, we define fibered-boundary bordism, introduce sphere-bundle bordism, and prove an exact sequence relating them to ordinary bordism. The sequence also holds when all sphere fibers are required to be non-$D^r$-bounding. Following Debray--Ye--Yu \cite{DebrayYeYu2026}, we define characteristic cycles with a chosen complement structure trivializing a characteristic class. For the GM and $\mathrm{KT}^{\pm}$ cases, deleting tubular neighborhoods and identifying sphere-bundle structures with determinant-twisted base structures give a characteristic exact sequence. This proves the bordism-group consequence of the DYY conjecture for our definitions, without constructing the conjectured map of spectra.
Vanilla Adiabatic Quantum Optimization Can Have Subexponential Advantage

We construct a family of objective functions $f \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ for which vanilla adiabatic quantum optimization along $H(s) = -(1-s)\sum_{i=1}^n X_i + s\sum_x f(x)\lvert x\rangle\!\langle x\rvert$ finds the global minimizer in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time, whereas any classical algorithm requires $\exp(n^{Ω(1)})$ time to do so in the black-box model. Our result is achieved by replacing the linearization technique in an earlier work of Leng et al. (arXiv:2504.14841), which establishes a similar subexponential quantum speedup using a transverse field Ising mixer rather than $-\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$.
Incidence methods for algebraic expanders over arbitrary fields

Let $A\subset F$ be finite, $N=|A|$, $p=\operatorname{char}F$ (with $p=\infty$ in characteristic zero), and $L=1+\log(2N)$. In the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, we establish \[ |AA+A|\gg N^{129/85}L^{-72/85}. \] This improves the long-standing $3/2$-exponent bound for $AA+A$ in positive characteristic in the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, without any assumption on the multiplicative doubling of $A$. We further establish uniform expansion bounds with exponents $129/85$ and $32/21$ for four families of three-variable product--quotient expanders, together with refined estimates over prime fields. For $λ\in F^\times$ and $N\le p^{1/2}$, our four-variable bounds include \[ |AA+λAA|\gg N^{214/135}L^{-7/9},\qquad |AA-AA|\gg_\varepsilon N^{6681/4175-\varepsilon} \quad(\varepsilon>0). \] In particular, several three- and four-variable targets admit uniform lower bounds with exponents greater than $3/2$ in the large-characteristic range. We also prove bounds with exponent $49/38$ for shifted products and shifted quotients, and for quadratic-image sumsets when $\operatorname{char}F\ne 2$, as well as characteristic-sensitive estimates for $AA+λA/A$ and $(A-A)^\times/(A-A)^\times$. The proofs combine higher-energy inequalities, regularisation, and point--line incidences.
Efficient Implementation of Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta Methods for Model Predictive Control
Anton Pozharskiy; Jonathan Frey; Katrin Baumgärtner; Armin Nurkanović; Moritz Diehl

In direct shooting methods for nonlinear optimal control, one of the major computational costs is simulation of the system and calculation of sensitivities. These costs are particularly steep when the stiffness of the controlled system prescribes the use of implicit integrators, amongst which, implicit Runge-Kutta schemes are most popular. These methods require the use of Newton's method to solve a moderately sized system of nonlinear equations with a dense Jacobian, the computation of which grows cubically with the number of stages, that is, the number of abscissa. To mitigate this we investigate the use of the family of Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta (DIRK) methods whose Butcher tableaux are lower triangular. We describe the structure exploiting linear algebra required to make the DIRK methods competitive with fully implicit methods, including efficient sensitivity calculations. Finally, we evaluate the performance of DIRK methods on several example systems, and show that the efficient implementation yields Pareto optimal integration schemes. The fixed step size integrators are provided as part of the acados package and use high-performance linear algebra provided by BLASFEO.
Boundary $ C^{2, γ} $ regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s MTW condition

We establish boundary regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s Ma--Trudinger--Wang condition. Let the source and target be bounded, mutually $ c $-convex domains in $ \mathbb{R}^n $, $ n\geqslant2 $, with $ C^{1,β} $ boundaries, and suppose that the cost is smooth, bi-twisted, and nondegenerate. For positive $ C^{0,α} $ densities bounded away from zero and having equal total mass, we prove that both Kantorovich potentials belong to $ C^{2,γ} $ up to the boundary, where $ γ= \min\{α,β\} $. Consequently, the optimal transport map is $ C^{1,γ} $ up to the boundary. The proof extends the monotonicity formula method of Collins and Tong to general costs through the geometry of the Kim--McCann metric. The resulting formula yields homogeneity of blow-up limits and uniform estimates for sections. These estimates give boundary obliqueness and allow comparison with solutions of the constant-density Monge--Ampère equation, leading to the claimed regularity.
Zeros of Pick and Hopf Differentials and Fences of Convex Domains

We prove that the vanishing order of a Pick or Hopf differential controls the corresponding convex domain through sharp disk comparisons. For a complete hyperbolic affine sphere, Pick vanishing order $m\ge0$ gives normalized projective coordinates in which the domain lies between disks of radii $\sqrt{\cos(π/(m+3))}$ and its reciprocal. For a harmonic diffeomorphism to a convex hyperbolic domain with complete $\partial$-energy metric, Hopf vanishing order $m$ gives a disk in the image of radius $\log\cot(π/(2(m+2)))$, centered at the image point. Equality characterizes the corresponding regular polygons. For polygonal targets, these comparisons prove the Fence conjecture of Dumas--Wolf and give explicit Hilbert and hyperbolic distance bounds for higher fences. We also construct simple-zero examples showing that these sufficient multiplicity conditions are not necessary.
Jingchao Lai; Danyi Li; Weigen Yan

For a matching-covered graph $G$, let $τ(G)$ denote the minimum number of perfect matchings needed to cover all edges of $G$. An $r$-regular graph $G$ is said to be an $r$-graph if $|\partial(X)|\geq r$ for each odd set $X\subseteq V(G)$, where $\partial(X)$ denotes the set of edges with precisely one end in $X$. The generalized Berge conjecture, which was proposed by Mazzuoccolo (J. Graph Theory, 73 (2013) 377-385) and equivalent to the generalized Berge-Fulkerson Conjecture posed by Seymour (Proc. London Math. Soc., 38 (1979) 423-460), states that $τ(G)\leq 2r-1$ for every $r$-graph $G$, while the 1-factorization conjecture, first explicitly formulated by Chetwynd and Hilton (Proc. London Math. Soc., 50 (1985) 193-206), states that $τ(G)=r$ for every $r$-graph $G$ of order $2n$ with $r\ge n$. These conjectures are still open. In this paper, we obtain the following two main results: 1. Let $G$ be an $r$-graph of order $2n$. If $r\ge n$, then $τ(G)\leq 2r-1$, which implies that the generalized Berge conjecture holds for $r\ge n$, and a linear upper bound of $τ(G)$ in the 1-factorization conjecture is obtained. 2. Let $G$ be an $r$-graph of order $2n$. If $r\ge 2n/3$, then $τ(G)\leq 4r$, which implies that a linear upper bound of $τ(G)$ in the generalized Berge conjecture is obtained if $r\geq 2n/3$. Our main approach combines equitable proper edge-colorings, matching extension techniques, and applications of Edmonds's perfect matching polytope theorem.
A Lie-Group Approach to Alfvénic Turbulence: The SO(3) Rotational p-model
Daniele Telloni; Sabrina Guastavino; Gary P. Zank; Luca Sorriso-Valvo; Michele Piana

The inner heliosphere is permeated by fully developed, highly intermittent nonlinear turbulence. Conventional stochastic models synthesize these multiscale fluctuations by injecting additive noise within a flat Euclidean space. However, such approaches fundamentally violate the topological constraints of ideal magnetohydrodynamics, inadvertently breaking the kinetic incompressibility of the plasma and introducing spurious magnetic compressibility. To preserve the exact geometrical invariants of Alfvénic fluctuations, a novel mathematical framework is presented: the rotational p-model. By mapping a multifractal singular measure directly into the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and integrating the associated stochastic differential equations in the Stratonovich sense on the spherical manifold $S^{2}$, the model generates highly intermittent, scale-dependent rotational dynamics. This Lie-group formulation conserves the magnetic field modulus while perfectly reproducing the fractional spectral envelopes and the non-Gaussian directional intermittency observed in space plasmas. Furthermore, by isolating purely directional reorientations, the framework provides exact analytical control over the waiting time statistics of magnetic intermittent bursts and the multifractal scaling exponents of angular deflections, offering a powerful new paradigm for the study of nonlinear turbulent phenomena.
Beyond Monotone Operators: Zarantonello-type Surjectivity Theorems and the Proximal Point Algorithm
José M. M. Brito; Felipe Lara; Jinyun Yuan

Outside the maximally monotone class, proximal point iterates need not exist, and their existence is usually assumed. We study the existence and convergence of inexact proximal iterates for set-valued star-monotone operators $T$ on real Hilbert spaces, with $\langle u,x-x^\ast\rangle\geq0$ for some zero $x^\ast$ and every $(x,u)$ in the graph of $T$. This class strictly contains monotone and pseudomonotone operators with zeros. We prove that $\mathrm{Id}+cT$ is surjective for every $c>0$ under four pairwise incomparable topological frameworks, several of whose hypotheses are necessary. Surjectivity can fail under the weak Minty condition with positive violation. For star $γ$-hypomonotone operators, $0<c<1/γ$ is the sharp range for guaranteed surjectivity. When $T$ is star-monotone at every zero, we give conditions for weak convergence of inexact sequences with summable errors, allowing arbitrary selections from the possibly set-valued resolvent. A counterexample exhibits nonconvergence under star monotonicity at a single zero. Under strong star monotonicity, we obtain strong convergence, including for certain nonsummable errors, and derive explicit R-linear rates. For a class of nonsmooth nonconvex--nonconcave minimax problems with star quasiconvex partial functions, every proximal step exists for every $c>0$. In the strongly star quasiconvex case, we obtain R-linear convergence results with subproblems solved to Clarke stationarity.
Local energy decay for small radial solutions of the two-dimensional Hamiltonian $abcd$ Boussinesq system

We consider the $abcd$ Boussinesq system in two space dimensions, a four-parameter family of models for the two-way propagation of small-amplitude long surface waves, in the generic regime $a,c<0$, $b,d>0$. We first revisit the local well-posedness theory in Sobolev spaces in dimensions $2\le n\le4$ and show that for the Hamiltonian case $b=d$ the Cauchy problem is globally well-posed for small data in the energy space $\mathbb{H}^1(\mathbb R^n)$. Then we consider the asymptotic behavior of these global solutions in the $n=2$ case. Under the condition $-a,-c>b/9$, we prove that every small solution with radial symmetry exhibits local energy decay. As a consequence, there are no small radial time-periodic (in particular, stationary) solutions. Decay also holds, along sequences of times, on balls whose radius grows almost linearly in time. The proof is based on new virial identities adapted to the radial structure of the system. In the proof we introduce two correction functionals such that the resulting quadratic form is coercive precisely when $-a,-c>b/9$, a threshold which is sharp for the functional. To our knowledge this is the first result describing the long-time dynamics of $abcd$ systems in dimension two.
Berry Esseen bounds for fractional Vasicek type processes: continuous and high-frequency regimes

We study the estimation of the drift parameters $(a,b)$ of the fractional Vasicek process $dX_t=a(b-X_t)\,dt+dB^H_t$, driven by a fractional Brownian motion of Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. The estimators are of moment type, built from the empirical mean and variance of the path, and are analysed in two regimes: continuous observation on $[0,T]$, and high-frequency observation at times $t_i=iΔ_n$ with $Δ_n\to0$ and $T_n=nΔ_n\to\infty$. Using the Malliavin--Stein method on the second Wiener chaos, we prove consistency of both estimators for every $H$, and quantitative central limit theorems in the Wasserstein distance: for $H<\frac34$ for the estimator of $a$, with explicit rates depending on $H$, and for every $H\in(0,1)$ for the estimator of $b$, at the rate $T^{-H}$. In the discrete regime the bounds contain an additional discretization term of order $Δ_n^{\min\{H+1/2,\,1\}}$, and for $H<\frac12$ the central limit theorem for the estimator of $b$ requires in addition $T_n^{1-2H}Δ_n^{1+2H}\to0$. A short Monte Carlo study illustrates the results.
Free energy distribution for two non-crossing directed polymers on the cylinder
Andrea De Luca; Pierre Le Doussal

We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th cumulant of (minus) the free energy $\log Z_L(t)$, grows as $c_k(L) t$, and we compute the amplitudes $c_k(L)$. To this aim we first study the integer moments $\langle Z_L(t)^n \rangle$, whose long-time behavior is determined by the ground-state energy of the one-dimensional attractive Lieb--Liniger model in the symmetry sector associated with the Young diagram $(n,n)$ (a two-component bosonic nested Bethe ansatz). This ground state energy is obtained using the nested Bethe-Ansatz involving $2n$ physical rapidities and $n$ auxiliary rapidities. The analytic continuation in the replica number $n$, which yields the cumulants $c_k(L)$, is performed through a non-trivial generalization of the method developed by Brunet and Derrida for a single polymer on the cylinder. We obtain fully explicit formulas for the mean $c_1(L)$ and the variance $c_2(L)$, and construct a systematic scheme for computing all higher cumulants $c_k(L)$. Finally, taking $L\to+\infty$ and $n\to0$ with $nL^{1/2}$ fixed, we derive a universal scaling function which characterizes the large-deviation statistics of the two-polymer free energy and is expected to be universal within the one-dimensional two-layer periodic SHE/KPZ class. The two tails of the large-deviation function are obtained analytically, revealing different roles of the non-crossing constraint in favorable and unfavorable fluctuations of the common disorder.
Real Determinantal and Segre Varieties: Stability and Area Minimization
Hongbin Cui; Xiaoxiang Jiao; Hangyue Zhu

We apply Liu's recently introduced moderation criterion to complete the classification of area-minimizing real determinantal varieties and real Segre varieties, thereby settling the remaining cases left open by Pedersen and Kerckhove--Lawlor \cite{Pedersen93,KerckhoveLawlor1999}. In particular, we prove that $C(2,3,1)$ is area-minimizing modulo $2$, resolving the $g=4$, $(m_1,m_2)=(1,1)$ case of the isoparametric focal-cone problem raised by Tang and Zhang \cite{TZ20} and recently revisited by Liu \cite{Liu2026}.
Optimal Deep Nonparametric Regression with Uniformly Bounded Lipschitz Constants
Jiaxin Shi; Ziyuan Chen; Jian Huang; Hansheng Wang

Stability under input perturbations is necessary for deep neural network estimators in many applications involving noisy covariates or estimated features. Weight norm constraints are widely used to control sensitivity to input perturbations by bounding the Lipschitz constant of neural networks. However, existing approximation results under fixed bounds on standard norm products are insufficient to establish optimal statistical rates. In this paper, we establish a sharp approximation theory for deep ReLU networks under a split spectral norm product constraint. This theoretical result shows that sufficiently smooth Hölder functions can be uniformly approximated to arbitrary accuracy as the network depth increases, with the norm-product bound held fixed. We then propose a penalized least squares estimator for deep nonparametric regression. The resulting estimator has a uniformly bounded Lipschitz constant while still achieving the optimal nonparametric rate up to a logarithmic factor. As applications, we establish optimal prediction rates for two-stage learning and provide robustness guarantees under adversarial input perturbations. Numerical studies show that the penalized estimator has well-controlled sensitivity to input perturbations and prediction accuracy comparable to that of classical deep network methods.
Boundary limits of the Bergman kernel and metric on generally decoupled domains of infinite type

In this paper, we compute the precise nontangential boundary limits of the Bergman kernel on the diagonal and its related invariants on generally decoupled domains in $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ ($n\ge1$) at a boundary point of infinite type. Our results extend recent work by Jaiswal for exponentially flat domains.
The $S$ and Double-Exponential Transformations with a Moment Expansion for Three-Centre Coulomb and Hybrid Integrals

Three-centre two-electron Coulomb and hybrid integrals over exponential-type functions involve semi-infinite radial integrals containing oscillatory spherical Bessel functions. We investigate the combination of the $S$ transformation with Fourier-type double-exponential (DE) quadrature for their accurate and efficient numerical evaluation. The $S$ transformation transfers derivatives from the spherical-Bessel factor to the radial amplitude, converting the integral into a sine representation particularly well suited to Fourier-type DE quadrature. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that the combined $S+\mathrm{DE}$ approach can substantially reduce the number of quadrature nodes required to achieve high accuracy compared with direct DE. We further identify a geometry-dependent oscillation-to-damping ratio and establish a convergent moment expansion in the weakly oscillatory regime. Exploiting this complementary representation markedly enhances the numerical reliability of the algorithm in regimes where direct oscillatory quadrature becomes inefficient. The method is examined through semi-infinite radial integrals and complete H$_2$O and C$_2$H$_4$ molecular integrals over Slater-type functions, with comparisons against complete $S$-series evaluations and values reported in the literature.
Spectrum of the parity operator for parafermions and parabosons from character formulas
N. I. Stoilova; J. Van der Jeugt

In a recent paper [J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 59 175201 (2026)] Green's triple relations for parafermions and parabosons were extended by including a new operator $P$, referred to as the parity operator. The spectrum of $P$ in Fock space representations was computed, making use of the action of parafermion (resp.\ paraboson) creation and annihilation operators. In the current paper, we adopt a different method to compute the spectrum of $P$, namely using character formulas. For a set of $n$ parafermions, the action of $P$ is deduced from character formulas of $so(2n+2)$. For a set of $n$ parabosons, the known spectrum of $P$ yields new character formulas of particular $osp(2|2n)$ representations.
Projection-Based and Modulus-Based Equivalent Reformulations of the Linear Complementarity Problem and Corresponding Iterative Methods: A Review
Bharat Kumar; Abhishek Kumar Singh Sengar; Deepmala

The Linear Complementarity Problem (LCP) is a fundamental mathematical model arising in optimization, equilibrium theory, and various scientific and engineering applications. Its complementarity structure admits several equivalent mathematical representations, which provide a foundation for developing a wide range of iterative solution methods. This review presents a systematic and critical analysis of the principal reformulations of the LCP, with particular emphasis on minimum-function, projection-based, positive-negative part, and modulus-based formulations. The mathematical equivalence of these representations to the standard LCP is examined, highlighting their underlying relationships and the preservation of the complementarity conditions. Building upon these formulations, the review surveys the corresponding iterative methods developed in the existing literature, focusing on their mathematical foundations, algorithmic structures, and convergence requirements. A comparative perspective is developed to discuss the relative advantages and limitations of the different approaches, emphasizing that the suitability of an iterative method depends on the structural properties of the underlying LCP and the specific algorithm employed. In addition, relevant performance measures, including iteration count, CPU time, complementarity residual, memory requirements, and parameter sensitivity, are discussed as criteria for numerical evaluation. Finally, the review identifies important challenges and potential research directions, particularly in adaptive parameter selection, effective matrix-splitting strategies, scalable implementations, and reproducible numerical benchmarking, with the aim of supporting the development of reliable and computationally efficient methods for solving LCPs
The algebraic classification of three-dimensional nilpotent left-symmetric dialgebras

Left-symmetric dialgebras (LSDA) are to left-symmetric algebras what Leibniz algebras are to Lie algebras. We classify the three-dimensional nilpotent LSDA over the complex numbers. To do this we adapt the annihilator-extension (Skjelbred-Sund) method to dialgebras, using the annihilator with respect to both products on both sides, and we compute the second cohomology of all two-dimensional nilpotent LSDA. Up to isomorphism, besides the null and split algebras there are nine non-split algebras and families; the 2-step nilpotent families depend on four and three parameters. We give isomorphism criteria and separating invariants, identify the left-symmetric and diassociative algebras in the list, and complete the two-dimensional classification of an earlier paper.
Stability for the Navier--Stokes and Incompressible Porous Media Equations with Only Vertical Dissipation on $\mathbb{R}^2$

For the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^2$, we prove that vertical viscosity alone yields global $H^2$ stability and algebraic decay of the vorticity and velocity for small reflection-symmetric data with polynomially weighted vorticity. Under stronger smallness assumptions, we obtain $H^3$ stability and vorticity-gradient decay, in contrast to unbounded gradient growth for Euler flows in the same symmetry class. For incompressible porous media (IPM), we obtain $H^2$ stability and decay under analogous assumptions with only vertical diffusion, despite the absence of derivative gain in Darcy's law. This complements finite-time blow-up constructions for nondiffusive IPM in periodic domains. The proofs combine a weighted inequality for odd functions with anisotropic energy estimates exploiting the structure of each system.
What Right-Angle Corners Reveal About an Uncalibrated Camera: Convex Cones, Certified Bounds and Identifiability

The corner of a box or a room, where three perpendicular edges meet, appears in an image as three segments meeting at a point. We ask what such junctions reveal about an uncalibrated camera's intrinsic parameters. Each junction is consistent with an explicit convex set of cameras; when only the focal length is unknown, this set is an interval in closed form. These sets are computed from the image alone, so calibrating from many junctions is a convex feasibility problem. Almost every junction bounds the focal length from below; we characterize when one also bounds it from above, and when many junctions determine it exactly. For a known vertex, the bounds can be certified against any bounded error in the measured edge directions.
Rigidity of randomly perturbed expanding circle maps
Jiangqiong Yu; Sandro Vaienti; Wenmeng Zhang

We extend the classical smooth linearization theory of expanding circle maps to randomly perturbed ones without requiring small perturbations, establishing two equivalent rigidity criteria of absolute continuity of random conjugacy and Lyapunov exponents along random periodic orbits. In the random setting, an essential difficulty is the uniqueness of absolutely continuous random invariant measures. For the first criterion, we overcome this difficulty by refining the memory-loss argument of Ott, Stenlund and Young, which gives the exponential convergence of probability densities, to establish the uniqueness of random invariant measures; for the second criterion, we bypass this difficulty by employing periodic-orbital averaging together with Jensen's equality condition to derive pointwise rigidity directly from the periodic data.
Semi-Implicit and Convex Splitting Schemes for the Surface Cahn--Hilliard Equation on Curved Closed Surfaces
Harri Hakula; Antti Rasila; Xinpeng Xu

The surface Cahn--Hilliard equation describes phase separation and coarsening of a conserved composition field on fixed curved surfaces. We study a mixed $hp$-surface finite element discretization with curvilinear high-order elements, primarily on the sphere, with the stabilized semi-implicit BDF2 integrator and a stabilized convex-splitting variant solved with the same factorization. For the semi-implicit scheme with a quadratic-growth potential and a truncated nonlinear bulk chemical-potential term, we prove exact discrete mass conservation, energy decay for the start-up steps, an exact per-step energy balance for the BDF2 phase, and a conditional monotone law for a modified Lyapunov functional. A manufactured solution with analytic forcing verifies second order in time and the expected $h$- and $p$-convergence. Torus tests include controlled equal-area bands, whose diffuse energies reproduce sharp-interface perimeters within $1\%$, deterministic coarsening, and a viscous R{ä}tz--Voigt model. Genus-two and genus-three calculations on implicit surfaces conserve mass to roundoff, and their unstable-mode counts agree with area-based Weyl estimates within $1\%$.
Time-Decay Rates toward a Rarefaction-Contact-Shock Composite Wave for the One-Dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations

We consider the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations when the end states are connected by a rarefaction wave, a contact discontinuity, and a shock. For a fixed weak nonzero shock, sufficiently weak rarefaction and contact waves, and small H^2(R) initial perturbations, we establish asymptotic stability with a time-dependent shift on the viscous shock. The L^4 time average of the uniform perturbation and the shift velocity over [t,2t] is bounded by C_S(1+t)^(-1/4). We prove pointwise-in-time bounds of order (1+t)^(-1/12) on the whole line, (1+t)^(-1/4) near the shifted shock, and (1+t)^(-1/6) on |x| >= ηt for each fixed η>0. The proof uses energy estimates and comparison on finite time interval
MIMO Channel Extrapolation to Unobserved Radiation Modes via Learned Path Refinement

A pattern-reconfigurable multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receiver can sample every antenna element and still leave entire radiation modes unobserved. The calibrated patterns weight a common set of propagation paths, which links these missing channels to the measured rows. Our estimator learns to correct the complex gains and spatial frequencies of those paths, so a correction inferred from measured rows updates every unmeasured mode. Each stage combines a damped least-squares proposal with a learned correction scaled by noise power and local array sensitivity. Training on complete simulated channels rewards corrections that reduce prediction error across modes, including those with no measured rows. The learned rule transfers from pursuit-based training estimates to a ridge variable-projection initializer without retraining. In matched simulations, refinement reduces error on wholly unobserved modes as well as across the full channel. Coefficient updates account for most of the gain, and the learned rule further improves on adaptive ridge shrinkage at fixed angles. Individual channel trajectories show that extrapolation can improve even as the residual on the measured rows increases.
Constructive Trend to Equilibrium for Low-regularity Boltzmann and BGK equations

We study the long-time behavior of global mild solutions to the cutoff Boltzmann and BGK equations on $\T^3$ under a Gaussian lower bound and a polynomially weighted $L^\infty$ upper bound. The main step is a finite-time estimate which uses free transport to control the entropy of the local Maxwellian by microscopic entropy and dissipation, without assuming Sobolev regularity. For Boltzmann, Villani's entropy-production inequality and a comparison of collision kernels give polynomial decay when the velocity weight has order $m>7$. For a sufficiently large weight, the large-amplitude theory then gives exponential decay in the weighted norm and in relative entropy. For BGK, the microscopic inequality is linear, so entropy decays exponentially from the finite-time estimate. Finally, we establish a density criterion for large-data BGK dynamics in the polynomially weighted $L^\infty$ class of Perthame and Pulvirenti. For weight order $m>10$, a uniform upper bound on the local density guarantees uniform-in-time weighted bounds and exponential convergence to equilibrium in both relative entropy and the weighted $L^\infty$ norm.
On global error estimates of a local discontinuous Galerkin method of the Boussinesq system of equations
Debendra K. Swain; Saumya Bajpai; Deepjyoti Goswami

In this paper, we develop and analyze a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) finite element method for the Boussinesq system of equations, and employ an upwind scheme to effectively manage the nonlinear convective terms, thereby ensuring stability and accuracy. Our analysis establishes new \emph{a priori} regularity estimates for the semidiscrete LDG approximations. We establish optimal \emph{a priori} error estimates for the velocity approximation in $\bL^2$--norm, the pressure approximation in $L^2$--norm and for temperature in $L^2$--norm for all $t>0$. Our proof relies on the standard elliptic and parabolic duality arguments and modified Stokes operators defined on appropriate broken Sobolev spaces. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the given data, we further establish error estimates that remain uniform in time. Furthermore, the backward Euler scheme is considered for a full discretization, and optimal fully discrete error estimates are derived. Finally, we carry out numerical experiments to substantiate our theoretical findings.
Categorified Koszul duality and deformation theory of higher categories

This paper develops a deformation theory for stable $(\infty,n)$-categories for $n > 1$. We introduce the framework of complete $t$-structured stable presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Within this setting, we establish a higher categorified Koszul duality among complete $t$-structured presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Using this duality, we develop the deformation theory. We prove that the deformation problem for such categories is a well-behaved formal moduli problem determined by Hochschild cohomology, and we deduce the corresponding obstruction theory. Finally, we apply our results to sheaves of categories on perfect stacks.
Asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic SPDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion
Diancong Jin; Minoo Kamrani; Xu Wang

We study the strong convergence and asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic stochastic partial differential equations driven by additive cylindrical fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(\frac12,1)$. The drift is globally Lipschitz and Gâteaux differentiable, with a second directional derivative taking values in a negative-order space. Under a weighted Hilbert--Schmidt condition on the noise and suitable derivative bounds, we establish strong error estimates that reflect the interaction between noise regularity and drift regularity. In a regime where the strong order is one, the normalized error $m(X^m-X)$ converges in probability in $C([0,T];\V)$ to the unique continuous solution of a random linear integral equation. Its stochastic forcing is a divergence integral plus an explicit covariance correction. The proof combines a Gâteaux chain rule for Malliavin derivatives, uniform spectral approximations, and time increment estimates. Localization gives the result for independent random initial values with finite moments, together with lower-moment convergence at each fixed time.
Vague rotational symmetry at BCC [100] twist grain boundaries

In earlier work (arXiv:2603.21158) we introduced vague rotational symmetry for proximal coincidence point sets at grain boundaries. A prescribed rotation must be realizable at every pair tolerance $\varepsilon$ by moving each midpoint of an admitted atomic pair by at most $\varepsilon/2$, half the maximum pair separation. We prove the proposed classification for the planar model of a body-centred cubic $[100]$ twist boundary. On $0\leqθ\leq45^\circ$, the maximal rotational order is twelve at $30^\circ$, eight at $45^\circ$, and four at every other misorientation. Vague $n$-fold symmetry forces $ξ_n M=M$ for the Fourier module $M$, hence $\mathbb{Z}[ξ_n]\subseteq M$ in crystal coordinates. For every rotation of finite order preserving $M$, we determine the least uniform displacement for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, allowing independent point motions and a free rotation centre. In this regime twelvefold symmetry at $30^\circ$ costs $\varepsilon/(2\sqrt3)$, and eightfold symmetry at $45^\circ$ costs zero. At a twist of approximately $25.53^\circ$, the Fourier module also has eightfold symmetry, but realizing it in the plane costs $\sqrt2\,\varepsilon$.
Quasi-Bisections of Cubic Graphs with Tree and Circuit Decompositions
Xixiong Tang; Rong-Xia Hao; Yilun Luo; Cun-Quan Zhang

A $2$-quasi-bisection of a graph is a vertex $2$-coloring in which the color classes differ in size by at most two and every monochromatic component has at most two vertices. Esperet, Mazzuoccolo, and Tarsi in [J. Graph Theory, 86(2017), 149-158] conjectured that every cubic graph admits such a coloring. DeVos and Nurse proved the conjecture for cubic graphs whose edge sets can be partitioned into a tree and a circuit. This result is generalized in this paper for a larger family of cubic graphs. The conjecture is verified for cubic graphs whose edge set can be partitioned into two subsets $E(T)$ and $E(J)$, where $T$ is a tree of $G$ and $J$ is an even subgraph containing at most two odd circuit components.
Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
Zhouxing Luo; Lei Wang; Xin Liu

Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. Under the mild assumption that the true distribution has a finite fourth moment, we further establish a uniform finite-sample performance guarantee for the proposed model. An iteratively reweighted majorization-minimization algorithm is also developed to solve the resulting nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problem, with a rigorous analysis of its convergence properties. Numerical experiments substantiate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and the practical effectiveness of the infinity-Wasserstein model in downstream applications.
Indecomposable representations of $C^{\infty}(S^1,\aff)$ on polynomial spaces over jet spaces

We study a class of finite dimensional complex vector spaces \(\pn\), \(n \in \bn\), consisting of polynomials on \(\jnmc\), the space of \((n-1)\) jets at a fixed point \(t_0 \in S^1\) of \(C^\infty\) functions \(S^1 \to \bc\). The loop group \(C^\infty(S^1,\aff)\) of the affine group \(\aff\) acts naturally on \(\pn\) by an indecomposable linear representation. The space \(\pn\) is canonically isomorphic to the space of holomorphic sections of a certain line bundle over the loop space of the Riemann sphere. It has an intricate structure, leading to infinite families of combinatorial identities. In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for a polynomial on \(\jnmc\) to belong to \(\pn\). Furthermore, we give partial answers to several conjectures concerning \(\pn\).
Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra

We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in \mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ as $λ$-lengths of return arcs on a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Markov--Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.
Comparing Data-Driven and Numerical Weather Prediction Forecasts of Extreme Weather: A Review
Gabriele Messori; Hiu-Wang Lau; Chenyu Dong; Gianmarco Mengaldo; Leonardo Olivetti

Data-driven weather forecasting models, chiefly trained on reanalysis data, now match or beat physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) models on most headline scores, but whether this advantage extends to extreme weather is contested. We review peer-reviewed studies that directly compare data-driven forecasts with NWP for extremes, from nowcasting to subseasonal lead times. We discuss grey literature in the outlook but do not include it in the formal review. There is good agreement on the fact that data-driven models mostly outperform NWP on temperature extremes, tropical cyclone tracks and the location of synoptic features across time scales. The evidence is mixed for extreme precipitation and feature-based extreme event detection such as extremes related to atmospheric rivers, while it leans toward better NWP performance for estimating event intensity. For record-breaking events that lie outside the training distribution, the evidence is narrower. Nonetheless, both a systematic global evaluation and several case studies find that physics-based models retain the advantage, with data-driven models underestimating both the frequency and the magnitude of records. Hybrid systems that post-process NWP with machine-learning (ML), or couple data-driven forecasts with physics-based models, deliver some of the largest and most consistent gains. We argue that headline scores, verification choices and case selection explain much of the apparent disagreement in the literature, and provide recommendations for a more trustworthy and interpretable evaluation of data-driven models for extreme and record-breaking weather.
Graded version of local-global principle for Steinberg and Chevalley groups

In this article, an analog of a graded version of Quillen-Suslin's local-global principle was established for Steinberg groups $St(Φ,-)$ and Chevalley groups $G(Φ,-)$ over a reduced irreducible root system $Φ$.
Zero-sum subsequences of cross number $1$ over cyclic groups

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $\mathsf{T}(G)$ be the smallest integer $t$ such that every sequence of length $t$ over $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of cross number $1$. We determine the exact value of $\mathsf{T}(C_n)$ for every positive integer $n$, showing that $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=2n-1$ when $n$ is odd and $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=3n/2-1$ when $n$ is even. In particular, $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=\mathsf{s}(C_n)$ for odd $n$.
Pseudocompact MAD families under $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak c$
Vinicius de Oliveira Rodrigues; Fabrício Yohei Ynone

We prove that if the bounding number $\mathfrak b$ equals the cardinality of the continuum $\mathfrak c$, then every infinite almost disjoint family of size less than $\mathfrak c$ can be extended to a maximal almost disjoint family whose Isbell--Mrówka space has a pseudocompact Vietoris hyperspace.
Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties
Yulia Alexandr; Moritz Grillo; Thiago Holleben; Guido Montúfar; Teresa Yu

We give a complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties. We show that the determinantal equations arising from rank constraints imposed by the activation patterns generate the defining ideals, thereby proving a conjecture of Alexandr-Montúfar. The set-theoretic proof uses a characterization of orbit closures of matrix pencils in terms of the Kronecker canonical form.
Symplectic $\mathbb{CP}^n$ recognition and filling rigidity via Rabinowitz Floer homology

We prove that a symplectic manifold $X$ admitting a pseudo-holomorphic line through two generic points, formulated as the non-vanishing of a genus zero Gromov--Witten invariant, is (rationally) homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^n$, with identical first Chern class and quantum cohomology. Together with generalizations of this result to pseudo-holomorphic lines with tangency constraints, they provide a new mechanism for establishing the topological uniqueness of Liouville fillings of certain contact manifolds. We obtain filling rigidity for the ideal boundary of a class of affine varieties that admit $\mathbb{CP}^n$ as a compactification; notable examples include the ideal boundary of the complement of any hyperplane arrangement and $ST^*\mathbb{RP}^n$ for $n\ge 3$. The proofs are based on Rabinowitz Floer homology and its variants.
Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality for equivariant vector bundles on Drinfeld spaces
Zhenghui Li; Benchao Su; Zhixiang Wu

We study duality and finiteness of locally analytic representations arising from compactly supported coherent cohomology of Drinfeld spaces. We prove that Grothendieck--Serre duality for equivariant vector bundles realizes Bernstein--Zelevinsky duality of locally analytic representations. We follow the strategy of Fargues for $\ell$-adic sheaves and obtain resolutions of locally analytic representations by compactly induced representations. The resolutions motivate us to introduce the notion of locally analytic representations of compact presentation, which generalizes the notion of finitely presented representations. These representations are related to prim objects on the classifying stack in the sense of $6$-functor formalism and their extension groups to admissible locally analytic representations are finite-dimensional. As an application, we establish Serre duality for extension groups of locally analytic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ attached to non-trianguline de Rham Galois representations under the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.
Near-optimal convergence of Widlund's method and numerical exploration of different implementations
Andrew J. Higgins; Logan O. Reed; Daniel B. Szyld

For linear systems arising from the discretization of certain classes of mathematical models, the splitting of the linear system into its Hermitian and skew-Hermitian parts has a physical meaning.
