Moreover, any constant vorticity $γ\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$ suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability at every finite depth. The proof combines Hamiltonian spectral perturbation theory, symbolic computations, and formal verification in Rocq. Away from the transition set, our results rigorously confirm the stability criterion predicted by the nonlinear Schrödinger approximation of Thomas, Kharif, and Manna.
Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs

Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.
Movable Antenna-Aided ISAC: A Time- and Frequency-Division Framework
Yuyan Zhou; Haocheng Hua; Jie Xu; Rui Zhang

This paper investigates movable-antenna (MA)-enhanced integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) under time division duplex (TDD) and frequency division duplex (FDD) protocols, where sensing and communications occupy orthogonal time and frequency resources, respectively. A wideband target-position Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) is derived under a pulse-radar framework with pulse compression, incorporating delay and angle estimation error bounds in Cartesian coordinates. Both bounds depend on sensing power; the delay bound also depends on sensing bandwidth, while the angle bound depends on the effective aperture determined by the antenna position vector (APV). A worst-case position CRB over a prescribed target region ensures robust sensing performance. For multiuser downlink communication, joint APV and resource-allocation problems are formulated for TDD and FDD to maximize the minimum achievable user rate subject to the sensing requirement. An alternating optimization algorithm is developed for FDD, while TDD is addressed by searching over feasible sensing pulse numbers combined with APV optimization. Representative scenarios clarify how MA improves channel orthogonality and enlarges the sensing aperture, and how these effects shape the TDD/FDD rate comparison. Numerical results show that APV optimization enlarges the communication-sensing tradeoff region over fixed-position antenna benchmarks. The optimized configurations exhibit distinct tendencies: TDD favors a larger antenna position variance, whereas FDD favors better channel orthogonality among users.

We establish stability results for internal homs of $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets, a framework motivated by nerves of Frobenius monoids in the category of relations. Rotations are modelled through edge witnesses and horn-filling conditions, without requiring unique fillers. For $\varepsilon$-fibrant objects $X$ and $Y$, we prove that the internal hom $\mathrm{Fun}(X,Y)$ satisfies the $\varepsilon$-coherence conditions and admits fillers for all $\varepsilon$-horns of dimension at least two. Its subobject consisting of simplices whose vertices correspond to $η$-edge-preserving maps is $\varepsilon$-fibrant. We also introduce $η\varepsilon$-simplicial sets by adding explicit $η$-witnesses and prove that the internal hom of two $η\varepsilon$-fibrant objects is again $η\varepsilon$-fibrant. Our proofs use adjunctions relating $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets and paracyclic sets. We characterise the $\varepsilon$-horn filling property by requiring the corresponding counit to be a trivial Kan fibration. Consequently, for every object satisfying this property, coherent choices of rotations of each simplex form a contractible Kan complex.
The Möbius function of factorizations with a simple prime factor

The poset of factorizations of a positive integer $n$ (ordered by refinement) is known to have a very irregular Möbius function. We prove that this function becomes completely explicit whenever $n$ is divisible by a prime $q$ to the first power only ($q^2 \nmid n$). Specifically, between a factorization with $k$ factors and $n$ itself, the Möbius function is given by $(-1)^{k-1}$ multiplied by the number of ways to order the factors that are not divisible by $q$. As a consequence, the sum of the absolute values of the Möbius function over this interval equals twice the number of ordered factorizations of $n/q$.

Haemers \cite{Haemers2020} conjectured that every connected noncomplete graph $G$ satisfies $t(G)\geqslantμ_2/(μ_n-δ)$, where $t(G)$ is the toughness of $G$, $μ_2$ and $μ_n$ are its algebraic connectivity and Laplacian spectral radius, and $δ$ is its minimum degree. Greaves and Zhu \cite{GreavesZhu2026} recently proved this conjecture, leaving the equality case open. We characterize all graphs attaining equality: a graph attains equality if and only if its complement has a complete component whose order is at least the Laplacian spectral radius of every other component. Equivalently, its algebraic connectivity and independence number sum to its order. We also determine all vertex cuts attaining the toughness, and show that for regular graphs, the equality graphs are exactly the complete multipartite graphs with parts of equal size.
Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors

The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only $2\times 2$ unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about $9\%$ better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.
Representing in Low rank II: Virtual structure and Isomorphism problem
Robynn Corveleyn; Geoffrey Janssens; Doryan Temmerman

We group theoretically characterise the finite groups $G$ and number fields $F$ such that all $F$-representations of reduced degree at least $2$ are so-called exceptional. If $G$ is not a $2$-group, we obtain a full classification. Secondly, we determine whether such groups are uniquely determined by their group algebra $FG$. In particular, we obtain an instance of the virtual structure problem of Kleinert and answer the rational isomorphism problem for such groups.
On the periodicity of meromorphic functions of the form $ff^{(k)}$
Shuang-Shuang Yang; Dong-hai Zhao; Chung-Chun Yang; Liang-Wen Liao

For a non-entire meromorphic function $f$ and an integer $k$, we will show that whenever $ff^{(k)}$ is periodic so is $f$. This result gives an affirmative answer to a significant class of the so called generalized Yang's conjecture.
Linear Dynamic Range Extension for Rydberg Atomic Receiver via Band-Limited Reconstruction
Meng Fang; Lebin Chen; Jun-Rong Chen; Ming-Min Zhao; Bin-Bin Wei

Rydberg-atom receiver offers a promising approach to radio-frequency (RF) signal reception in wireless communication and sensing systems, combining high sensitivity with the potential for broad frequency coverage. However, the limited linear dynamic range (LDR) of the atomic system causes nonlinear distortion at high input signal levels, thereby restricting the receiver's effective linear input range. To address this issue, we analyze the mechanisms underlying nonlinear distortion in Rydberg atomic receivers and propose a physics-informed band-limited iterative reconstruction (PI-BLIR) method. Specifically, by exploiting the known nonlinear atomic response and signal bandwidth prior, we formulate a constrained maximum-likelihood problem to reconstruct the distorted complex intermediate-frequency (IF) waveform. With the bandwidth constraint absorbed into the frequency-domain parameterization, the constrained maximum-likelihood problem is transformed into an unconstrained optimization problem, which is solved using gradient descent. The proposed method relies solely on digital post-processing and requires no changes to the local-oscillator (LO) field strength, optical parameters, or atomic operating conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that PI-BLIR extends the receiver's LDR by more than 14 dB and enhances the demodulation performance of the atomic receiver.
Cartesian products of groups as quantum metric spaces

We provide a new class of finitely generated groups whose word-length functions give rise to compact quantum metric spaces. Kaad's recent theory of matrix compact quantum metric spaces is instrumental in obtaining this new class, and along the way we also show that any length function on an amenable group which gives rise to a compact quantum metric space in fact gives rise to a matrix compact quantum metric space, and that the corresponding result is false for the free group on two generators.
Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part~II: a new pathwise analysis with randomized subspaces
Sara Shashaani; Coralia Cartis; Kwassi Joseph Dzahini

Stochastic trust-region methods are usually analyzed in expectation or with high probability: the guarantee is about the law of the algorithm, not about the run in hand. This paper analyzes the adaptive sampling stochastic trust-region method ASTRO-DF (which is the reuse variant ASTRA-R in Part I) in random subspaces along almost every sample path. The route has one probabilistic ingredient, the accuracy of the common-random-number estimates at the adaptive sample size, uniformly over the trust region; Part~I established it by chaining, here it is obtained at the stopping time by optional stopping and converted, by the first Borel--Cantelli lemma, into an accuracy that holds from a random index on, after which the deterministic trust-region argument applies. We prove almost sure convergence and almost sure iteration and sample complexity of orders $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(dε^{-2})$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(d^2ε^{-4})$, with a subspace dimension growing logarithmically; we show that at a fixed subspace dimension the eventual-accuracy argument yields $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-2-\mathcal{O}(1/p)})$ iterations and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-4-\mathcal{O}(1/p)})$ samples; we show that the random index after which the rates hold cannot be too large and has an explicit, rapidly decaying tail. Compared with the supermartingale route, the pathwise route needs no lower bound on the per-iteration probability of a good iteration, no coupling between the trust-region expansion factor and the sketch, and no moment condition on the summed squared radii.
Safety Certificates for Systems under Attack via Stackelberg Set Games
Nikolaos Athanasopoulos; David Laverty; Gregory Provan; Quanyan Zhu

We study a Stackelberg set selection game for linear systems subject to bounded disturbances and additive attacks. The defender selects the vector parameter of a polytopic safe set template; the attacker, after observing this choice, selects the vector parameter of an admissible attack set. The payoff is a signed, facet-normalised invariance margin that tests invariance exactly and quantifies either the available contraction or the facet inflation needed when invariance fails. Both controlled and robust controlled invariance are treated, corresponding to different information patterns for the control input. Exploiting the structure of parameterised polyhedra, we show that within each validity region the margin is concave in the attack parameter, which reduces the follower minimisation to finitely many extreme parameters. The complete max--min game is then solved by a finite family of LPs, one per defender validity region, each enforcing all attacker regions under a common defender decision and guaranteed margin. The framework handles hard state constraints and additional costs related to the safe set size, and recovers optimal set parameters together with state and attack realisations that activate the certificate. A load frequency control example under false data injection illustrates the construction, the validity decomposition, and the two information patterns.
Equidistribution of Gross lattices of supersingular elliptic curves

For a prime $p$, we consider two important families of integral quadratic lattices associated to isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}$, the lattices of endomorphisms of trace zero, and the Gross lattices of endomorphisms. We prove effective equidistribution of the shapes of these lattices as $p\to\infty$ through primes, in the arithmetic locally symmetric space of unimodular lattices up to isometry. As an application, we obtain, as $p\to\infty$, the asymptotic distribution of successive minima of these lattices. These results are proved using tools from homogeneous dynamics, in particular, the key dynamical input is a recent adelic equidistribution theorem due to Einsiedler, Margulis, Mohammadi, and Venkatesh.
An entropy-stable splitting strategy for a hyperbolic dispersive shallow-water model on unstructured meshes
Frédéric Couderc; Arnaud Duran; Maria Kazakova; Bastien Lombard; Pascal Noble; Rémy Baraille; Jean-Paul Vila

This paper presents an entropy-stable splitting strategy for the numerical solution of a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre--Green--Naghdi (SGN) model, leading to an efficient solver for dispersive water waves on unstructured meshes. The model was introduced by Escalante et al. (2019) and justified shortly thereafter by Richard (2021) as an asymptotic model of the free-surface Euler equations under a weak compressibility assumption. While the parent model includes full topography terms and enhanced dispersive properties, the present study focuses on its mild-slope form without enhanced dispersion, which retains an exact energy equation, the cornerstone of the stability analysis. The splitting yields a shallow-water subsystem with two passive scalars, governed by the \textit{slow} gravity waves, and an acoustic subsystem carrying the dispersive effects, governed by the \textit{fast} acoustic waves. The gravity step adapts an existing entropy-stable scheme, while an original scheme is derived for the acoustic step; both dissipate the energy at the discrete level, under local fully discrete stability criteria on general unstructured meshes. Complementary linear analyses select the low-dissipation calibration of the gravity step used in the computations, outside the scope of the nonlinear estimate. The acoustic step, which requires no global linear solve, is sub-iterated after each gravity time step; the resulting solver is three to six times more expensive than a classical shallow-water solver, depending on the chosen acoustic speed. Numerical validations, ranging from academic benchmarks to a realistic coastal configuration, highlight the properties of the approach and pave the way for operational use.
The Thermodynamic Limit and the Landau degeneracy

Usually, thermodynamic quantities are calculated by first regularizing the system in a confining box, which may have hard walls or periodic boundaries. One then studies the finite system and takes the thermodynamic limit by letting the box grow indefinitely. Here, we discuss a regularization scheme devised in the late 1980s [1] to study the thermodynamic equations of an anyon gas [2]. Instead of confining the system with walls, the method adds a smooth harmonic potential. Quantities are evaluated in its presence, and the potential is then gradually removed. A suitable prescription for taking this limit is needed to obtain meaningful thermodynamic results.
Holonomy groupoids of singular subalgebroids in the non-integrable case

The holonomy groupoid of a singular foliation was constructed by Androulidakis and Skandalis around 2006. The construction was later extended to singular subalgebroids of an integrable Lie algebroid, upon a choice of integrating Lie groupoid. In this work, we extend the construction of the holonomy groupoid even further, by allowing for non-integrable Lie algebroids. To do so, we make a choice of integrating local Lie groupoid $G$. When the Mal'cev completion $AC(G)$ is smooth, our construction recovers the holonomy groupoid associated with the Lie groupoid $AC(G)$. Furthermore, our holonomy groupoid has an associated $*$-algebra. We present examples in which the holonomy groupoid is realized as a quotient of the transformation groupoid of a Lie group action.
Hamming and Johnson-Type Bounds for Joint Error Correction and Detection

We derive upper bounds on the size of codes for joint error correction and detection over classical $q$-ary Hamming spaces. A $(c,c')$ joint error correcting and detecting code corrects every error of weight at most $c$ and detects every error whose weight lies between $c+1$ and $c+c'$. We establish equivalent conditions for this decoding requirement using Hamming balls and Hamming rings, and derive a joint bound that reduces to the Hamming bound when $c'=0$. We introduce joint perfect codes and show that binary repetition codes attain the joint bound whenever $n=2c+c'+1$. For codes satisfying $d_{\min}=2c+c'+1$, we investigate an alternative joint bound based on ring multiplicity and constant-weight code bounds. A further argument using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and pairwise ring intersections yields a refined joint bound that is always at least as strong as the original joint bound. We then incorporate an additional outer Hamming shell to obtain a Johnson-type extension. This extension provides a strict improvement for binary codes with $c'=1$, $d_{\min}=2c+2$, $c\geq2$, and $d_{\min}+2\leq n\leq3d_{\min}/2-1$. These results connect sphere-packing bounds with the geometry of joint error correction and detection.
Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data

For the unforced Euler equations, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity within the class of axisymmetric flows without swirl, whose solution blows up in finite time. The initial vorticity belongs simultaneously to every Hölder space $C^α$, $α<1/3$. This is sharp given that global regularity is known when $α=1/3$ in the case of axisymmetric flows without swirl. Previous constructions by Shkoller \cite{Shk26}, Chen \cite{Chen26I,Chen26II}, and Shao--Wei--Zhang--Zhang \cite{SWZZ26} establish blow-up for each prescribed exponent $α$ in the same sharp range. Our construction achieves simultaneous membership in all these spaces. In addition, our construction is short. Our proof uses multiscale initial data, in the spirit of Kim--Jeong~\cite{KJ22}, Córdoba--Martínez-Zoroa--Zheng~\cite{CMZZ25}, and Bang--Cheskidov~\cite{BC26}. The blow-up mechanism is a forward cascade through successively smaller scales. A main difficulty in approaching the critical exponent $1/3$ is caused by large self-deformation. Our main idea to overcome this difficulty is to obtain a lower bound for strain at the stationary non-smooth point by using angular redistribution. A related outstanding open problem is to establish an unforced Euler blow-up from smooth data in the case of axisymmetric flows with swirl. A recent multiscale construction by OpenAI for the unforced Euler equations is, however, non-axisymmetric. Although we work in the no-swirl class, the axisymmetric multiscale mechanism developed here may offer a possible route toward the still-open problem of axisymmetric smooth blow-up.
Certificate-Based Verification of Pulsed Field Ablation Models

Computational models of pulsed field ablation predict the lesion as the tissue where the electric field exceeds a lethal threshold. Their numerical error is rarely bounded, and automated pipelines increasingly run them without an expert checking each result. To verify each run, we separate the question "was the stated model solved correctly?" from the solver that answers it. An untrusted solver returns with its answer a certificate, consisting of a potential with the correct electrode and ground values and an exactly charge-conserving current. A small independent checker verifies the certificate against a written specification of the physics. Using the Prager-Synge hypercircle theorem evaluated in ball arithmetic, it turns the certificate into guaranteed two-sided bounds on the impedance and on the root-mean-square field of every tile of a lesion map, also over a range of blood/tissue conductivity ratios. A vectorized version of the checker takes about a tenth of the solve time. For a focal electrode in contact, the tile-resolved depth at 1000 V and 700 V/cm is proven to lie in 3.50-3.75 mm for every ratio from 1.7 to 3.75. For a bipolar catheter, certified depths overlap published in-vivo depths. Where they differ from a published reference model, the certificates prove that the difference is not numerical error in our computation. We compare the certificate with a grid convergence study on the same solver. On graded grids the study is sharper for local fields but remains an estimate. On uniform grids it fails to converge at the electrode edge, where the certificate still gives a valid bracket. Solvers that deliberately solve equations other than the specified ones pass the grid convergence study, but the certificates refute their claims or leave them unsupported.
Characterizing M-estimators using canonical divergences from information geometry

On Euclidean space, the losses that produce consistent M-estimators of a functional are its strictly consistent scoring functions (Dimitriadis, Fissler and Ziegel, 2024), and Osband's principle characterizes these through identification functions, which define method-of-moments estimators. We extend this characterization to the probability simplex. We define the residual, which on Euclidean space is a subtraction, as the inverse exponential map of an affine connection. It identifies the exponential barycenter of the connection: the arithmetic, normalized geometric and Fréchet means for the mixture, exponential and Levi-Civita connections. Its integral along geodesics is the canonical divergence of Ay and Amari (2015). A geometric form of Osband's principle decides which losses each connection admits. For the flat connections every strictly convex generator yields a consistent Bregman loss. For the curved $α$-connections, half the squared Fisher-Rao distance is (up to scale) the only consistent loss for the Fréchet mean, and for $α\notin \{-1, 0, 1\}$ no such loss exists and only the method of moments remains. The residual is integrable only at $α= 0$, sharpening the integrability claim of Ay and Amari. The characterization yields the estimating equations of regression on the simplex and the calibration decomposition of compositional forecasts.
Universal Spaces for Coarsely Light Maps

Coarsely light maps were introduced by Dydak--Weighill as a large-scale analogue of light maps. We show that a proper metric space has asymptotic dimension at most $n$ if and only if it admits a coarsely light map to $\mathbb R^n$. As an application, we resolve two questions of Benjamini--Schramm--Timár concerning semi-regular maps.
Rate Optimal Streaming Codes Under an Extended Delay Profile for Three-Node Relay Networks
Ke Wang; Wenjie Ma; Zhipeng Li; Yaqiang Zhang

We study streaming codes for a three-node relay network with burst lengths $b_1,b_2$ and an end-to-end decoding delay $T$. Let $u=\max\{b_1,b_2\}$ and $v=\min\{b_1,b_2\}$, and write $T-v=pu+q$, where $T\ge u+v$ and $0\le q<u$. We develop two binary constructions, SR and SR-2, using extended delay profiles that allow the relay to forward causally invertible combinations of current and past source symbols. The SR construction attains the non-adaptive rate upper bound whenever \[ \frac{T-u-v}{2u-v}\le\left\lfloor\frac{T-u-v}{u}\right\rfloor. \] SR-2 enlarges this range under the sufficient condition \[ q(v-q)\le(p-1)u(u-v). \] These constructions complement the known divisibility and large-delay regimes. We also establish two limitations of systematic ordinary coordinate forwarding. First, it cannot attain the rate upper bound when $0<T-u-v<v$. Second, for equal burst lengths $b$, it attains the bound if and only if $b\mid(T-2b)$; a quantitative upper bound gives a strictly positive rate gap in every nondivisible case. These converses allow nonlinear components and predetermined time variation within the stated ordinary-forwarding architecture. Existing adaptive schemes for equal bursts approach the same rate upper bound asymptotically using time-varying convolutional codes and lie outside the non-adaptive setting considered here.
Quantum Preparation without Disturbance: Information Costs and Hypothesis Testing
Pablo Costa Rico; Robert Salzmann; Mario Berta; Ángela Capel

We determine the minimum information cost of preparing either of two quantum states with one common device while preserving its memory. Measured by the Umegaki relative entropy between the two possible memory states, this minimum is the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy of the target states. If the memory may instead be consumed, the minimum is their Umegaki relative entropy. More generally, for any divergence satisfying data processing, memory preservation selects the maximal extension of its classical restriction. We also study the cost of requiring only finitely many outputs, with the costs increasing from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy as the number of outputs grows. Finally, we consider hypothesis testing of an unknown device over independent runs. The optimal Stein exponent per run converges to the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy whenever the number of outputs per run diverges. This gives an operational characterization of the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy in quantum statistics.
On the Construction of New Families of Distance Equienergetic Graphs

For a graph $G$ with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_{i}:1\leq i \leq p\}$ and edge set $E(G)=\{e_{j}:1\leq j \leq q\},$ its subdivision graph $S_G$ is generalized to $S_{G}(n,m),$ by replacing each vertex $v_{i}$ with $n$ vertices and each edge-vertex $e_{j}$ with $m$ vertices, with each copy having the same neighbors as the vertex it replaces. Building on this construction, we define the generalized subdivision vertex join $S_{G_{1}}(n,m)\dot{\vee} G_{2}$ and the generalized subdivision edge join $S_{G}(n,m)\veebar G_{2},$ which extend the known subdivision vertex and subdivision edge join of graphs. In this paper, we determine the distance spectrum of $S_{G_{1}}(n,n)\dot{\vee} G_{2}$ and $S_{G}(n,n)\veebar G_{2},$ when $G_{1}$ and $G_{2}$ are regular graphs. As an application, we construct new families of $D$-cospectral graphs and $D$-equienergetic graphs of diameter $4.$

Andrews and Newman \cite{AN1} introduced the minimal excludant (mex) of an integer partition, and Aricheta and Donato \cite{AD} extended it to overpartitions. More recently, Meher \cite{Meher} and Tejash, Bhowmick and Meher \cite{TBM} studied the analogous statistic for $\ell$-regular partitions. In this article, for an integer $\ell\ge 2$, we define the minimal excludant $\omex_\ell(π)$ of an $\ell$-regular overpartition $π$ as the smallest positive integer that is not divisible by $\ell$ and does not occur as a non-overlined part of $π$. We study $\sm{\ell}(n)$, the sum of $\omex_\ell(π)$ over all $\ell$-regular overpartitions $π$ of $n$. We obtain generating functions for $\sm{\ell}(n)$ as eta-quotients for $\ell=2$ and $\ell=3$. Later, motivated from \cite{TBM}, we obtained explicit generating functions for $\sm{\ell}(n)$. We show that $\sm{\ell}(n)$ is weakly increasing in $n$, and we derive Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $\sm{2}(n)$ and $\sm{3}(n)$. We then determine the parity of both functions completely: $\sm{2}(n)$ is even for every $n\ge 1$, while $\sm{3}(n)$ is odd if and only if $n=0$ or $n$ is a centred hexagonal number. Also, we obtain for every $\ell\ge3$, $\sm{\ell}(n)$ is odd for infinitely many $n$, and the number of such $n\le X$ is $\gg\sqrt{X}$. Finally, we establish congruences for these functions modulo $3$, $4$ and $8$.
Muon Attains $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ Iteration Complexity under Shuffling
Kun Huang; Shi Pu; Karl Henrik Johansson

Muon is a stochastic first-order optimizer for matrix-valued parameters. It maintains an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients in a momentum buffer with coefficient $β$, and orthogonalizes the buffer to obtain the update direction. Muon has been reported to accelerate and stabilize the training of large language models. In practice, it is often used with shuffling (sampling without replacement), where each epoch visits the components of a finite-sum objective in a permuted order. However, its iteration complexity in this setting remains open. We analyze Muon under shuffling, with the momentum buffer orthogonalized by the polar map. For smooth nonconvex finite-sum problems, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ iteration complexity for finding an $\varepsilon$-stationary point. This guarantee holds for every sequence of permutations, covering random reshuffling, shuffle once, and the incremental gradient method. This complexity matches that of stochastic gradient descent under shuffling in its dependence on $\varepsilon$, and improves on Muon's $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ complexity under sampling with replacement. Our guarantee requires a problem-dependent $β$ that approaches one as the number of components grows. In contrast, no fixed $β$ guarantees convergence to stationarity for every number of components. We show this by constructing a family of smooth convex problems on which, for any fixed $β\in[0,1)$, Muon remains bounded away from stationarity once the number of components is sufficiently large. This failure occurs for every sequence of permutations and persists even with small stepsizes. These results suggest two practical tuning rules: if the training loss stops decreasing even after reducing the stepsize, increase $β$; when increasing $β$, reduce the stepsize accordingly.
On the spectrality of non-homogeneous self-similar measures

We develop a finite-cylinder difference-set obstruction to the existence of an exponential orthonormal basis for a compactly supported probability measure. This obstruction uses the equal-scale and equal-mass structure of finitely many disjoint affine copies of the measure, together with Parseval's identity and an elementary atom bound for positive measures. We apply it to prove that the golden-mean self-similar measure generated by $x/2$ and $(x+2)/4$ is non-spectral. Together with a weight-rigidity argument, this excludes spectrality for every positive choice of weights in this iterated function system. We also analyze a logarithmically incommensurable example generated by $x/2$ and $(x+2)/3$, proving non-spectrality for all first-branch weights $p\in[1/3,5/6]$, including the natural weights. The latter proof reduces to two finite, exactly checkable integer difference-set conditions; an independent verification program is included in the paper.
Singularly embedded solitons and Stokes phenomenon in the fifth order KdV equation
Roberto Barrio; Vassili Gelfreich; J. Tomás Lázaro; Juan Ramon Pacha

We study embedded solitons (ES) in a fifth-order Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation near a reversible Hamiltonian saddle-centre bifurcation. The solitons correspond to homoclinic orbits to an equilibrium whose linearisation has a pair of real and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. Existence of symmetric homoclinic near the bifurcation is a codimension-one phenomenon governed by a parameter-dependent Stokes constant associated with an inner equation. Using complex matching, we derive an oscillatory large-parameter asymptotic formula for the Stokes constant. This formula implies the existence of a countable sequence of zeros and gives their asymptotic distribution in parameter space. We also develop two complementary high-precision numerical procedures for evaluating the Stokes constant: one based on the late terms of the formal inner expansion and another on direct computation of the stable and unstable manifolds. The numerical results agree with each other and with the asymptotic prediction, confirming both the existence and the predicted locations of the embedded-soliton branches.
Training-point consistency of kernel ridge regression with varying correlation scales
Weiyan Mu; Shifeng Xiong; Yuming Shen

The scale parameter in kernel ridge regression plays a pivotal role in modeling the correlation structure of data. In modern applications, sampling density and the underlying correlation range often change simultaneously, making a fixed-scale assumption highly restrictive. However, establishing asymptotic theories under varying scale parameters is fundamentally challenging. To address this gap, this paper develops a unified theoretical framework for kernel ridge regression under varying scale parameters. We establish that, on uniform tensor grids with product exponential kernels, the consistency of the training-point risk holds if and only if the effective local sample size diverges to infinity. This sharp criterion universally covers all regimes along arbitrary deterministic scale sequences, seamlessly unifying the long-range, fixed-scale, and short-range. Furthermore, we provide an explicit, signal-independent construction of a deterministic regularization penalty that guarantees this consistency. Numerical experiments illustrate the criterion and the corresponding penalty across all the three regimes.
Controllability-Informed Distributed Electric Propulsion Aircraft Design Using Probabilistic Attainable Moment Sets
Umut Demir; Torbjørn Cunis; Aamir Ahmad; Walter Fichter

Integrated aircraft design combines models of aerodynamics, propulsion, mass, and mission performance in one design loop, so that the disciplines can be traded against each other from the earliest stage. For configurations with distributed electric propulsion (DEP), part of the control authority comes from the propulsion system itself, which directly affects the required size of the tail and should therefore be known while the aircraft is being sized. This paper presents a controllability measure that is evaluated for every design in the loop and returned to it as a design signal. The attainable moment set of each candidate design is computed from the surrugate models of the loop and it is compared with a required moment set. Since the low-fidelity surrugate models are uncertain, the comparison is formulated with probabilistic attainable moment sets: the uncertainty is propagated to the boundary of the set, which yields a margin for every direction in the moment space and the probability of violating the requirement. The design loop thereby informed whether a configuration provides sufficient control authority, on which axes it falls short, and how this changes with the design variables. The approach is demonstrated on a DEP regional aircraft, where the signal is used to assess the size of the vertical tail.
Bound-preserving finite volume scheme for a coupled parabolic system with nonlinear and nonlocal drift

We propose a bound preserving finite-volume scheme for a coupled system of partial differential equations with nonlinear, nonlocal drift. The main contribution of this work is twofold: $(1)$ we show that the proposed scheme preserves physically motivated bounds; $(2)$ we prove that the scheme is well-posed and leads to a sequence of approximate solutions converging to the weak solution of the original problem. This setting is motivated by questions related to morphology formation in organic solar cells.
On the convergence of the False Nearest Neighbours algorithm

The False Nearest Neighbours (FNN) algorithm is one of the most widely used methods for choosing the embedding dimension, i.e. the number $k$ of delay coordinates, in the time-delay reconstruction of a dynamical system from an observed scalar time series. We prove rigorous results on the behaviour of this algorithm for long time series. We consider a smooth dynamical system on a compact manifold $M$ and an invariant probability measure $μ$. For a typical measurement function and $μ$-almost every trajectory, we show that the proportion of false nearest neighbours tends to zero (provided that the tolerance threshold is large enough) once $k >\dim M$. On the other hand, for systems with super-polynomial decay of correlations, we prove that this proportion tends to one whenever $k$ is smaller than the Hausdorff dimension of $μ$. Consequently, in this case, the FNN algorithm (run for long enough time series) returns an embedding dimension $k$ satisfying $\dim_H μ\leq k \leq \dim M + 1$. This is below the threshold $2\dim M + 1$ required by the Takens embedding theorem, so the classical Takens embedding theory does not explain why reconstructions and predictions with $k$ chosen by the FNN algorithm work in practice. The explanation for this case is provided by a recent probabilistic theory of time-delay embeddings. We apply our results to the Hénon and Lorenz attractors, showing that the FNN algorithm typically returns $k=2$ for the Hénon map (in the chaotic case) and $k \leq 3$ for the Lorenz system.
Separability defects in artificial satellite theory: intermediaries, zonal harmonics and secular separatrices

A five-input Poisson-bracket operator, which reproduces the Levi-Civita separability expressions and is cubic in the Hamiltonian, is used as a diagnostic of artificial satellite theory, in a modified polar-nodal chart regular at prograde equatorial orbits. For the general intermediary proposed by the author in 2020, covering those of Sterne, Garfinkel, Brouwer, Aksnes, Cid and Lahulla and Deprit, the linearised defects vanish if and only if the integrability ansatz holds, the condition for additive first-order Hamilton-Jacobi separation in polar-nodal variables. Second-order defects follow in closed form, and the coupling with the nodal pair comes from the dependence on the physical latitude, shared by the zonal term, Aksnes's intermediary and the originals of Sterne and Garfinkel. For every axisymmetric field the radial defect is linear, with a torque form, and the first-order zonal defect is the operator response to the first-order Lie generator, which also gives the second-order mean radial defect per revolution. In its gauge the long-period second-order average is common to intermediaries without latitude terms. Oblate structures with a displaced centre separate the zonal field exactly if and only if its coefficients satisfy the recurrence of Vinti's translated spheroidal potential, and along orbits propagated over 300 periods in the field truncated at $J_4$ they conserve the approximate third integral better than the centred structure, by median factors of 23 to 77. On secular separatrices the integrated defect is the derivative of the Melnikov function, tested in the eccentric Kozai-Lidov problem, and transverse zero sets of the operator define event surfaces.
High-order IMEX local discontinuous Galerkin methods with sparse grids for high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs
Joel P. Villarino; Manuel J. Castro; J. A. García-Rodríguez; J. G. López-Salas

In this work, we develop a high-order IMEX-LDG scheme on sparse grids for solving nonlinear parabolic PDEs in moderate to high dimensions. The method combines the advantages of LDG methods for convection--diffusion problems, IMEX-RK time integrators for stiff systems, and sparse-grid techniques to mitigate the curse of dimensionality. The resulting scheme is fully parallelized in MPI, is robust, efficient, and scalable, making it suitable for a wide range of applications involving high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs.
Upper bounds for the number of spanning forests of a graph
Tingzeng Wu; Shuxin Lu; Xiangshuai Dong

Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $F(G)$ denote the number of spanning forests of $G$. Bencs and Csikvári proved that every $r$-regular graph $G$ with $r\ge 2$ satisfies $F(G)\le r^n$. Motivated by this result, they conjectured that if $G$ has minimum degree at least $3$, then $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$, where $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n)$ is the degree sequence of $G$. In this paper, we prove that graphs with minimum degree at least $n/3$ $(n\geq7)$ satisfy $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$. We also construct a counterexample to the conjecture. We therefore further study the enumeration of spanning forests in general graphs, proving an upper bound in terms of the degree sequence and characterizing the extremal graphs attaining this bound. In addition, using the matrix-forest theorem, we obtain an upper bound for the number of spanning forests of a connected graph in terms of its algebraic connectivity, and characterize the extremal graphs attaining this bound.
Stochastic inverse source problem in inhomogeneous media: far-field statistics
Dong Qiu; Xiang Xu; Yue Zhao

This paper is concerned with an inverse random source problem for the stochastic Helmholtz equation in a known three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is driven by spatial white noise. We seek to recover its mean and strength from the mean and cross-frequency covariance of the far-field pattern. For a smooth nontrapping wave speed, we use the spectral measure of the acoustic operator to relate the far-field data to the source statistics. Under a priori regularity bounds, this relation gives conditional stability for the source mean and the source strength. We derive explicit reconstruction formulas for both quantities and bound the errors due to frequency truncation and data perturbations. We also obtain mean-square error bounds for reconstructions from finitely many independent experiments. Numerical experiments illustrate the reconstruction accuracy and the effects of bandwidth and sample size.
A Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition Method for Single-Temperature Gas Mixtures
Domenico Caparello; Lorenzo Pareschi; Thomas Rey

This paper introduces a domain-adaptive numerical method for multi-species kinetic models that relax toward a single-temperature and single-velocity hydrodynamic limit. To this end, we derive moment realizability matrices for this regime. In this way the ideas of Levermore, Morokoff, and Nadiga are extended to non-equilibrium mixtures in which inter-species and intra-species collisions occur at comparable rates, so that all species relax to a common velocity and a common temperature. The realizability conditions are used as an indicator to divide the computational domain, at each time step, into macroscopic and kinetic regions. In the kinetic regions, where the continuum description fails (e.g., across strong shocks, non-equilibrium interfaces, or kinetic boundary layers), the method solves the multi-species kinetic equations. Close to local thermodynamic equilibrium, the Euler equations of the mixture are solved instead. Confining the kinetic computations to the non-equilibrium regions reduces the simulation time, while the results remain close to those of the full kinetic solver. The method is discretized on Cartesian grids with high-order schemes in space and time. The kinetic equations are integrated with an Asymptotic-Preserving Implicit-Explicit (IMEX) scheme, so that a consistent discretization of the single-velocity, single-temperature Euler system of the mixture is recovered when the Knudsen number goes to zero. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first realizability-based adaptive spatial domain decomposition method for gas mixtures in this single-velocity, single-temperature setting.
Strong endpoint estimates for bilinear spherical averaging operators on closed hypersurfaces and curved patches

Tainara Borges~\cite[Section~7.1, Question~7.2]{Borges2026} asked whether the strong $L^1\times L^1\to L^{1/2}$ estimate for bilinear spherical averages extends to all compact smooth hypersurfaces without boundary and with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We give a positive answer when $d\ge2$. The geometric argument concerns the difference projection $(y,z)\mapsto y-z$: at every critical point, two definite directions in its fiber already ensure that the projected surface measure has bounded density. This condition holds for the closed hypersurfaces in the original question. The ensuing strong endpoint uses the localization principle of Iosevich, Palsson and Sovine~\cite[Propositions~4.1--4.2]{IPS2022}. Our proof also establishes a partial positive result for the curvature-rank problem in Borges~\cite[Question~7.1]{Borges2026}. We exhibit a smooth full-curvature patch with boundary for which the strong estimate fails. The endpoint yields the entire fixed-scale Hölder family.

Let $(Γ,+)$ be a finite Abelian group and let $g\inΓ\setminus\{0\}$. A partition of $Γ$ is called $g$-compatible if no part contains both $x$ and $x+g$. For a prescribed involution $h$ and odd $r\ge3$, we prove that $Γ$ admits an $h$-compatible partition into zero-sum $r$-element sets if and only if $r$ divides $|Γ|$ and $Γ$ has at least three involutions. Moreover, the partition can be chosen so that the multigraph whose vertices are its parts and whose edges are the pairs $\{x,x+h\}$ is Hamiltonian and has a proper edge coloring with $r$ colors. We also give examples, for groups of odd order and for even block sizes, in which zero-sum partitions exist but compatible ones do not. We give two applications of these partitions. For block size three, we obtain complete mappings whose cycles are precisely the parts of the partition. We also construct Hamiltonian $r$-regular $Γ$-distance-magic graphs admitting $0$ and every involution of $Γ$ as magic constants.
Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph

In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation $\E[Y|X]$, where $X$ is the observed path and $Y$ is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signature kernel and the response, we provide finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the method. We supplement our theoretical analysis with numerical experiments that illustrate our results.
A solution to Petty's polar projection problem

In 1971, Petty asked whether a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geqslant 3$, must be an ellipsoid if its projection body is a dilate of its polar. In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to this question.
High-Dimensional Gaussian and Bootstrap Approximation: Near $1/\sqrt{n}$ Rates with General Covariance

We consider Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of $n$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$ that are i.i.d. A longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics is whether bounds of order $1/\sqrt n$ are attainable up to factors of $\log(pn)$ when the population covariance matrix is unrestricted. We answer this question affirmatively, provided that the random vectors have sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance. In addition, we provide analogous results for bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison, which make use of a special discrepancy measure between covariance matrices that enables improvement with respect to prior work. Taking an approach based on interpolation, the novel aspects of the proofs deal with bounding the interpolation derivatives in a way that is not sensitive to the covariance structure.
Existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions to semilinear elliptic problems on the exterior of a unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$

We study the problem \begin{equation}\notag \begin{cases} - Δu &= λK(x) f(u) \hspace{.1cm} \mbox { in } B_1 ^c, \\ u(x)&=0 \hspace{1.5cm} \mbox { on } \partial B_1, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $λ$ is a positive parameter, $B_1^c:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:|x|>1\}$ is the exterior of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $K:B_1^c\rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a $C^1$ radial function and $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a $C^1$ concave function which is sublinear at infinity such that $f(0)<0$. We establish the existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions for large values of parameter $λ$. Moreover, we prove certain qualitative properties of nonnegative radial solutions for a class of problems in dimension 2. In contrast to the case $n\geq3$, where positive solutions decay to zero at infinity, we prove that non negative solutions are positive, radially increasing with the limit existing at infinity.
The speed of convergence for propagation of chaos in the mean-field Ising model
Jonas Jalowy; Matthias Löwe; Sara Terveer

We derive sharp relative-entropy asymptotics for increasing propagation of chaos in the Curie--Weiss model at zero external field. For every fixed inverse temperature $0<β<1$, the relative entropy of a $k$-spin marginal with respect to the symmetric product measure is $$ \frac{β^2}{4(1-β)^2}\frac{k(k-1)}{N^2}+o\left(\frac{k^2}{N^2}\right),\qquad k=o(N). $$ At the critical inverse temperature $β=1$, the rate changes to $α_{\mathrm c}^2 k(k-1)/(4N)+o(k^2/N)$ in the regime $k=o(\sqrt N)$, where $α_{\mathrm c}$ is the second moment of the limiting quartic law of the rescaled magnetization. We also obtain asymptotics for sequences $β_N\uparrow1$ that interpolate between these two regimes. Crucially, the proof reveals that the pair correlations determine the leading correction to the likelihood ratio, providing precise control of both the chi-square divergence and relative entropy.
Well-Posedness of Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Partial Marginal Constraints for Model Calibration
Jean-François Chassagneux; Stéphane Crépey; Grégoire Loeper; Justin Ruelland

We study the well-posedness and stability of a semimartingale optimal transport problem with partial marginal constraints at several maturities, motivated by the calibration of financial models to finitely many option prices. We connect its probabilistic and Eulerian formulations within the Benamou--Brenier framework. Under convex-duality assumptions, we establish strong duality for every price vector in the extended-value sense and existence of a primal optimizer whenever the value is finite. Under additional PDE assumptions, we establish dual attainment on the relative interior of the admissible price set, together with uniqueness of the primal optimizer. Under further non-degeneracy assumptions, we show that this price set has nonempty interior, on which the dual optimizer is unique and depends locally Lipschitz continuously on the prices. The analysis combines convex methods with regularity and local strong convexity results for Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman solution maps established in a companion paper. For a fixed deterministic initial state, we also prove continuity of the optimal law on path space in the adapted Wasserstein distance of order two as prices vary within this interior. This stability concerns the optimizer over the full admissible class of semimartingale laws, allowing characteristics that depend on the past. The framework accommodates bounded uniformly continuous payoffs, including European puts in log-price coordinates, without payoff regularization or spatial truncation.
Chow Stability of Polarized K3 Surfaces with ADE singularities

The asymptotic Chow stability of smooth polarized K3 surfaces is known through the existence of Ricci-flat metrics and Donaldson's theorem. We give a purely algebraic proof and extend the result to polarized K3 surfaces with at worst ADE singularities. The proof gives a uniform effective bound for the exponent, depending only on the degree of the polarization. Following the approach of Mumford and Morrison, we establish quantitative estimates for linear systems and their contributions to Chow weights, without restrictions on the Picard number.

We study $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano threefolds of Fano index greater than $1$ whose Weil divisor class group has nontrivial torsion. We give a complete list of their possible numerical types: there are $176$ of them, which refine to $182$ possible graded Hilbert series. At least $40$ numerical types are realised: $27$ by quotients of weighted complete intersections by cyclic groups, twelve by quotients of threefolds of codimension $4$ or $5$ and one by a quotient of the del Pezzo threefold of degree $5$. Seventy-two numerical types are shown not to occur. In particular the torsion subgroup need not have prime order, and the Weil and $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano indices can be $(1,2)$, $(1,3)$ or $(1,4)$.
Non-vanishing of central $\rm GL_3$ L-values in the level aspect

We study non-vanishing of central standard $L$-values of spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newforms of prime level. A logarithmic Möbius mollifier with finite inverse Euler factors, combined with a conjugate term from the functional equation, gives a non-vanishing harmonic proportion of at least $1/2-\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large prime levels. The required mixed moment is evaluated by an asymmetric approximate functional equation.
Goodman-type lower bounds for graph homomorphism densities

For a finite graph $H$ with $v(H)$ vertices, chromatic number $χ(H)$, and chromatic polynomial $P_H$, define $Φ_H(p)=(1-p)^{v(H)}P_H((1-p)^{-1})$. This polynomial interpolates the homomorphism densities of $H$ in balanced complete multipartite graphons. We study the lower bound $t(H,W)\geΦ_H(p)$ on the homomorphism density of $H$ in graphons $W$ of edge density $p>1-1/(χ(H)-1)$, which generalises Goodman's triangle bound. We prove the inequality for chordal graphs whose maximal cliques have equal size, for trivially perfect graphs, and for joins of a clique and an odd cycle. The proofs use entropy along clique trees and a convexity criterion for adding a universal vertex. We also prove that a nonbipartite graph satisfies the inequality at all sufficiently high edge densities if and only if its girth is odd. For a graph on $n$ vertices whose girth is odd, the bound holds whenever $p>1-(72n^{12})^{-1}$. The proof combines Whitney's forest expansion with a spectral comparison of cycle densities. Finally, among the $117$ nonbipartite graphs on at most six vertices with no isolated vertices or isolated edges, exactly $94$ satisfy the bound. The main results are formally verified in Lean 4.
HOL in HOL: mechanized soundness, completeness and consistency, with and without infinity

What can a logic certify about a copy of itself? For Church's simple theory of types, formalized as a deep embedding in Isabelle/HOL with Henkin semantics and a natural-deduction calculus, the answer has two tiers. On the first tier, plain Isabelle/HOL certifies the logic without an axiom of infinity, by a standard model with one individual. On the second tier, the logic with a Dedekind-style axiom of infinity is certified only in Isabelle/HOL extended by a large enough set-theoretic universe. Both tiers appear in Harrison's self-verification of HOL Light. What the present formalization adds is Henkin completeness, and with it a semantics that matches the calculus exactly, compactness and model existence on the first tier, and the boundary between the tiers. Comparing two ways of adding infinity to the object logic shows where the boundary lies. One is an infinite domain of individuals, expressed by the first-order sentences "there are at least $n$ individuals", each of which has a finite model; the other is the Dedekind axiom, a single sentence with no finite model, and there the first tier ends. In the calculus the axiom is strictly stronger than the sentences together: it derives each of them, but they do not derive it. The witness is a countable Henkin model in which every sentence holds and the axiom fails, because its function domain is too sparse for an injective, non-surjective self-map. On the second tier, the universe serves one purpose only: to prove the Dedekind axiom consistent. Everything that follows, completeness and even the countable Henkin model of the axiom, is obtained in plain Isabelle/HOL. The universe axiom is Harrison-style, realized in Paulson's ZFC_in_HOL with the domain of every type in $V_{ω+ω}$; with it, full classical higher-order logic with infinity and relational choice is consistent relative to set theory.
Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems

Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.
On configurations that are nearly generalised polygons
Sam Adriaensen; John Bamberg; Jason Williford

Payne (1972) introduced nearly generalised $n$-gons as $(s+1)$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $2n$ with small excess over the Moore bound. Biggs and Ito (1980) proved nonexistence of such graphs if $s > 1$ and $n > 3$, leaving open the existence of regular antipodal planes. We revisit this problem from several equivalent viewpoints. First we show that a regular antipodal plane of order $s$ is equivalent to a balanced weighing matrix whose support is the incidence matrix of a biplane with parameters \[ 2-\left(\frac{s^2+s+2}{2},\,s+1,\,2\right). \] This gives short determinant and local-arithmetic obstructions to existence. We then formulate the question of signing a biplane as an affine linear system over $\mathbb F_2$, and use this formulation to prove that no regular antipodal plane of order $s$ exists with $4\le s\le 14$. Finally, we give further equivalent formulations in terms of sharply deranged families of permutations and mutually orthogonal array-bic squares. These translations provide new computational and structural approaches to Payne's conjecture that regular antipodal planes exist only for $s=2,3$.
Extreme central $L$-values of almost prime quadratic twists of elliptic curves II

We prove lower bounds for central $L$-values of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve by discriminants with at most five prime factors. Under the rank-zero Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, these bounds give large Tate--Shafarevich groups.
Projective surfaces with infinite fundamental group and trivial profinite completion

For every nontrivial finite abelian group \(A\) of odd order, we construct a smooth complex projective surface with infinite topological fundamental group and trivial étale fundamental group. The isomorphism types of its finite subgroups are precisely those of the subgroups of \(A\). The surface is Kobayashi hyperbolic and has Stein universal cover.
A Helly theorem for the Bruhat-Tits building
Rudrendra Kashyap; Kiumars Kaveh; Christopher Manon; Boris Tsvelikhovskiy

Let $K$ be a discretely valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}$. We show that a finite family of $\mathcal{O}$-lattices in $K^m$ is adapted to a common basis if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ $\mathcal{O}$-lattices is. In other words, in the Bruhat-Tits building of $\operatorname{GL}(m)$, a finite family of simplices lies in a common apartment if and only if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ simplices does. The proof uses a version of Radon's theorem for $\mathcal{O}$-lattices. We also give an alternative proof using truncated modules.
Inequalities for intersection numbers from Hodge-Riemann relations

We derived inequalities for intersection numbers of nef classes inside algebras satisfying the Kähler package, using Hodge-Riemann relations up to degree two. As an application, we construct certain strictly Lorentzian polynomials and show that they cannot be realized as the volume polynomial of nef classes inside such an algebra.

For $a>0$ and a polynomial $F$ of degree $m$, let $H_{a,F}$ denote the weighted Euler numerator of $F$, defined as the numerator of the generating function $\sum_{k\ge0}(a)_kF(k)x^k/k!$ with denominator $(1-x)^{a+m}$. For every $a>0$, we show the following preservation result: if the numerators $H_{a,F}$ and $H_{a,G}$ have only real nonpositive zeros, then the same holds for $H_{a,FG}$. The proof relies on an explicit multiplication formula in falling-factorial coordinates and a characterization of multiplier sequences for generalized Laguerre bases due to Brändén and Ottergren. Furthermore, when the symmetric degrees coincide with the ordinary degrees of the input polynomials, the same operation preserves $γ$-positivity. For positive integers $a=r$, the weight is the Ehrhart polynomial of the standard simplex $Δ_{r-1}$. This yields geometric preservation theorems for products with a single simplex factor, as well as applications to Gorenstein polytopes and a Reeve tetrahedron example.
Contractions of realizations and differential invariants of the algebra sl(2,C)

In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincaré algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.
Scalar Entropic Damage Transport: Well-posed softening with a single damage variable
Jonas Nutz; Vikram Laheri; Matti Schneider

Entropic Damage Transport (EDT) represents material softening via a local continuum damage model while ensuring the well-posedness of the mechanical boundary value problem. It is based on a convexification of the time-incremental potential associated with a rate-limited scalar damage model. A one-dimensional distribution of damage states serves as the internal variable, and the number of these states grows with the number of time steps. We show that the emergence of the damage distribution is an artifact of the time discretization. Surprisingly, the distribution concentrates at a single damage state in the time-continuous limit, and EDT converges to a rate-limited damage model with a scalar damage variable, whose free energy is jointly convex in the strain and the reciprocal degradation. We exploit this hidden convexity by a frozen-metric discretization in terms of the reciprocal degradation, which renders every increment jointly convex. The resulting scalar update preserves damage irreversibility, the prescribed damage-rate limitation and thermomechanical consistency, reduces to a scalar equation and provides a symmetric and positive definite algorithmic tangent in closed form. Computational experiments assess the accuracy and the efficiency of both formulations from the material point to the microstructure level, and demonstrate that the scalar update permits a finite-element computation of industrial size with more than 14 million degrees of freedom.
An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping

In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.
Closed formulas for the permanents of structured matrices

We give finite formulas for permanents of structured matrices and prove polynomial bounds for their evaluation. Over any field, the permanent of a matrix of bounded rank-width can be computed from the matrix alone, answering a question of Lyaudet. In characteristic $p>0$, the bound is $p^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$, where $k$ is the rank-width. In characteristic zero, a determinant formula treats Cauchy matrices with an added polynomial of fixed degrees in the row and column nodes. This includes polynomial perturbations of Hilbert matrices and dense Toeplitz and Hankel families. For ordered cuts we give a single determinant; in positive characteristic, rational diagonal sequences give a fixed rational generating function for the Toeplitz permanents. We also give formulas for cycle weights and hook immanants. For translation matrices we obtain signed determinant formulas and classify the supports for which the permanent is the coefficientwise absolute value of the determinant. Further formulas cover cyclic block matrices, residue supports, and bands bounded on one side.
Localization for Lipschitz monotone quasi-periodic operators with power-law hopping
Hongyi Cao; Yunfeng Shi; Peizhen Wang

We prove spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators on $\mathbb Z^d$ with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping. For sufficiently small coupling, localization holds at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent $r$ exceeds the Diophantine exponent $τ$. The proof is based on multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales. We use homotopy in the coupling constant to select the local eigenvalue branches and Schur complement estimates to control the successive elimination of coordinates.
The Dirichlet Problem for Quaternionic $k$-Hessian Equations
Xi-Nan Ma; Yang Zhou; Jingyong Zhu

We study the Dirichlet problem for quaternionic $k$-Hessian equations on smooth bounded domains. For a smooth positive density $f(q,z)$ satisfying $f_z\ge0$, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth admissible solution whenever a smooth admissible subsolution with the prescribed boundary values exists. The proof extends the quaternionic Monge--Ampère subsolution method to $2\le k<n$ through boundary second derivative estimates. We also construct subsolutions on strictly quaternionic $(k-1)$-convex domains and characterize smooth solvability for constant boundary values.
Domains of attraction of quasi-stationary distributions for an absorbed random walk

We study a continuous-time random walk on the positive integers, killed at zero, where the downward rate $a$ and upward rate $b$ satisfy $a>b>0$. Its quasi-stationary distributions form a one-parameter family. We show that if the initial distribution $(m_n)_{n\geq 1}$ is strictly positive and satisfies $m_{n+1}/m_n\to r$, where $(b/a)^{1/2}<r<1$, then its conditional distribution given survival converges in total variation to the corresponding nonminimal quasi-stationary distribution. We obtain asymptotic equivalents for the joint probabilities of position and survival, and for the survival probability itself. We also give a moment condition under which the minimal quasi-stationary distribution is selected. Finally, we construct an initial distribution whose successive-term ratios do not converge but whose conditional distribution nevertheless converges to a nonminimal quasi-stationary distribution. Thus the ratio condition is sufficient but not necessary.
Entire curves in surface bundles over tori

Cattalani recently initiated the study of Ahlfors currents in symplectic topology. We combine these with the symplectic pairs of Bande-Kotschick to show that some non-trivial surface bundles over tori have pseudoholomorphic entire curves. In particular the Kodaira-Thurston manifold has an entire curve for every $J$ tamed by an invariant form.
Exceptional sequences of line bundles on $\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)$

Let $X_\ell=\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)\subset\mathbb{P}^\ell\times(\mathbb{P}^\ell)^\vee$ be the incidence variety of points and hyperplanes in $\mathbb{P}^\ell$. We prove that for every $\ell\ge 3$, every exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ of maximal length $\ell(\ell+1)=\operatorname{rk} K_0(X_\ell)$ is full. Together with the case $\ell=2$, due to Altmann, Hochenegger and Witt, this shows that for all $\ell\ge2$ an exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ is full if and only if it has maximal length. The proof translates exceptionality into a combinatorial condition on lattice points of $\operatorname{Pic}(X_\ell)\cong\mathbb{Z}^2$ and reduces fullness to sequences containing a non-orthogonal descent. A capacity count for admissibly ordered subsets rules out all but one family of descents; for that family we classify the possible configurations and verify generation using Euler sequences and Koszul complexes.
Compatible by Construction: Bottom-Up Nonlinear Model Reduction without Interface Bases

Nonlinear manifolds can provide compact representations of solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs), but generating training data and learning these representations on large domains remain costly. We present a bottom-up framework that reuses local nonlinear representations learned on a small training domain to solve larger PDE systems. A shared nonlinear decoder represents the full set of degrees of freedom owned by each subdomain, without separate interior and interface models. Each global degree of freedom has a unique owner, and local residuals directly use decoded state values from the corresponding neighboring subdomains. The resulting discrete state is single-valued by construction, eliminating the need for independent interface copies and additional interface compatibility constraints. Physical coupling is retained through the original time-discrete PDE residual. With the decoder held fixed, the subdomain-specific reduced coordinates are determined jointly by minimizing this residual, and the Gauss--Newton system is assembled from local contributions. Experiments on parameterized viscous Burgers and incompressible Navier--Stokes problems demonstrate reuse on larger domains without retraining. Comparisons with local proper orthogonal decomposition models under the same coupling construction show favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-offs in the tested regimes.
Toward the Minimal Set of Information Inequalities in Regenerating Codes: An Algebraic Approach
Rui-Juan Jing; Laigang Guo; Yan-Feng Xie; Chun-Ming Yuan

Information-theoretic outer bounds for exact-repair regenerating codes can be formulated as linear programs, but the associated Shannon-type systems contain many implicit equalities and redundant inequalities. We directly specify a reduced system for the $(n,n-1,n-1)$ exact-repair model using the closure structure induced by its repair dependencies. Nonempty closed sets index the reduced joint-entropy coordinates, and inseparable edges determine the defining inequalities. We prove equivalence with the initial system by characterizing its implicit equalities and establishing sufficient redundancy criteria. We also give an algorithm that constructs the directly defined system for any $n$, count its entropy coordinates, and derive an explicitly computable upper bound on its number of inequalities. For every $n\ge2$, we prove that the reduced system has no implicit equalities and that each distinct defining inequality is nonredundant and defines a facet in the nonempty closed-set coordinate space. Exact enumerations for $n\in\{2,3,4,5\}$ verify the reported system sizes.
Rational lines on pairs of quadrics and cubic hypersurfaces
Tim Browning; Stephanie Chan; Nick Rome

We study rational lines on smooth intersections of two quadrics and on smooth cubic hypersurfaces over number fields. For an intersection of two quadrics in $n$ variables, we prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation for the variety of lines when $n\geq 11$, and more generally for the variety of $r$-planes when $n\geq 3r+8$. In this range an $r$-plane exists over the ground field if and only if one exists over every real completion. For the variety of lines, we also prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation when $n\geq 8$, conditional on the finiteness of certain Tate-Shafarevich groups. For a smooth cubic hypersurface in $n$ variables, we prove that a line exists over the ground field when $n\geq 23$.
Convergence analysis of physics-informed neural networks for subdiffusion
Bangti Jin; Qiqi Rao; Zhi Zhou

Physics-informed neural networks have emerged as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations, yet their rigorous convergence theory for time-fractional problems remains limited. We present a convergence analysis of PINNs for linear subdiffusion equations and for the associated backward problem of recovering the initial data from terminal observations. To address the nonlocality and weakly singular kernels of fractional derivatives, we introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on some popular time-stepping schemes satisfying discrete maximal regularity, including backward Euler, BDF2, L1, and fractional CN schemes. This approach avoids the exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while preserving the stability structure needed for convergence analysis. For the forward problem, we prove that, under the natural fractional maximal-regularity condition $u\in W^{α,p}(0,T;L^2(Ω))\cap L^p(0,T;H^2(Ω)\cap H_0^1(Ω))$, the piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution. This result avoids the higher-order regularity assumptions on the exact solution that are often imposed in existing PINN convergence analyses. We also verify the required discrete maximal regularity and consistency properties for the aforementioned popular time discretizations. We then extend the analysis to the backward subdiffusion problem and establish convergence of the regularized recovery of the initial data from terminal observations, despite its ill-posedness. Numerical experiments for both forward and backward problems support the theoretical results, demonstrate the necessity of regularization, and show that $L^2$-type losses alone are generally insufficient. These results establish a rigorous theoretical basis for discretization-based PINNs for time-fractional diffusion problems.
One-bubble stability, reduced coefficients, and threshold compactness for the Escobar functional

Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact manifold with nonempty boundary and coercive conformal energy. For $n\ge5$, in a conformal representative with $H_g=0$, we prove quantitative stability near a concentrating boundary bubble whose center stays away from the umbilic locus. The norm of the constrained gradient controls the distance to the standard bubble family with sharp exponent $1/2$, and the distance to the Lyapunov--Schmidt corrected family linearly. In the same one-bubble neighborhood, at energies at least the sharp hemisphere value $S_\ast$, the distance to the standard family is also controlled linearly. These estimates follow from the exact reduced quadratic coefficient and the scale-derivative expansion of the reduced functional. The same scale equation shows that sequences of critical points at $S_\ast$ can concentrate only at umbilic points. For $n\ge3$, a profile decomposition without a sign assumption gives Palais--Smale compactness between $S_\ast$ and the first mixed level $(S_\ast^{n-1}+Y^{n-1})^{1/(n-1)}$, where $Y=C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)$, and this endpoint is sharp. Between $S_\ast$ and the two-bubble level, we characterize noncompact levels by the lower critical values. For $n\ge7$, we obtain the fourth-order reduced expansion at umbilic centers. Under local total umbilicity, we evaluate the correction exactly, determine the conformal weight of the reduced coefficient, and obtain the optimal algebraic comparison with the squared ambient Weyl norm.
Exponential Double and Multiple Riordan Arrays as Fiber Products

A double Riordan array has nonzero entries only in positions $(n,k)$ with $n+k$ even, and its even and odd parts are Riordan arrays with the same multiplier function.
