As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional operator coefficients.
PF-Exec: Large-Scale UAV Relay Load Balancing with an Anchored Potential Direction Decider and a Per-Dimension Gain-Learning Executor
Liheng Zeng; Hanzhang Jia; Yiran Li; Yi Gao; Bo Ma

Relay load balancing in large-scale UAV networks requires joint decisions on association, bandwidth, power and hovering position, while the dimension grows with the number of UAVs and each UAV sees only its local state. This paper splits the decision into two layers. An anchored potential direction decider emits a closed-form target at every instant and returns its direction only. A gain-learning executor maps a local observation into a positive gain per dimension, composes gain and target, and clips the action against the physical single-step bound; the two layers form PF-Exec. The unit gain is the default start, so the executor reduces to the pure potential policy before training. The load is first-order homogeneous in bandwidth, making the bandwidth target closed form, and the position target is the demand-weighted centroid of the served users. The system uses a two-hop access and millimetre-wave backhaul link with soft association, a 3GPP UMa-AV channel with two shadowing layers, an OU-type social-force crowd and a quadrotor physical layer. Evaluation spans all fleet sizes, two crowd scenarios, independent seeds, the published baselines in their own settings and a degraded-information line. In the highest-pressure burst setting the fixed-step comparison breaks down on part of the seeds, losing fairness and mean load at once, while PF-Exec holds fairness near one. Among the ten comparison methods only the greedy heuristic survives that setting; its load variance stays far higher. Under stale global state and position noise the fairness index stays high at both largest-scale scenarios. Flight energy is nearly identical between the learned and the fixed-step executor, and three constants are fixed once across all settings. The convergence properties of both layers, from the truncated gain iteration to the perturbed tracking bound, are proved in the companion analysis.
A graph discretization of the Steklov and Neumann problems on domains in complete Riemannian manifolds

We establish quantitative spectral convergence for graph discretizations of the Steklov and Neumann problems for bounded domains in complete Riemannian manifolds. Our construction uses weighted proximity graphs built from maximal $ε$-separated sets, with a correction to the discrete energy accounting for the geometry near the boundary. We consider two discrete Steklov problems: one defined using an averaged boundary trace, and the other using restriction to boundary vertices. Both approximate the continuum Steklov spectrum, but under different conditions on the discretization parameters. The additional scale condition required for the restriction-based problem is also necessary for spectral convergence. As a byproduct, we obtain quantitative convergence of the Neumann spectrum. The estimates are uniform under suitable geometric bounds.

A copy of a hypergraph $F$ is called an $F$-copy. For any integers $k$ and $r$ with $2 \leq r \leq k$, let $K_k^r$ denote the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph whose vertex set is $[k] = \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ (that is, the edges of $K_k^r$ are the $r$-element subsets of $[k]$). Given an $r$-uniform $m$-edge hypergraph $H$, the $K_k^r$-isolation number of $H$, denoted by $ι(H, K_k^r)$, is the size of a smallest subset $D$ of the vertex set of $H$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $K_k^r$-copies contained by $H$ (equivalently, $H-N[D]$ contains no $K_k^r$-copy). We prove that if $H$ is connected and not a $K_k^r$-copy, then $$ι(H, K^r_k) \le \left \lfloor \frac{(r-1)m + 1}{(r-1)(\binom{k}{r}+1) + 1} \right \rfloor.$$ The bound is best possible. This is a solution to a problem of Li, Zhang and Ye. We also provide an alternative proof for $r < k$. Both proofs introduce new ideas for establishing bounds on isolation parameters.
Convergence Properties of PF-Exec: Homogeneous Structure, Anchored Closed Form, and Gain Dynamics
Hanzhang Jia; Liheng Zeng; Yiran Li; Yi Gao; Bo Ma

This paper establishes a layered mathematical char acterisation of PF-Exec, the algorithm of the companion system paper. Demand-proportional bandwidth allocation yields an exact first-order homogeneous decomposition, from which the equal-load bandwidth target and its feasibility bound follow in closed form. The logarithmic knee view preserves strict load order and shares its global optimum with the Jain fairness index, while the demand-weighted centroid minimises the position potential. The damped softmax association block possesses a fixed point on the product of simplices. The truncated one-dimensional gain iteration admits a complete characterisation, with geomet ric convergence below the critical gain, initial-value-dependent bounded oscillation at it, and a family of bounded two-state cycles above it. A global invariant error ball and an explicit tracking recursion complete the execution guarantee. A numerical audit confirms the structural identities on every measured state and quantifies the local amplification of the coupled association and resource dynamics. Together, the results explain how closed form recovery directions and bounded adaptive gains provide stable execution without requiring a global Euclidean contraction assumption.
Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
Shuzhou Wang; Zhenhua Wang; Matthew Zediker

Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology. We characterize quantum fundamental groups for a wide class of examples, including $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We show that these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces with finite fundamental groups that are either non-abelian or of non prime order.
SURFACE: Preference Distribution Matching on Pareto Fronts via Scalarization Steering
Liuyuan Jiang; Prasanna Sattigeri; Lisha Chen

Constructing a finite Pareto representation requires allocating a limited number of solutions across the Pareto front (PF). A desired preference distribution specifies this allocation by assigning more solutions to some PF regions and fewer to others. Scalarization generates Pareto solutions by varying objective weights and solving single-objective problems. However, a distribution of scalarization weights generally does not translate into the same distribution of Pareto solutions along the PF, because the weight-to-solution map is nonlinear and unknown in advance.To account for this distortion, we introduce SURFACE (Scalarization Updates for Redistributing Finite Approximations with Chart Estimation}), which adaptively updates scalarization weights to match a desired PF distribution. SURFACE estimates how each region of the weight grid corresponds to an area of the PF from the current scalarized solutions, then redistributes the weights accordingly. The method supports parallel, warm-started, inexact optimization with standard single-objective solvers. Theoretically, we establish that, under the stated regularity conditions, SURFACE achieves linear convergence of the preference distribution mismatch to a finite-resolution error floor of $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2/(M-1)})$, where $N$ is the number of adaptive weights and $M$ is the number of objectives. Empirically, experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate improved target-mass balance and PF coverage compared with established baselines.
On discrete harmonic functions with non-negativity on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$
José Gaitan Montejo; Carlos Garzón; José Madrid

An improvement of Liouville's theorem for discrete harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ was obtained by Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin. Namely, they proved that if a discrete harmonic function is bounded on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, then the function is constant. In this paper, we study the corresponding problem if we replace the boundedness assumption with non-negativity. We establish this non-negativity result in some classes of discrete harmonic functions (polynomial growth and finite-translation-rank). Moreover, we prove that if a discrete harmonic function is non-negative on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, then it has at most exponential growth.
First-order characterizations of strong quasiconvexity with the exact modulus
John Matos Ascona; Jackeline C. Huaccha Neyra; Lizet Santa Cruz Calderón; Heraclio López-Lázaro

In this paper, we study first-order characterizations of strong quasiconvexity for functions defined on convex subsets of real normed spaces. For functions that are continuous along segments, an inequality involving the lower Dini derivative is a known necessary condition for strong quasiconvexity with a given modulus, whereas the established converse guarantees only half of that modulus. By means of a one-dimensional lemma, we prove that this inequality, and even its weaker version with the upper Dini derivative, ensures strong quasiconvexity with the same modulus, without requiring the domain to be open; this answers a question raised in the recent literature. The main result leads to a characterization with the same modulus in terms of the Clarke subdifferential for locally Lipschitz functions on Banach spaces, which answers another open question, and to a formula for the exact modulus of radial functions defined on Hilbert spaces. We also present some consequences in optimization, such as an optimality condition without Clarke regularity, an error bound with optimal constant and, for the projected subgradient method, the same convergence rate as in the strongly convex case, together with the exponential convergence of the associated flow. Finally, we show that the converse of a relation between proximal points and strong subdifferentials fails in general, but holds for a truncation of the function.
Ozone groups and fixed rings of double Ore extensions

We determine centers of two families of four-dimensional double Ore extensions without torsion assumptions, restricting to $f\ne0$ in $\mathcal O$. On the PI locus of $\mathcal K$, we classify the ozone groups and obtain normal commutative fixed rings of generic degree two over the center, including a nonmonogenic example. For an odd-torsion subfamily of $\mathcal O$, independent odd orders $n\geq1,m>1$ yield ozone group $C_n^2\times C_2^2$, PI degree $2nm$ and fixed-algebra PI degree $m$, with unchanged center. A PI specialization of $\mathcal G$ has trivial ozone group.
Forcing global $Π^2_n$ uniformization with or without projective determinacy

We construct a set-forcing extension of $L$ which has the same reals as $L$ and satisfies the $Π^2_n$-uniformization property for every $n\geq1$. Assuming $ω$ Woodin cardinals and a measurable cardinal above them, we also obtain a forcing extension of $L(\mathbb R)^{M_ω}$ which has the same reals and satisfies projective determinacy together with the $Π^2_n$-uniformization property for every $n\geq1$.
CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes, Bipodality and the Parallel Wall Property

Coxeter cell complexes are a simultaneous generalization to cube complexes and the Davis complex of a Coxeter group. We show that 1-skeleta of CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes isometrically embed into a CAT(0) cube complex. When the resulting cube complex is finite dimensional, we show that the condition of bipodality (satisfied by both CAT(0) cube complexes and Davis complexes of Coxeter groups) implies local finiteness of the cubulation. To this end, we show a Parallel Wall Theorem for bipodal CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes satisfying a uniform bound on the size of a collection of pairwise intersecting walls. In particular, our methods give a new, purely geometric proof of the Parallel Wall Theorem for Coxeter groups.
Dimension bounds for higher Bruhat orders

We study the Dushnik-Miller dimension of higher Bruhat orders. For the inclusion order $B_{\mathrm{inc}}(n,k)$, with $k$ fixed, we prove that the order of dimension growth is $n^k$, by exhibiting standard examples for the lower bound and explicit systems of coordinates for the upper bound. A recent Turán-system construction of Gao, Kuang, Pikhurko and Wang gives an upper coefficient within a factor smaller than $4$ of the lower coefficient. For the genuine higher Bruhat order $B(n,k)$, we construct for every fixed $k\ge3$ a standard example of order $n^{2k+1}$. We leave it open whether a polynomial upper bound on this dimension exists.
Classification with Large-Step Gradient Descent: Unifying Self-Stabilization and Convergence Rates
Salma Tarmoun; Lachlan Ewen MacDonald; Konstantinos Emmanouilidis; Ziqing Xu; René Vidal

Neural networks are often trained with gradient descent (GD) using step sizes that exceed classical stability thresholds, a regime where standard convergence theory no longer applies. Despite exhibiting non-monotonic loss and oscillatory dynamics, this regime frequently leads to faster convergence and better generalization. Existing theoretical perspectives offer complementary but incomplete insights: one identifies a self-stabilization mechanism that drives GD toward flat regions but does not yield convergence rates; another derives rigorous rates for specific losses but does not explain the underlying stabilization mechanism; and a third unifies these views for overparameterized least squares, but relies on the existence of a minimizer manifold, which is absent in classification settings. In this work, we extend this unified geometric perspective to exponential-tail losses, including logistic and cross-entropy losses in separable linear classification, where the loss infimum is not attained at any finite parameter. We identify a curvature-defined reference subspace that replaces the role of the minimizer manifold, yielding a coupled dynamical system in which orthogonal oscillations are damped by parallel progress along directions of decreasing sharpness. Under regularity conditions, which we verify for logistic and multiclass cross-entropy losses on symmetric data models, we derive explicit bounds for the iterates, not just the loss, covering both the unstable and stable regimes, and revealing a three-phase damping structure in the latter. Our analysis further uncovers a transient implicit bias induced by large step sizes: although GD converges asymptotically to the max-margin direction, large steps can leave persistent orthogonal residuals and, in certain geometries, amplify them, affecting finite-time alignment with the max-margin direction.
Polynomial integrals and Poisson structures of the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator

We classify the autonomous polynomial integrals of the nondegenerate fourth-order Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator. For a rational frequency ratio $m:n$ in lowest terms, the two sector energies together with the real and imaginary parts of a single ladder product generate all polynomial integrals, subject to one defining relation. The smallest total degree of an integral not expressible through the sector energies is $m+n$, and this bound is attained. For an irrational ratio only polynomials in the sector energies are conserved. In normal-mode variables the commensurate case is the negative oscillator resonance, and the classification realizes its invariant theory in the original higher-derivative variables. Two compatible Poisson structures generate the same dynamics with an indefinite and a positive-definite Hamiltonian. They induce different brackets on the same physical generators. We show that diagonal rescalings of the generators identifying the two abstract Poisson algebras exist only when $m$ or $n$ is even, and that none of them preserves the physical domain of nonnegative sector energies. Finally, we express the generators in terms of the original coordinate and its first three derivatives. The classical multiplier identity gives their variational characteristics in closed form and shows that the additional resonant integrals cannot arise from point variational symmetries.
Methanol substitution suppresses deflagration-excited knock and increases the efficiency of a hydrogen-fuelled CFR engine
Riming Xu; Mebin Panithasan; Xinyang Wang; Giovanni Vorraro; James W. G. Turner

Knock restricts the performance of hydrogen spark-ignition engines and is usually attributed to end-gas autoignition. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study in which methanol is used to replace part of the hydrogen in a hydrogen engine at constant fuel energy addition, and it shows that near the knock boundary the limiting oscillation is excited by the deflagration itself, which methanol removes without derating the performance. Port-injected methanol replaced 20--50% of the hydrogen energy in a variable-compression Cooperative Fuel Research engine at 600 rpm and compression ratios of 8--12. With pure hydrogen, oscillation in the 4--15 kHz range began before 10% of the charge had burned in 97--100% of cycles, and its maximum amplitude (MAPO) followed the maximum pressure-rise rate across 2499 cycles (Spearman $ρ=0.94$). Methanol slowed the deflagration: it replaced high-flame-speed hydrogen, cooled the intake by 24--25 K and, at unchanged intake pressure, enleaned the mixture by 10--13%. At 50% methanol, the 10--90% combustion duration lengthened 2.7--3.0-fold, oscillation onset moved 4.5--8.3$^\circ$CA after CA10 and mean MAPO fell by 89--93% although the spark timing was advanced by 13--19$^\circ$CA, and IMEP and indicated thermal efficiency rose by 2.4--7.8%. Methanol was thus worth more than this advance, and at matched CA50 MAPO was still about 90% lower. The measured combustion duration of all 25 data sets scaled with the computed laminar flame speed as $S_L^{-0.58}$ ($R^2=0.99$); fuel replacement accounted for about three quarters of the reduction in $S_L$, and the end-gas autoignition integral stayed below 0.07, against 1 at autoignition. The chamber kept its cylindrical acoustic modes, whose frequencies fell by 8--9%. The trade-off is formaldehyde emissions, which rose five- to sixfold while NO$_x$ fell by 49--85%.
Distributionally Robust Risk Evaluation with Low-Rank Perturbations
Linglingzhi Zhu; Dongze Wu; Yao Xie

We study distributionally robust risk under perturbations restricted to low-rank matrices whose row and column spaces are shared across observations, focusing on how much worst-case risk this restriction sacrifices and how to compute the restricted worst case. Under moment or Wasserstein budgets, we derive quantitative bounds on the gap between the unrestricted and low-rank worst-case risks, characterize when the gap vanishes, and identify the smallest lossless row and column dimensions. To generate worst-case perturbations, we apply projected gradient ascent to a curvature-corrected concave problem and derive computable risk certificates. We establish global sublinear convergence for the corrected objective and linear convergence to a worst-case distribution when the budget constraint is sufficiently active.
Christopher J. Eagle; Isaac Goldbring; Timothy H. McNicholl; Russell Miller

We study the computable content of nuclearity for $C^*$-algebras. We show that nuclearity effectivizes automatically: a presentation of a $C^*$-algebra is effectively nuclear, in the sense that the completely positive approximations witnessing nuclearity can be computed uniformly from the data they approximate, if and only if it is a computable presentation of a nuclear $C^*$-algebra, and likewise for the effectivization of the Choi--Effros form of nuclearity. The main tool is an effective version of the Arveson extension theorem: we prove that the $n$-th matrix numerical range of a tuple from a computable presentation is computably compact, uniformly in all of its data, and deduce an algorithm which converts an approximately attainable tuple of matrices into a computable unital completely positive map attaining it. A byproduct is that the computable states of any computable presentation of a unital $C^*$-algebra are weak$^*$-dense in its state space. We also prove that the Cuntz algebras $\mathcal{O}_n$ are computably categorical and obtain an effective form of Kirchberg--Phillips absorption. By contrast with the conditions above, we do not know whether every computable presentation of a nuclear $C^*$-algebra admits a computable embedding into $\mathcal{O}_2$ with a computable conditional expectation; we answer this affirmatively for commutative $C^*$-algebras, for AF algebras, and, by a dynamical argument using invariant states, for the group $C^*$-algebras of a class of amenable groups including all finitely presented residually finite ones. Finally, we show that the set of indices of computable presentations of nuclear $C^*$-algebras is $Π^0_2$, and that the corresponding set for c.e. presentations is $Π^0_2$-hard; the latter rests on a result of independent interest, namely that amenability of computable groups is $Π^0_2$-complete within the class of computable groups.
A Cut Finite Element Method with Boundary Value Correction for Robin, Neumann and Interface Conditions
Erik Burman; Peter Hansbo; Mats G. Larson

We extend the cut finite element method with boundary value correction of Burman, Hansbo and Larson [Math.\ Comp.\ 87 (2018) 633--657] to Robin and Neumann conditions and to interface problems with imperfect bonding. The formulation retains a piecewise affine boundary for all integration, while using the exact geometry only at boundary quadrature points. The correction uses Taylor expansions of the solution and its gradient along the discrete normal, with the exact normal used to evaluate the transported flux. At an interface, a further correction to the normal flux jump accounts for the difference between these two normals. Under the stated trace and Poincaré bounds, the corrected form is an $O(h^{1/2})$ perturbation of a symmetric form, whose matrix can therefore be used as a preconditioner. For a fixed finite Robin coefficient, we obtain the energy error bound $C_β(h^p+δ_h^{m+1})$, whereas the bound uniform in the Robin coefficient is $C(h^p+h^{-1/2}δ_h^{m+1})$, provided the Poincaré constant is uniform. With $δ_h=O(h^2)$, the sufficient Taylor orders are therefore $2m+2\ge p$ and $2m+\frac32\ge p$, respectively. Numerical examples for $p=1,2,3$ illustrate these rates and the effect of the flux-jump correction in the interface problem.
Dispersive decay for the modified Benjamin-Ono equation with small data

We study the modified Benjamin-Ono equation for small, localized initial data where no solitons arise, and prove a dispersive estimate. Unlike the standard Benjamin-Ono equation, the modified version is not known to be completely integrable, so we cannot rely on integrable systems tools. First, to manage the nonlocal Hilbert transform in the linear part of the equation, we project the equation to positive and negative frequencies. We then combine wave packet testing of Ifrim-Tataru, the Klainerman-Sobolev vector field method, and a bootstrap argument.
$A_1^{(1)}$-Grounded partitions at levels $1$ and $2$, Part II: affine crystal structure

Grounded partitions are coloured partitions with difference conditions, introduced by Dousse and Konan, that are in bijection with the paths of the Kyoto path model of Kang, Kashiwara, Misra, Miwa, Nakashima and Nakayashiki. We describe the affine crystal structure on the grounded partitions arising from the level $1$ and level $2$ perfect crystals of type $A_1^{(1)}$. At level $1$, grounded partitions are naturally identified with $2$-restricted partitions, and the affine crystal structure is given by Kleshchev's modular branching rule for symmetric groups in characteristic $2$. At level $2$, we give explicit bracketing rules which make grounded partitions into affine crystal graphs of highest weights $2Λ_0$, $Λ_0+Λ_1$, and $2Λ_1$. We prove this by constructing explicit graph isomorphisms with the asymptotic model of Ariki and Mathas, whose vertices are Kleshchev multipartitions arising from Ariki-Koike algebras. Finally, we erase the $0$-arrows, which leaves the crystal graphs of the restrictions to the Levi subalgebra, and decompose them into finite strings. This decomposition gives new $q$-series identities at levels $1$ and $2$.
A BMO Extension of Oskolkov's Criterion for Rectangular Trigonometric Fourier Sums

We give a sufficient condition in terms of sectional BMO for almost everywhere Pringsheim convergence of rectangular trigonometric Fourier sums. For continuous functions, the condition includes Oskolkov's criterion, and an example shows that the inclusion is strict.
Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations

We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $Ω(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.
Christopher H. Cashen; Michelle Chu; Jing Tao

We show that for every finite rank Coxeter system, the Coxeter group is hierarchically hyperbolic relative to its nonhyperoctahedral irreducible higher rank affine parabolic subgroups. This is sharp---the Coxeter group admits a hierarchically hyperbolic group structure if and only if it has no such parabolic subgroups, and we give a complete diagrammatic characterization of when this is true. Moreover, this condition is equivalent to the existence of a coarsely equivariant coarse median on the Coxeter group. We also show that the Coxeter group is virtually a colorable hierarchically hyperbolic group. This is achieved by passing to a congruence subgroup of the Tits representation. As consequences, the Davis complex is a hierarchically hyperbolic space and the group admits a coarse median of rank equal to its algebraic rank. Furthermore, the Coxeter group is quasimedian quasiisometric to a finite dimensional CAT(0) cube complex and is virtually coarsely injective. Two appendices prove results of independent interest that are not Coxeter-specific. The first promotes a relative HHS structure with HHS peripheral coordinate spaces to an HHS structure. The second shows that a virtually Abelian group admits a coarsely equivariant coarse median precisely when it is hyperoctahedral.
Sasakian Hodge Numbers of Calabi-Yau Links

The link of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity whose degree equals the sum of its weights is a Sasakian manifold that admits a contact Calabi-Yau structure, and its Sasakian Hodge numbers are dimensions of graded pieces of the Milnor algebra of the defining polynomial. In earlier work these numbers were computed with Gröbner bases for the $7$-dimensional links of $7549$ of the $7555$ weighted Calabi-Yau threefold links, and two conjectures were raised from the data. The first asserts that polynomials with the same weights have Milnor algebras whose relevant graded pieces have equal dimensions; the second asserts that the Sasakian Hodge number $h^{2,1}_S$ of the link is bounded above by the Hodge number $h^{2,1}$ of the base Calabi-Yau threefold. Both conjectures are proved here. The first holds for every polynomial with an isolated singularity, because its partial derivatives form a regular sequence; an independent derivation of the Sasakian Hodge numbers by sheaf cohomology on the leaf-space orbifold is also given. For the second, the stringy Hodge numbers of the Calabi-Yau orbifold are shown to bound the middle Sasakian Hodge numbers in every dimension $n\ge2$, and for $n\ge3$ the gap in $h^{n-1,1}$ is shown to be a sum of geometric genera of loci of orbifold points; for threefolds the bound is attained exactly when all curves of orbifold points are rational. The resulting closed formulae give the Sasakian Hodge numbers of the six $7$-dimensional links left open in the earlier work and complete datasets for all $95$ five-dimensional K3 links and all $1\,100\,055$ nine-dimensional Calabi-Yau fourfold links; for the K3 links they recover the previously known second Betti numbers.
Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras

We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible families conjecturally associated with specific $D^b_q(\mathfrak{g})$ Argyres--Douglas theories. Specialising to $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ with $N$ prime, we find a stronger result: under the same $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration assumption, four-dimensional unitarity rules out all levels except the boundary admissible $k = k_{N,q}$, which are precisely those corresponding to the $D_q^N(\mathfrak{sl}_N)$ Argyres--Douglas theories.
Depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets of tame covers

We generalize DeBacker and Reeder's construction (or rather, its refinement by Kaletha) of depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets to tame covers of unramified reductive groups defined by étale levels. These include, in particular, all tame covers associated to Brylinski-Deligne data. We prove that our L-packets satisfy invariance of formal degrees and an appropriate notion of stability.
Admissibility-Preserving Control for Block Strict-Feedback Systems Under Time-Varying Asymmetric Actuator and State Constraints
Saurabh Kumar; Lohitvel Gopikannan; Shashi Ranjan Kumar; Abhinav Sinha

This paper addresses the tracking control of block strict-feedback nonlinear systems subject to time-varying asymmetric actuator and full state constraints. To that end, we develop a time-varying Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) framework, in which the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the plant input through a dynamic realization. The APIR guarantees input admissibility under the moving actuator set whenever each actuator bound contracts slower than the decay rate of the realization, and a closed-form lower bound on its gain is derived. The state constraints are handled by a logarithmic barrier coordinate at every backstepping step, with widths measured from the virtual control to the moving envelope of the corresponding state. We prove that every state lies inside its envelope, with each virtual control only required to remain inside the envelope of the next state, while the tracking error converges to zero exponentially. Simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed safety-critical control scheme.
Evolutionary-based Transfer Learning for Physical Attack on End-to-End Autoencoder Communications
Ho Viet Duc Luong; Lang Hong Nguyet Anh; Huynh Thi Thanh Binh; Trinh Van Chien

End-to-end autoencoder communication has emerged as a promising means of achieving efficient data transmission across various domains. Nevertheless, vulnerabilities have recently been revealed in these systems by adversarial attacks, wherein malevolent entities manipulate the transmitted signals to deceive the autoencoder. This paper leverages the applications of evolutionary algorithms to solve a challenging optimization problem of launching physical attacks against end-to-end autoencoder communication. For white-box scenarios, we introduce PAGA (Physical Attack based on Genetic Algorithm), which combines a genetic algorithm with elite population initialization to craft attack signals that degrade autoencoder performance. To gauge the efficacy of these attack signals, we employ a fitness function that assesses their capacity to induce substantial reconstruction errors and misclassification rates. A Multi-Factorial version of PAGA, referred to as PAMFGA, is proposed to deal with practical scenarios where the attackers have limited knowledge about the receiver, also known as a black-box attack. Our experimental results show that the proposed attacks can substantially degrade the reliability of the considered autoencoder communication systems across the evaluated settings. This study also underscores the critical importance of incorporating security considerations into the design and implementation of end-to-end autoencoder communication systems.
Composition operators on weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces

Given a function $φ:\D\to \D$ holomorphic in a neighborhood of the closed unit disk $\overline{\D}$, we study the matrix \[ A_φ= \big(\widehat{φ^n}(k)\big)_{n,k\geq 0}. \] We obtain a complete characterization of those $φ$ for which $A_φ$ acts boundedly from $\ell^p$ to $\ell^q$, $p,q\in [1,\infty]$. These results can be reformulated in terms of composition operators, providing a complete description of the symbols $φ$ holomorphic in a neighbourhood of $\overline{\D}$ that induce a bounded composition operator $C_φ:f\mapsto f\circ φ$ between two possibly different Beurling--Sobolev spaces. In particular, we prove that $C_φ$ is bounded on $\ell_a^p$ for some $p\neq 2$ if and only if it is bounded on every $\ell_a^p$, $p\in [1,\infty]$, if and only if $φ$ satisfies an analytic condition at the points of $\overline{\D}$ where it touches the unit circle. Extensions to weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces are also provided.
A hyperbolic area proof of the Kahn-Lyubich Covering Lemma and its generalization

The Covering Lemma of J. Kahn and M. Lyubich is a fundamental analytic tool for controlling conformal moduli of annuli under branched coverings of finite degree. In the last several decades, it has played a crucial role in establishing rigidity of multicritical polynomial and rational maps. The classical proof uses the Near-Degenerate Regime as the main mechanism. In this short note, we prove this lemma using hyperbolic area and the Dirichlet energy. We also establish a version of the Covering Lemma for holomorphic maps of infinite degree. Our argument is inspired by recent applications of the hyperbolic area method to the study of wandering domains in rational and transcendental dynamics.
The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity

We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $Σ$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.
$C^{1,α}$ Regularity of $W^{2,2}$ $Q$-Valued Maps with Small Laplacian

We establish a regularity criterion for $Q$-valued maps $u\in W^{2,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Ω,\mathcal A_Q(\mathbb R^k))$, where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is open. If $|Δu|\leqδ_*|D^2u|$ almost everywhere, with $δ_*=δ_*(n,k,Q)>0$ sufficiently small, then $u\in C^{1,α}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $α=α(n,k,Q)>0$, with quantitative estimates. The result holds for arbitrary $n\geq2$, $k\geq1$, and $Q\geq1$. The proof establishes uniform energy decay using a rigidity principle for positive-semidefinite matrix-valued measures with an aperture bound and approximately atomic divergence, extending the target-stress argument for the homogeneity gap in \cite{Luc26}. The argument relies only on first variation identities. As consequences, we obtain $C^{1,α}$ regularity for Dirichlet-stationary $W^{2,2}$ maps and for locally Lipschitz $W^{2,2}$ maps whose graph varifolds are stationary and have sufficiently small slope. Combining the latter result with Bellettini's Lipschitz sheeting theorem \cite{Bel25}, we establish $C^{1,α}$ sheeting in the multiple-valued sense for two-sided stable minimal immersions whose singular set has vanishing $2$-capacity relative to the immersion, under suitable flatness and mass bounds. Our results allow us to reduce the proof of compactness within this class, under locally uniform mass bounds, to the conjecture that branch sets of stationary $C^{1,α}$ multiple-valued graphs in codimension one have vanishing $2$-capacity.
Countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit

We study countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit. Given an infinite compact metric countable space $X$, we show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$, the collection of continuous functions on $X$ to itself admitting a dense orbit, is always nonempty. We then classify the systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ up to topological conjugacy in terms of the second Cantor--Bendixson derivative $X^{(2)}$: if $X^{(2)} = \emptyset$ then all systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ are mutually conjugate, while if $X^{(2)} \neq \emptyset$ then $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ contains $2^{\aleph_0}$ pairwise nonconjugate systems. The proof of the latter relies on a gluing construction for countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit, which is of independent interest. We also show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ is nowhere dense in $C(X,X)$ with the compact-open topology. We also study the Ellis semigroup $E(X,f)$ of a countable dynamical system. We characterize, under the assumption that $|ω(x,f)| = 1$ for each $x \in X^{(1)}$, when the nontrivial functions of $E(X,f)$ are continuous. In particular, for the family constructed on spaces with $|X^{(2)}| \geq 2$, every nontrivial function of the Ellis semigroup is discontinuous.
Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
Omar Bachain; Mohamed Amazioug; Rachid Ahl Laamara

We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.
Three-ends Furstenberg estimates and approximate rectangles

We prove a three-ends incidence estimate whose multiplicity exponent is sharp for one-dimensional Katz-Tao point sets.} At the heart of the argument lies rectangular non-concentration and its incidence theory introduced earlier by the authors. As an application, we obtain a strong quantitative bound on the number of approximate rectangles with the vertices belonging to four separated camps, each retaining a non-concentration condition.
A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
Xuwen Chen; Justin Holmer; Shunlin Shen

We consider the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a bounded forward-global solution which starts arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The core has two limits in distinct similarity orbits. A single energy-space norm identity identifies the radiation and reduces every competing fixed list to one profile; the two limits then give a contradiction. The construction uses summable radiation packets whose quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. We control the nonlinear error uniformly over these intervals and select the endpoints by a compact fixed-point map. A computer-assisted certificate validates the stationary state and its complete odd energy kernel.
Well-Balanced WE-PINNs for the Shallow Water Equations over Smooth and Discontinuous Bathymetries
Ismail Oubarka; Imad Kissami; Mohamed Boubekeur; Imad Elmahi; Fayssal Benkhaldoun

Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations without a mesh, but they do not in general preserve the steady states that well-balanced schemes reproduce exactly. We present a well-balanced extension of the weak and entropy PINN (WE-PINN) framework to the shallow water equations over smooth and discontinuous bathymetry. The residual is a weak space--time control-volume identity enforced on randomly placed control volumes that may overlap, so no mesh is needed. In free-surface variables, the geometric source is integrated by parts onto the bed, so that the network is never differentiated, and a cell-local bed-slope correction makes the quadrature reproduce the exact bed increment. Bed discontinuities, located from the bathymetry alone, separate sub-domains carrying independent networks, coupled through conservation of discharge and total head. We prove that the fully discrete residual vanishes identically on the lake at rest for any control-volume family, quadrature order and nominal bed slope, so that the equilibrium is an exact global minimiser of the training objective; that the continuous residual characterises weak solutions; that the slope correction is consistent; and that no approximation with a continuous free surface can satisfy the head condition at a step with non-zero discharge, so that the decomposition is necessary. Numerically, the residual vanishes to round-off on four lake-at-rest configurations over smooth, discontinuous, compound and tabulated beds, and the trained network reaches the equilibrium to round-off under an extended training budget. On seven Riemann problems at a bottom step, covering sub-, super- and critical transitions, the network attains relative $L^1$ free-surface errors between $6.9\times10^{-4}$ and $3.5\times10^{-3}$, and reaches critical states without prescribing them.
Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
Zhiyao Yang; Bowen Xiao; Huangjun Zhu

Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit. Sampling and spectral completion of any 3-design yield, with probability $1-O(1/d)$, a measurement with linearly many outcomes and a dimension-independent Fisher floor. Such a measurement separates all pure states in Hellinger distance, so pure-state maximum-likelihood estimation from $N$ copies attains mean infidelity $O(d/N)$ uniformly over pure states, optimal up to a universal constant factor.
Fictitious Play When Agents Are Not Expected-Utility Maximizers: A Geometric Analysis in $2$-Action Games
Hao Liang; Solaleh Mohammadi; Kaiqing Zhang

Fictitious play (FP) is one of the earliest and most fundamental learning procedures in games, where each agent independently chooses a best response to the empirical distribution of opponents' past actions by maximizing the expected payoff with respect to it. However, learning agents may not always be expected-utility maximizers: they may use nonlinear evaluation functionals to account for the uncertainty induced by the opponents, e.g., via risk measures. In this work, we study nonlinear fictitious play (NL-FP), in which each pure action is evaluated by a general, possibly nonlinear functional of the payoff distribution induced by the opponent's empirical belief. To analyze NL-FP, we first identify a single-crossing property (SCP) of evaluation functionals that preserves the classical geometry of FP in $2\times2$ games. Furthermore, we conduct a novel geometric analysis of the convergence behavior of NL-FP in $2\times2$ games, even when the SCP fails. Beyond $2\times2$ games, we show that the convergence of NL-FP in $2\times n$ ($n\ge3$) games may fail even for continuous-time NL-FP, when the two-action player uses conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) in a $2\times3$ game. In addition, we identify a finite-crossing condition that ensures convergence of the selected continuous-time dynamics and the discrete-time iterates in general $2\times n$ games, which also provides new insights into the global landscape of continuous-time classical FP in such games.

The free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is obtained from the free group of rank $m$ by imposing the relations $w^n=1$ for all words $w$. We prove that $B(m,n)$ is completely $C^*$-selfless for every $m\geq2$ and every odd exponent $n\geq557$. Consequently, its reduced group $C^*$-algebra has stable rank one and strict comparison of positive elements by its canonical trace. This answers the question of whether $C^*$-selfless groups can satisfy a nontrivial group law. The proof establishes Ozawa's property $P_{PHP}$ by combining a combinatorial construction with a relative power-avoidance argument based on the canonical forms of Atkarskaya-Rips-Tent.
Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians

We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form. Under appropriate split-generation assumptions, we construct a Bridgeland stability condition whose stable objects are isomorphic to special Lagrangian branes, as predicted by the Thomas-Yau conjecture. The geometric construction is based on a one-parameter family of special Lagrangian submanifolds with boundary. One part of the boundary is contained in the Lagrangian underlying the domain of the morphism and the other in the Lagrangian underlying the codomain. Surgeries occur as the family encounters singularities or obstruction walls. We prove that the construction always terminates for the two-torus and provide higher dimensional examples.
Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases
Bowen Xiao; Zhiyao Yang; Huangjun Zhu

Multiparameter pure-state metrology is limited by the incompatibility of measurements optimized for different parameters. We characterize uniform sensitivity by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) retained over all pure states and parameter directions. We prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases suffices for a nearly optimal Fisher floor, independently of the Hilbert-space dimension $d$. With high probability, five independent Haar bases already achieve a positive, dimension-independent floor, and larger constant families achieve approximate universal Fisher symmetry: they retain nearly one half of the QFI in every direction, the largest uniform fraction permitted by measurement incompatibility. The required number of bases is optimal up to a logarithmic factor in inverse accuracy. In contrast, $d+1$ mutually unbiased bases, when they exist, can minimize mean Fisher anisotropy among families of $d+1$ bases yet have a Fisher floor of at most $1/(d+1)$, showing that optimal average balance does not ensure uniform sensitivity.
On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.
Unequal-probability distributional balance and the Horvitz-Thompson estimator
Blair Robertson; Chris Price; Marco Reale; Philip Davies

Auxiliary information can improve estimation precision under probability sampling, but the relationship between the study and auxiliary variables may not be known well enough to specify suitable balancing variables. Distributionally balanced designs address this by targeting agreement between sample and population auxiliary distributions. We extend energy-based distributional balance to prescribed unequal inclusion probabilities by comparing the empirical sample distribution with an inclusion-probability-weighted population distribution. Under a regularity condition relating the study values divided by their inclusion probabilities to the auxiliaries, we establish an upper bound on the design variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator in terms of the expected energy distance. This bound motivates an algorithm that exchanges units between randomly paired candidate samples without increasing their average energy distance. Combined with random initialization and uniform selection of a final candidate, the procedure preserves the prescribed first-order inclusion probabilities. We evaluate its auxiliary-space properties and estimation performance using generated populations and the Meuse data.
Niche construction as an emerging phenomenon from fast ecological and slow evolutionary-environmental timescales in individual-based models
Nicolas Champagnat; Coralie Fritsch; Pablo A. Marquet; Cristobal Quiñinao; Leonardo Videla; Nicolás Zalduendo

We consider an individual-based model of niche construction built upon birth-death processes of d interacting biological entities (e.g., species, subpopulations or mutant strains in the same species) immersed in a slowly-varying environment which is influenced by the population state. In this setting, extinction and/or emergence of entities with negligible size or rarity, on long time scales can be observed. We prove that the joint dynamics of the environment and the species sizes on a logarithmic scale undergo a piecewise deterministic Markov process in a large time regime, which can be approximated by an explicit dynamical system in the limit of large populations. This convergence result holds true under the assumption that no "bad event" occurs during the population dynamics, corresponding to situations where several species become dominant or go extinct simultaneously. We also prove that no such bad event occurs for Baire-almost all initial conditions of the population sizes and the environmental resources. We apply this framework to study the long term coexistence of two specialist species consuming two resources, with a "joint" niche construction where each species constructs the niche of the other while depleting its resources. We also study an example of immune escape in cancer, where the environmental variable is associated with the state of the immune system and the species are associated with three types of tumor cells.

Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. Beyond the two twists available at any finite $N$, which we studied in our previous work, we find five additional classes at infinite rank which require non-commuting backgrounds associated with D-branes in IIB supergravity. Together, these twists realize representatives of every equivalence class of twisting supercharges in flat-space type IIB supergravity recently classified by the first author; however, the precise form of the orbit stratification differs. This difference is related to a higher central extension of the IIB superalgebra that appears in our treatment of the IKKT model in the BV formalism. Expanding around the non-commutative backgrounds gives worldvolume theories on products of A- and B-branes, including four-dimensional BF theory on an emergent D3-brane. We relate all these twists to deformations of BCOV theory (the closed string field theory of the topological B-model) using the open-closed duality of classical string field theory. For one of the twists with Spin$(7)$ symmetry, we also show the localization of the IKKT partition function by Moore, Nekrasov, and Shatashvili can be directly reconstructed with the BV formalism, with their auxiliary field completion encoded by quadratic antifield terms. Throughout, we provide self-contained treatments of the formal techniques we employ.
Mohammad Ghomi; Hongda Qiu; Matteo Raffaelli; Yuetong Zhang

We construct smooth isometric embeddings of closed surfaces of positive genus in Euclidean 3-space which are tight, i.e., have minimal total positive curvature, but are not congruent. These embeddings agree outside a compact subset of the region of negative curvature, and enclose different volumes. Thus the rigidity theorem of Alexandrov for analytic tight surfaces does not hold in the smooth category, which settles problems of Nirenberg and Banchoff-Kuhnel.
Stability for the Bray-Brendle-Neves Scalar Sphere Rigidity Theorem

Let $(M^3,g)$ be a closed and oriented 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $π_2(M)\neq 0$ and let $A_{π_2}(M,g)$ denote the least area among homotopically nontrivial two-spheres in $M$. By a theorem of Bray-Brendle-Neves, $A_{π_2}(M,g)\inf_M R_g \leq 8π$ with equality characterizing the cylindrical geometry $S^2\times\mathbb{R}$. Motivated by Sormani's questions on volume preserving intrinsic flat stability for scalar curvature rigidity problems, we study the almost equality regime of this theorem. We build, using Sweeney's tunnel construction, a sequence satisfying $A_{π_2}(M_j,g_j)\inf_{M_j} R_{g_j} \rightarrow 8π$ with uniformly bounded volume and diameter whose volume preserving intrinsic flat limit is not the Bray-Brendle-Neves rigidity space, showing that stability fails in general. We then prove stability in two special cases: for sequences of rotationally symmetric metrics (with non-collapsing assumptions) and for sequences of manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature.
Triameter, distance packings, and vertex connectivity

We study upper bounds for the triameter of a connected graph in terms of distance packings and vertex connectivity. For any positive integer $k$, we bound the triameter of a graph by a linear function of its $k$-packing number and show that this bound is tight for all values of the parameters. As a corollary, we confirm the conjecture of Das and Abdioğlu on the upper bound for the triameter in terms of the order and the minimum degree of a graph. We also find the maximum triameter among graphs with given order and vertex connectivity, and describe the extremal graphs. Our main tool is a projection of a graph onto a spider or a unicyclic graph which preserves the distances between three prescribed vertices.
Structure-Preserving Integrators for Locally Conformally Symplectic Systems: Variational Methods and Globalization
Ayten Gezici; Melvin Leok; Cristina Sardón

Locally conformally symplectic (LCS) manifolds are characterized by a nondegenerate two-form $Ω$ satisfying $\mathrm{d}Ω=φ\wedgeΩ$, where $φ$ is a closed one-form, called the Lee form. Although an LCS structure is locally conformal to an ordinary symplectic structure, the local symplectic descriptions need not arise from a single global symplectic form. This creates a natural local-to-global problem for geometric numerical integration: local symplectic discretizations must be compatible on chart overlaps in order to determine a globally defined numerical dynamics. We develop a Hamiltonian variational framework for the construction and globalization of structure-preserving integrators for LCS systems. The continuous theory is first recalled in a form adapted to a Type~II Hamiltonian variational principle. We then introduce exact and approximate discrete right Hamiltonians for the local symplectic representatives and identify the transformation law that they must satisfy on overlaps. This compatibility condition implies equivariance of the associated local discrete Hamiltonian maps and therefore provides a sufficient condition for their globalization. The resulting global discrete map preserves the LCS two-form conformally, with a discrete conformal factor determined by the local conformal potentials. The framework applies naturally to Type~II Hamiltonian variational integrators and, in the cotangent-type setting considered here, to symplectic Runge--Kutta methods. In particular, Gauss--Legendre methods and the implicit midpoint rule yield globally compatible LCS structure-preserving schemes. Under suitable regularity assumptions, the corresponding Lagrangian formulation is recovered through discrete Legendre transformations. Numerical examples illustrate overlap compatibility, chart switching, convergence, and discrete conformal preservation.
The lifting problem for Galois representations of global fields

We prove that all mod $2$ Galois representations of a global field lift modulo $4$. In contrast, for every odd prime $p$, we exhibit examples of global Galois representations modulo $p$ that do not lift modulo $p^2$. Our methods also allow us to prove liftability of generalized quaternion groups and hence to complete the classification of liftable finite groups initiated by Khare and Merkurjev.
Sowing the Seeds of Intractability: Kalah is PSPACE-complete

Kalah is a classic two-player game in the mancala family of sowing games. Computers have solved several standard-size starting positions, but the complexity of the game on boards of growing size has remained open. We study the natural generalization in which the number of pits per side is part of the input and an arbitrary position is given, with the stone counts given in unary. We show that deciding whether a designated player can force a win from such a position is PSPACE-complete. The hard positions have Alice to move first and both stores initially empty. The same positions are hard under either common convention for capture opposite an empty pit, and with or without the bonus rule, which gives a player another turn when the last stone is sown into their own store. We introduce Line Kalah as an intermediate problem, a game on a line in which stones that leave the line effectively disappear and Alice must save each of her target pits before Bob captures it, and we reduce quantified Boolean formulas to it. The reduction uses a set of sequential timer piles whose last stones approach a group of targets, forcing Alice to choose between two captures in order to set the truth value of a variable, and a final capture gadget to test a clause chosen by Bob (only one is needed adversarially). Since either player may move any pile at any time, the stages are placed so that premature timer firings protect earlier potential targets. For a true formula, Alice's strategy against arbitrary opposing play either gains enough time to save the remaining targets (after Bob deviates from the intended play) or reaches the final test with a correctly encoded, protected input. Finally, the line positions are embedded in Kalah with both stores empty. A separate Bob pit holds the score adjustment, so the winner takes a strict majority of the stones.
Shikhar Shah; Rui Peng Li; Vassilis Kalantzis; Yuanzhe Xi

Analog in-memory computing offers the potential to accelerate approximate inverse preconditioning, but hardware errors can degrade preconditioners designed in digital arithmetic. We develop an analog-digital preconditioner for symmetric positive-definite linear systems that combines analog block Jacobi with a small digital low-rank residual correction. The correction space is constructed by probing the same programmed analog arrays used in the solve, targeting errors from both the coupling omitted by block Jacobi and persistent hardware perturbations. Under a random linear-operator model, we separate the programmed-mean error from fresh read fluctuations, distinguish the effects of copy averaging and repeated reads, and quantify the sampling accuracy of columnwise probing. Under a centered additive write-noise model, we also derive a computable regularization threshold and identify the approximation error introduced by the regularization shift. Experiments with an analog hardware simulator show that programming errors can change the directions that block Jacobi reduces poorly. In the tested comparisons with significant programming errors, learning the correction space from the programmed copies reduces FGMRES iteration counts relative to construction from digital block Jacobi.
Stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions seven and eight
Serena Dipierro; Joaquim Serra; Raphael Tsiamis; Enrico Valdinoci

We establish optimal sheet separation estimates for stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions up to seven, using an iteration argument in the nonlocal approximation theory of Chan-Dipierro-Serra-Valdinoci. These estimates imply that every stable $s$-minimal hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a hyperplane when $s$ is close to $1$. More generally, every finite Morse index $s$-minimal set in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a half-space. We also establish a compactness theorem for stable $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$. We prove uniform curvature and area estimates for their links and show that, as $s \uparrow 1$, they subconverge graphically in $C^{2,α}$, either with multiplicity one to a classical stable minimal cone, or with multiplicity two to a hyperplane. The stability of Lawson and axisymmetric $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$ shows that these results are optimal.
Erhan Bayraktar; Shuoqing Deng; Daxin Huang; Dominykas Norgilas

Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. In this work, we consider the case where dynamic trading incurs quadratic temporary price impact. First, we prove a duality result for the superhedging price. In particular, the primal of the duality relaxes the strict martingale constraint by penalizing the deviation from a specific martingale. Second, for one asset and one trading period, we interpret this price-impact martingale optimal transport (PIMOT) as a weak optimal transport (WOT) problem, and provide a characterization in the spirit of Wasserstein projection. Finally, we justify that PIMOT is an interpolation between MOT and classical optimal transport (OT), and derive the convergence rate to both sides. Numerical examples with SPX option data show how the price bounds per claim depend on the order size.

We construct $n$-categories $\mathscr{P}_n$ with generators given by simplices and relations given by bistellar moves between them, in any dimension $n$. We show that functors out of $\mathscr{P}_n$ into an $n$-category of theories, give the correct input for the orbifold construction for TQFTs, and subsume all previously known examples, which are all in dimensions $n \leq 3$. In particular, in dimension 3 the construction gives a highly nontrivial categorification of a kind of nonunital, noncounital, Frobenius algebra.
Radiation and persistent shape dynamics for the five-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear wave equation
Xuwen Chen; Justin Holmer; Shunlin Shen

We consider the nonradial five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a forward-global solution which remains arbitrarily close to a nondegenerate sign-changing stationary state in the energy space and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The stationary profile moves in a compact conformal family, but its limit set contains a continuum of classes modulo translations, dilations and rotations. Consequently, the solution admits no soliton resolution using a fixed finite collection of stationary profiles and fixed Lorentz velocities, with pairwise orthogonal spatial parameters. That is, we disprove the fixed-profile soliton resolution conjecture for the five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. The construction uses a sequence of incoming waves with summable energies. Their quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. The main estimates control the zero eigenvalue of the linearized operator and the nonlinear error uniformly over the entire sequence. The stationary input uses a computer-assisted spectral bound for a symmetric single-node state.
Permutation patterns and higher connectivity in inversion graphs

We prove that any permutation $π\in S_n$ whose inversion graph is $k$-connected has at least $\frac{k+1}{2}n - C$ inversions, where $C$ depends only on $k$. In particular, inversion graphs beat the general lower bound $\frac{kn}{2}$ for the number of edges in a $k$-connected graph. Furthermore, we characterize the permutation patterns $σ$ having the property that if $π$ avoids $σ$, then the bound improves to $kn - C$. The collection of patterns is $\mathrm{Av}(321, 2341, 4123)$, and it is independent of $k \geq 2$. This work is motivated by a result of Linusson and Verkama (2025) that can be reinterpreted as stating that any $1324$-avoiding permutation whose inversion graph satisfies a certain weaker notion of $2$-connectivity must have at least $2n - C$ inversions. Our final result gives a characterization of the patterns having this stronger property.
On the maximum of Poissonian log-correlated fields

We consider stationary log-correlated random fields of the form \[ X_n(t):= \sum_{j\le n} f(e^{τ_j} t+ v_{j})\,,\quad t\in \mathbb{R} \] for a centered 1-periodic analytic function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, where $(τ_j)_{j\ge1}$ are the arrival times of a rate-1 Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}_+$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ are iid uniform random variables in $[0,1)$. We show that with high probability, \[ \max_{t\in[-1,1]}X_n(t) = c_1 n + c_2 τ_n- (c_3+o(1))\log n \] where $c_1,c_2,c_3$ are positive constants depending on $f$. In particular, the random frequency $τ_n$ produces a central limit fluctuation of order $\sqrt{n}$, together with a logarithmic correction different from the ubiquitous Bramson correction for models with strong comparisons to Gaussian fields, such as homogeneous branching random walks and log-characteristic polynomials of C$β$E matrices. Our proof makes a connection with branching random walks in random time-environment, where coarse-scale fluctuations of the arrival times $τ_j$ play the role of a quenched random environment, and fine-scale fluctuations are leveraged to establish a branching decorrelation structure. We conjecture analogous asymptotics for the characteristic polynomials of random permutation matrices, and expect the same mechanism to arise in other Poissonian fields such as characteristic polynomials of sparse random matrices.
Mean-field Fluctuations for First-Passage Percolation with Symmetric Kernels

We study first-passage percolation on finite weighted graphs whose normalized Weibull edge hazards form a symmetric Markov kernel on $N$ vertices. We prove that a uniform absolute spectral gap and an $O(N^{-1})$ bound on a fixed even-step return probability imply the stochastic mean-field passage-time limit and an independent Gaussian hopcount limit. Jointly with these quantities, the entire geodesic from an arbitrary source to an independent uniform target is approximated in total variation by an independent Markov chain stopped at the hopcount. This comparison yields laws of large numbers for fixed-length path segments and joint central limit theorems for bounded additive observables. The results extend to edge laws with a uniform relative hazard error $o(1/\log N)$, including common noise distributions with a power-law hazard and a positive-power error near zero. Applications include integrable singular torus kernels, macroscopic spread-out graphs, non-transitive regular graphs, finite groups, and discretizations of symmetric continuum kernels.
Luenberger observers for two-gene regulatory networks with sigmoidal regulation: explicit observability conditioning, polytopic convergence certificates, and a logistic--Hill comparison

Only a few species of a gene regulatory network can be measured, so the others must be reconstructed by a state observer, and how well this works depends on the function chosen to describe regulation. We examine this for the two-gene negative feedback loop with one measured protein, for monotone regulation functions including the logistic function and the Hill function with its leaky and shifted variants. Using standard tools, we show that the answer is set by the smallest and the largest slope of the regulation function on the concentrations visited. For every function considered, the unmeasured concentration can be recovered from the measured signal and its rate of change, with an error sensitivity set by the smallest slope. A Luenberger observer with explicit gains converges exponentially from any initial guess and tolerates bounded measurement noise whenever a checkable matrix condition involving only the largest slope holds, as it does for every model examined with bounded slopes. The guaranteed rate cannot exceed the degradation rate of the unmeasured protein unless the smallest slope is positive, and faster rates then hold only for small initial errors. All reported rates are certified from above and below. At matched threshold and steepness, no family is uniformly better: the logistic function is better conditioned when the threshold lies mid-range, leaky or shifted Hill functions when it lies low. Hill functions with exponent below one have an unbounded slope at zero concentration and lose the global guarantee, which logistic and shifted Hill functions keep.
Linear Regression with Self-Selection Bias in Polynomial Time

We revisit the problem of estimating $k$ linear regressors with self-selection bias in $n$ dimensions up to error $\varepsilon$ with the maximum self-selection criterion, as introduced by Cherapanamjeri, Daskalakis, Ilyas, and Zampetakis [CDIZ23, STOC]. Our main result is a $\mathrm{poly}(n,k,1/\varepsilon)$ time algorithm for the unknown-index variant of this problem, thereby improving upon the running times of the best known algorithms due to Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] and Kalavasis, Mehrotra, and Zhou [KMZ26, COLT] with exponential dependence on $k$. Our algorithm succeeds in the presence of correlated noise between regressors, which captures the related setting of max-affine regression. Consequently, we also give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem, improving on the prior works of Ghosh, Pananjady, Guntuboyina, and Ramchandran [GPGR22, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory] and Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] with exponential dependence on $k$. Prior works exhaustively search over a $k$-dimensional subspace spanned by the regressors, using conditional moments of the response to test candidates. In contrast, our algorithm is driven by an improved understanding of the moments of the covariates. We show that, restricting to observations with large response values, the degree-$(\log n)$ Hermite moment of the covariates approximately decomposes as a sum of tensor powers of the regressors. The first step of our algorithm can be viewed as a tensor decomposition algorithm for these implicitly represented high-order tensors, which outputs unit vectors parallel to the regressors. A secondary step based on a simple variant of ordinary least squares extracts estimates for the regressors given these unit vectors. We believe our analytic insight and algorithmic components may have applications to designing efficient algorithms for other latent-variable problems.
Laguerre tessellations in spaces of constant curvature and their sectional distributions

We determine the sectional distributions of Poisson--Laguerre tessellations in spaces of non-zero constant curvature, proving closure under totally geodesic sections and deriving explicit weight intensity measures. This includes sections of Poisson--Voronoi tessellations. We construct the generalised polar region, a new geometric object which extends existing polar constructions for both positive and negative curvature and provides an alternative representation of Laguerre tessellations. We also give deterministic conditions for tessellation existence and establish sharp integrability criteria for Poisson--Laguerre tessellations.
Combinatorial Bernoulli Factories with Polynomially Many Coins

We provide an efficient implementation of combinatorial Bernoulli factories. Such a factory turns coins of unknown biases $x$ into a random vertex of a polytope $P$ whose mean is exactly $x$. For every affine slice of the cube (the class of polytopes that admit a factory), we give a single algorithm whose expected number of coin flips and running time at every interior $x$ are polynomial in the dimension and in $1/{δ_*}$, where ${δ_*}=\min_i\{x_i,1-x_i\}$ is never supplied to the algorithm. For perfect matchings this gives $O(n^{8}{δ_*}^{-2}\log(n/{δ_*}))$ flips, while the factory of Niazadeh, Paes Leme, and Schneider [STOC 2021] spends at least $n^{2n-1}$ flips in expectation at the uniform doubly stochastic matrix. For other polytopes, our method rounds exactly given a point deep inside $P$ and the promise that $x$ is far from the boundary of $P$.
FanCyqlone: A Parallelized Solver for Multi-Horizon Optimal Control
Matisse Teuwen; Pieter Pas; Mathijs Schuurmans; Panagiotis Patrinos

Multi-horizon optimal control aims to select optimal control sequences simultaneously for several possible future scenarios, ensuring consistency at the first stage. While this enables advanced model predictive control schemes that explicitly handle prediction uncertainty, solving these problems tends to be costly. We introduce FanCyqlone, a linear solver that exploits parallelism across both time steps and scenario branches. The method builds on Cyqlone to compute the contribution of each branch and combines these results through a shared root problem. We integrate FanCyqlone into QPALM to develop FanCyQPALM, a solver for multi-horizon optimal control problems with general linear stage-wise constraints. We compare its performance with state-of-the-art solvers on spring-mass and quadruped control benchmarks.
Structure-Preserving Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Dynamics on Arbitrary Time Scales

The leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron combines a passive membrane law with threshold-triggered firing and reset. We formulate this hybrid neuron model, under constant input, on an arbitrary Hilger time scale $\mathbb{T}$. Our central result is that, after the first spike, the firing times satisfy $t_{n+1}=Π_{\mathbb{T}}^{+}(t_n+T_c)$, where $T_c$ is the classical reset-to-threshold travel time. This recursion requires no periodicity, homogeneity, or translation invariance of $\mathbb{T}$; it holds for every time scale that is unbounded above. To preserve the passive membrane physics, we use the inverse cylinder transformation to construct a positively regressive coefficient $p_m$. The resulting delta-dynamic equation is exactly the restriction to $\mathbb{T}$ of the classical continuous-time LIF trajectory. By contrast, the direct transcription $V^Δ=-(V-V_\infty)/τ_m$ exhibits graininess-dependent sign reversal and amplification at coarse right-scattered points.
