We prove correctness, everywhere-shortness, and linearity, and give a publicly computable entrywise bound on the reconstruction vector our algorithm returns for each authorized set. For privacy, we introduce hard-core local leakage resilience, which strengthens the leakage-resilience notion of Nielsen and Simkin (EUROCRYPT 2020) to protect a hard-core function of the secret, and we prove that SEC satisfies it against correlated multi-query local leakage under the MatrixHint-MLWE problem, which admits a reduction from the standard MLWE problem. Antipodal paths: a short proof by counting intersections

We give a short elementary proof of Norine's antipodal-coloring theorem: every red--blue edge coloring of a hypercube in which antipodal edges have opposite colors contains a monochromatic path joining antipodal vertices.
Hwijae Son; Sung Woong Cho; Jooyoung Hahn

We propose the Lower-envelope Eikonal Neural Operator (LENO), a physics-informed neural operator for eikonal equations with heterogeneous velocity fields and general source sets. LENO encodes the variational minimum principle of viscosity solutions by constructing source-wise candidate fields and taking their pointwise minimum. This lower-envelope structure enforces the source condition exactly and represents nonsmooth multi-source solutions without a soft boundary penalty. The model is trained without precomputed solution data, using a Godunov upwind residual as the sole training signal. Experiments on point sources and curve sources, sample-dependent piecewise velocity fields, and OpenFWI CurveVel-A and Style-A media show accurate agreement with references of Fast Marching Method (FMM). Additional validation shows that the Godunov residual outperforms conventional finite difference residuals on a high-resolution test, that velocity conditioning and the lower-envelope transform are essential in realistic heterogeneous media, and that the trained operator supports efficient batched evaluation and resolution transfer.
Fully Explicit Stabilized Runge--Kutta Methods for Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard Dynamics

Stiff phase-field dynamics are typically solved by semi-implicit or fully implicit time discretizations, since the interfacial scales in the Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard equations impose severe step-size restrictions on standard explicit methods. In this paper, we investigate a different strategy based on stabilized Runge--Kutta solvers, in particular the Runge--Kutta--Legendre (RKL) and Runge--Kutta--Gegenbauer (RKG) families. These schemes possess enlarged stability regions and therefore provide a natural explicit framework for diffusion-dominated gradient flows without requiring implicit solves. For the modified energy dissipation analysis, we further introduce two new first-order stabilized schemes of RKL and RKG type and derive a novel eigenvalue estimate for the second-order RKG method. We also conduct extensive numerical experiments with both constant and adaptive time stepping, on regular domains as well as on an L-shaped irregular domain. The numerical results show that stabilized explicit Runge--Kutta methods provide an effective and flexible approach for the numerical simulation of Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard dynamics while preserving key structural properties. The Python implementation is available at https://github.com/ZT220501/SRK-for-Gradient-Flows.

The proof rests on an identity for the mean squared support function of the $ε$-subdifferentials of a smooth convex function at a standard Gaussian vector, obtained from two Gaussian integrations by parts.
Axial von Mises Framework for Tensor-Dependent Second-Harmonic Generation

We derive closed-form relations between projected fibril-axis statistics and tensor-dependent second-harmonic generation (SHG) harmonics using a single axial von Mises population. Under coherent emission within domains and detected intensity addition across domains, each angular harmonic factors into a local tensor coefficient and an axial circular moment. Seiedali, Z. Akhlaghi, B. Khosravi. Generalized Cayley graphs and perfect code. Discrete Math. 2026]. For compatible tree rules, we establish integrated consistency and polynomial risk bounds under explicit approximation and entropy conditions. Simulations with matrices, distributions, spherical data and mixed predictors, together with an application to taxi-flow networks, demonstrate competitive predictive performance.
A One-Sided Chord Trim of Wetzel's Sector Covers Unit Arcs

We show that half of its arc is not needed: replacing the arc between the angles $15^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ by its chord gives a convex cover of area $π/24+(\sqrt6-\sqrt2)/8=0.2603092\ldots$. We also reduce the inclusion-minimality of the trimmed sector to two families of cuts.
Asymptotic analysis of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with squared Bessel arrival intensity

Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. The asymptotic properties of the model are also analysed. More precisely, these results are obtained for three important settings: cumulative occupancy over a finite time interval, system occupancy under a diverging long-run mean arrival intensity, and the superposition of independent infinite-server queues with Cox-BESQ arrival intensities. Numerical experiments illustrate the associated rate functions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting rare-event approximations.
Holomorphic Sectional Curvature of Flag Manifolds via Kähler Reduction

We give an alternative proof of Li and Petersen's theorem that every invariant Kähler metric on a compact generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. The defining equations place the level set on a sphere of radius \varrho, where the radial component of its second fundamental form gives the explicit lower bound 4/\varrho2 through the quotient curvature formula. Finally, we use a holomorphic isometric totally geodesic embedding to transfer the bound to generalized flag manifolds of every Lie type.

Thus, the distance guarantee matches the leading coefficient of the GV bound at low rates. For each fixed $\varepsilon$, the construction uses a single inner encoding map throughout the family and admits polynomial-time encoding and unique decoding within a guaranteed radius. This answers the question of Doron, Mosheiff, and Wootters for subcodes of scaled algebraic geometry codes at low rates.
Null designs and switching in polynomial spaces
Masatake Hirao; Koji Imamura; Hiroshi Nozaki; Masanori Sawa; Tomoki Tamaru

Null designs are finite point configurations with real weights whose polynomial moments vanish up to a given degree. In Godsil's framework of polynomial spaces, we give elementary proofs of sharp lower bounds on the number of points in the Euclidean and spherical cases. We characterize the spherical null designs attaining the bound and give explicit formulas for their weights. We then study how null designs can be used to replace part of a weighted design while preserving its polynomial moments. We give conditions ensuring nonnegative weights and apply the minimum-size classification to switching on circles. Examples on spheres and in Hamming and Johnson spaces illustrate these results, including a replacement between noncongruent spherical $5$-designs that preserves equal weights and the number of points.
Rational contractions in quasi-Banach spaces: convergence, multiplicity of fixed points and applications
A. H. Ansari Komachali; Y. U. Gaba; M. Aphane; I. Yildirim

We study self-maps $f$ of a complete $b$-metric space $(U,d)$ (constant $b\ge1$) satisfying the rational contractive condition \[ d(fu,fv)\le\frac{d(u,fv)+d(v,fu)+κ}{b\,[d(u,fu)+d(v,fv)]+1}\,d(u,v)\qquad(u,v\in U), \] with $κ\in[0,1)$. We first observe that the two-parameter family of conditions studied in our earlier work reduces, after a rescaling of the $b$-metric, to this one-parameter form. We then prove: (A) every Picard sequence converges to a fixed point, with an explicit a~priori estimate whose geometric ratio depends only on $b$, $κ$ and $d(u_0,fu_0)$, an a~posteriori estimate, and asymptotic rate at most $κ$; (B) a structure theorem: such maps are automatically continuous, every fixed point attracts the whole ball of radius $(1-κ)/2$, distinct fixed points are at distance at least $(1-κ)/2$ (sharp), basins of attraction are clopen, and the number of fixed points does not exceed the number of connected components of $U$; in particular the fixed point is unique on connected spaces; (C) Ulam--Hyers stability of the fixed-point problem. The class of such maps is not invariant under passing from a quasi-norm to the equivalent $p$-norm metric, so the quasi-Banach results are not formal consequences of the metric ones. A gluing principle shows that the multiplicity permitted by (B) occurs. As applications we obtain existence, exact multiplicity and error estimates for infinite nonlinear systems with relay-type forcing in $\ell^p$, $0<p<1$, and for nonlinear perturbations of Volterra-type equations $f=\pm a+T_gf+ψ(f(z_0))k$ in the Hardy space $H^p$, $0<p<1$, where $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(ζ)g'(ζ)\,dζ$ and $g\in\BMOA$.
Admissibility of unbounded complexes of smooth representations

Let $G$ be a $p$-adic Lie group and $k$ a field of characteristic $p$. We prove that a complex of smooth $k$-representations of $G$ has admissible cohomology if and only if it is globally admissible, i.e., its hypercohomology with respect to a torsion-free open compact pro-$p$ subgroup is finite dimensional in every degree. This extends the bounded-below and bounded-above comparison of Schneider--Sorensen to arbitrary unbounded complexes.

Following Gábor Czédli, the \emph{congruence density} of a finite lattice $A$ is $\cd(A)=|\Con A|/2^{|A|-1}$, where $\Con A$ is its congruence lattice and $|A|$ is its number of elements. Czédli proved that density cannot increase under several kinds of sublattice extension and asked whether this holds for every sublattice inclusion. For a sublattice $S$ of $L$, we prove the stronger inequality $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. The proof follows congruence labels along the chains into which prime intervals of $S$ split in $L$. We also prove that $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ if and only if every element of $L-S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of G. Czédli and L.~Szabó relating compatible quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding quasiorder-density results.
Contiguity of unions of perfect matchings and random regular uniform hypergraphs

For fixed integers $s\ge3$ and $r$ satisfying $\log(r!)>\frac{r(s-1)}s\log r$, the union of $r$ independent uniform perfect matchings of the complete $s$-uniform hypergraph is mutually contiguous to the uniform simple $r$-regular $s$-uniform hypergraph, as $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $s$. In particular, $r=\lceil e^s\rceil$ suffices. The main input is the sharp entropy inequality for random permutations of Bristiel and Caputo. It proves the global maximization needed for the second moment of the number of complete factorizations. The remaining calculation, including its lattice factor, matches the short-cycle contribution required by small-subgraph conditioning.\\ This is an expanded version of a proof provided by ChatGPT-Astra.
The limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erdős problem 521
Zengjing Chen; Xiaodong Liu; Jie Peng; Hanchao Wang; Mingjian Zhang

We resolve Erdős Problem~521 by proving that the normalized real-root count $N_n/\log n$ of Rademacher polynomials almost surely has no limit. More generally, consider the Kac polynomials \[ P_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}ξ_jx^j \] with i.i.d.\ real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment. Let $N_n$ denote the number of distinct real roots of $P_n$. We prove that, almost surely, \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π+C_*, \] and the set of subsequential limits is exactly \[ \left[\frac1π,\;\frac1π+C_*\right]. \] Here $C_*>1/π$ is a constant uniquely determined by an equation. The lower-limit identity remains valid under the weaker assumption that $\mathbb{E}|ξ_0|^{2+δ}<\infty$ for some $δ>0$.
Many more odd zeta values are irrational
Stéphane Fischler; Li Lai; Johannes Sprang; Wadim Zudilin

We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $ζ(3), ζ(5), \dots, ζ(s)$, where $ζ$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.
Conditional Gaussian Limits and Character Laws for Randomized Symmetric-Group Representations

Let $ρ_n$ be a real orthogonal representation of the symmetric group $S_n$ of dimension $d_n\to\infty$, let $σ_n$ be a uniform random permutation, and let $O_n$ be an independent Haar-orthogonal matrix. We study the linear statistics $\operatorname{Tr}(A_nO_nρ_n(σ_n)O_n^T)$ for deterministic real test matrices $A_n$ normalized only in Frobenius norm, which allows tests that isolate individual entries. Conditionally on $σ_n$, the statistic has mean $s_nχ_n(σ_n)$, where $χ_n$ is the character of $ρ_n$ and $s_n=d_n^{-1}\operatorname{Tr} A_n\to s$. We show that the centered statistic has conditional Gaussian limit $N(0,1-s^2)$ for every such test if and only if the trivial and sign constituents of $ρ_n$ occupy $o(d_n)$ dimensions, and that this limit is asymptotically independent of every convergent $σ_n$-measurable observable. The key input is a tensor-square estimate, based on the Frobenius-Schur identity and the minimum degree of non-linear irreducible representations of $S_n$, which shows that this single condition controls both normalized traces needed in the Haar-conjugation argument. For the uncentered statistic, convergence in distribution of $χ_n(σ_n)$ to a law $Ξ$ is necessary and sufficient for every test statistic to converge to $sΞ+\sqrt{1-s^2}G$, with $G$ standard Gaussian and independent of $Ξ$. For every irreducible sequence with $d_n\to\infty$, finitely many entries scaled by $\sqrt{d_n}$ have independent standard Gaussian limits. Finally, we compute $Ξ$ explicitly for diagrams with a fixed first-row tail, their transposes, and diagrams with sublinear largest hook, answering in these cases a question of Tsou.

We study a Nim-adjacent poset game, where chips are arranged in a pyramid and two players take turns removing chips that do not currently support chips to the upper-left and upper-right; upon removing this chip, all supported chips above are also removed. Play continues until the final chip is removed. We use a bijection between the game states, Dyck paths, and unit interval graphs to count the number of possible game states up to isomorphism.

We give an information-theoretic formulation of two-stage secret sharing for situations in which secret information becomes available progressively. In the proposed model, shares for an initial part of the secret are distributed before the remaining part becomes available, and additional shares are distributed to new participants after the remaining part becomes available, without updating the shares already distributed and without using any additional information other than shares. To characterize this setting, we propose the notion of a two-stage access structure and provide its characterization. We further quantify the amount of information about the first-stage secret that the dealer must retain between the two distribution stages, derive a universal lower bound, and present a construction that achieves this bound for every two-stage access structure. We also position advance sharing as a special case of the proposed model and give its characterization and a related construction in classical information-theoretic secret sharing.
Congruences Modulo 16, 32 and 64 for a Restricted Overpartition Function

Let $\overline{t}^{(3)}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which consecutive parts differ by a multiple of $3$ unless the larger part is overlined, and the smallest part is overlined unless it is divisible by $3$. Using dissections of theta functions, we establish two infinite families of congruences modulo $32$ and $64$. We also obtain two residue formulas modulo $16$ and use them to derive four further infinite families of congruences modulo $16$. In particular, for every positive integer $M$ and nonnegative integer $n$, the residue of $\overline{t}^{(3)}(M^2(18n+12))$ modulo $16$ is $8$ if $6n+4$ is a square and $0$ otherwise.
Fast circular convolution with periodic kernels
Fernando González del Cueto; Fernando Guevara Vasquez

We study the periodic circular convolution or PCC, where the convolution kernel depends periodically on the spatial location. We introduce two fast algorithms to compute the PCC that rely on the Discrete Fourier Transform. One of the algorithms reveals that the matrix representation of the PCC is unitarily equivalent to a block diagonal matrix, which facilitates the analysis of PCCs and operations such as their product and inversion. We present two sample applications. One to deconvolve the action of an optical system whose point spread function depends periodically in space. The second is to compute dispersion relations for a periodic chain of masses.
Gradient Flows over Convex Bodies for Learning Optimal Regularizers
Nilava Metya; Oscar Leong; Yong Sheng Soh

We consider the question of describing gradient flows over the collection of convex bodies. This is motivated by foundational questions arising in inverse problems. Suppose we wish to solve an ill-posed inverse problem using regularization techniques. Can we learn an optimal choice of a convex regularizer directly from prior data? Given a numerical algorithm that computes such an optimal regularizer, is there a principled manner for describing the evolution of its iterates? The objective of this paper is to lay the foundation towards answering these questions. To this end, we consider a criterion of an optimal regularizer based on seeking a convex body that minimizes the expected gauge evaluation with respect to a prior data distribution subject to a volume constraint. The formulation is initially nonconvex, but admits hidden convexity by passing to its polar. We characterize the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions that certify global optimality. We also analyze the $L^2$-gradient flow as well as a minimizing movement scheme with the Hausdorff penalty. Our results show that the objective gap decays exponentially along the gradient flow and we obtain dimension-dependent rates for both the objective gap and distance to the optimal body for the Hausdorff scheme. Finally, we apply the KKT conditions to identify explicit optimal convex bodies. For data where the optimal nonconvex regularizer is the $\ell_p$-quasinorm, $p \in (0,1)$, the optimal convex regularizer is the volume-normalized $\ell_1$-ball. For data described by paired basis atoms, the optimal convex regularizer is the polar of a shifted zonotope.

We determine the asymptotically sharp minimum number of $q$-cliques that appear in any $n$-vertex graph with $γn^2$ edges and $δn^{p}$ $p$-cliques for $q>p>2$. The question of determining the minimum number of $r$-cliques that appear in any $n$-vertex graph with $γn^2$ edges was previously resolved by Razborov for $r=3$, Nikiforov for $r=4$ and Reiher for all $r\geq 5$. For all $r\geq 3$, the minimum is attained by a complete multipartite graph where all parts are equal except for one that can be smaller or by a limit of such graphs. Very recently, Ma, Wang and Zhu as well as Li, Liu and Zhang showed that the same construction is also a minimizer for the number of $r$-cliques when the number of $s$-cliques is fixed for any $2\leq s<r$. A minimizer in our setting is the disjoint union of the same complete multipartite graph with an independent set. This establishes the lower boundary of the three-dimensional $\{K_2, K_p, K_q\}$-profile.
John Francis; Owen Gwilliam; Rajiv Kaipa

We describe a quantization procedure for Betti mapping stacks with shifted Poisson targets by combining factorization homology and formal geometry. We quantize derived stacks of local systems of low-dimensional manifolds.
Aldo Garcia Guinto; Lucas Hall; Brent Nelson

We define a locally compact quantum group $\mathbb{G}$ to be almost unimodular if its modular element is diagonalizable. This is shown to be equivalent to the almost periodicity of a novel weight on the dual von Neumann algebra, which we call the middle Haar weight. The point modular spectrum of this weight is related to the point spectrum of $δ$, and we prove that unimodularity of $\mathbb{G}$ is equivalent to traciality of this weight. When $δ$ is affiliated with the center of $L^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, we show that there is a canonical closed, normal, unimodular quantum subgroup $\mathbb{G}_1 \leq \mathbb{G}$ which assumes the role of the unimodular part of $\mathbb{G}$, and moreover the openness of this quantum subgroup is equivalent to the almost periodicity of $\mathbb{G}$. Additionally, we establish several permanence properties of almost unimodularity.
A global rigidity criterion for Coxeter $3$-polytopes

We give a combinatorial condition ensuring global projective rigidity of simple hyperbolic Coxeter $3$-polytopes. As an application, we prove that every right-angled Löbell polytope is globally rigid.
A Probabilistic Characterization of the Ideals of Resolvent Algebras

We characterize the ideal theory of Buchholz for resolvent algebras in probabilistic terms. Regarding closed two-sided ideals as kernels of representations, we pass from representations to the Gelfand--Naimark--Segal representations of states, and describe the singular, trivially regular, and regular parts, which Buchholz gives through the one-particle space, by the behavior of the corresponding probability measures of the fields. On an isotropic subspace, the resolvent algebra is a commutative $C^{\ast}$-algebra whose states correspond to probability measures, and this correspondence carries the description further to sub-$σ$-algebras. Starting from Bose--Einstein condensation of the free Bose gas with its direct integral representation and from the treatment of the infrared singularity of the van Hove model, we connect the ideal-theoretic and the probabilistic arguments. Since the ideals carry physical information in these arguments, we show that the corresponding sub-$σ$-algebras and their inclusions carry this information in correspondence with the ideals.
Maximum Principles and Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Models
Willian Cintra; Jônatas Peralta; Julio D. Rossi; Antonio Suárez

In this paper, we analyze the validity of the maximum principle and the existence of a principal eigenvalue for a problem involving two regions, in one of them the main operator is the classical Laplacian (a local operator) while in the other region the operator is a nonlocal one (these regions are coupled via a transmission term that is also nonlocal). The main difficulty here comes from the lack of compactness of the nonlocal part that occurs since we are considering non-singular kernels.

We prove that $\mathbb{Z}$ is a Diophantine subset of $\mathbb{Q}$. More precisely, there exist an integer $m\ge 1$ and a polynomial of total degree at most four in $m+1$ variables whose rational zero set projects onto $\mathbb{Z}$ under the first coordinate. We construct a Diophantine model of $\mathbb{Z}$ on an elliptic curve and use it to define real intervals with rational endpoints, each containing an integer. A denominator bound identifies a rational number in a sufficiently short interval with that integer. The key ingredients are a criterion for square denominators, obtained using the Tian--Yuan--Zhang genus-point criterion for congruent number elliptic curves, and a height bound from quaternionic abelian surfaces. The Green--Tao theorem supplies prime progressions needed to define squaring, and hence multiplication, in the model. Our proof is inspired by OpenAI's approach to Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$, but does not rely on the $2$-converse or $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and invoked by OpenAI.

These notes, which are based on four lectures delivered at the summer school "Knotted Surfaces in Four-Manifolds" at PCMI in 2026, discuss classifications of locally flat surfaces in simply-connected $4$-manifolds.
Condorcet's nontransitive dice: A minimal realization of a complete ranking profile
Sándor Bozóki; László Csató; József Temesi

We construct three independent finite-support random variables whose six strict ordering probabilities reproduce the complete ranking-frequency profile in a classical example of Condorcet's paradox. The construction has total support size seven, and we prove that no realization of this profile has smaller total support size. Here dice are allowed to be weighted: different outcomes need not have equal probabilities. We then formulate the realization problem for an arbitrary vector of six ordering probabilities. We distinguish constraints on the pairwise comparison probabilities from constraints on the full ranking distribution and give an example showing that pairwise feasibility is not sufficient. For the fixed interlaced supports $\{1,4,7\}$, $\{2,5,8\}$, and $\{3,6,9\}$, we derive the polynomial realization system. On the branch where the smallest outcome of the second variable has probability zero, we give a compact polynomial characterization for profiles with their first two ordering probabilities positive. This yields an explicit semialgebraic sufficient condition for the general realization problem and a rational construction, both with elementary proofs.
Michelson and Logarithmic Operator Contrasts Spectral Geometry, Tracial Extensions, and Random Products

The Michelson contrast of a positive invertible operator is a bounded coordinate for its condition number. Its logarithmic lift, $\operatorname{OLC}(A)=\frac12\log(\|A\|\|A^{-1}\|)$, connects spectral spread with projective Thompson geometry. This preprint collects the Novikov--Nikolaeva series and the associated single-author extensions by Novikov into one treatment. We develop the equality criterion for product subadditivity, its dimension and Jordan-rank thresholds, quantum-state examples, and contrasts associated with unitarily invariant norms. The latter have a sharp additive defect, while the full Schatten family records a logarithmic spectral profile up to homometry. Tracial extensions give characterisations of traces, dimension-sensitive defects, and spectral-edge asymptotics. Unbounded operators are described through critical exponents and finite sections. Tensor, matrix and free independence lead to distinct growth laws for products. Finally, symmetric cones provide a setting for the equality criterion, Lorentz boosts, and Jordan products. Classical ingredients are distinguished from the refinements developed in the series; conjectural asymptotic statements remain explicitly labelled.
An ODE to Changing Variables: $v = y/x$ Is For Victory
Joseph Kraisler; Kayla S. Miller; Steven J. Miller

Most first courses in differential equations introduce students to very special differential equations which can be solved in closed form from a small set of techniques (such as separable equations and integrating factors). Frequently other equations can be converted to one of these forms through a change of variable; however, these transformations are usually just given without any explanation of \emph{how} people found them, or \emph{why} problems of these forms have nice solutions, but not related ones. We consider the first order differential equation $dy/dx = f(x,y)$ where $f(x,y)$ does not factor as $A(x)B(y)$, and assume $f(x,y) = g(y/x^r)$ for some nice function $g$ and some real number $r$. This can be reduced to a separable equation only when $r=1$. We then discuss generalizations and what conditions on $f$ lead to a change of variables yielding a separable equation. Our goals are twofold. First, to encourage students and instructors to be active, questioning the methods and results, seeing how far they can be extended and why they work. Second, we discuss how to appropriately use AI to take ideas and special cases as prompts and quickly create extensions and editable notes that can be shared with students, freeing up professors (and students) from straightforward calculations \emph{without} sacrificing learning and understanding.
Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices

Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.
Portfolio-Size Constraints on Default Correlation: Exact Coherence Tests and Sharp Asymptotic Bounds

An absorbing default process imposes joint restrictions on cumulative default distributions across horizons. We characterize these restrictions for finite homogeneous portfolios. For binomial mixtures whose mixing distribution functions cross at most once, stochastic ordering of the entire default count is equivalent to two inequalities: the probability of no defaults must be nonincreasing and the probability of all defaults must be nondecreasing. In the one-factor Gaussian model, these inequalities give an exact interval of admissible later correlations, obtained from two scalar equations. The intervals are nested as portfolio size increases. If the earlier and later default probabilities are $p_0<p_1$ and the earlier latent correlation is $ρ_0\in(0,1)$, both interval boundaries approach $ρ_0$ at rate $(\log n)^{-1/2}$, with common leading magnitude $ρ_0\sqrt{2(1-ρ_0)}[Φ^{-1}(p_1)-Φ^{-1}(p_0)]$. We also give a constructive absorbing coupling, an exact sequential repair, differential conditions for smooth horizon curves, and a finite-size certificate of incompatibility. Log-domain quadrature, bracketed root finding, and deterministic numerical experiments evaluate the intervals and verify the restrictions on the full count distribution. The framework provides a feasibility analysis of prescribed horizon laws.
Lower semicontinuity of dimension for quasi-Bernoulli measures under conformal projections

We study the dependence of the Hausdorff dimension of projected quasi-Bernoulli measures on a conformal iterated function system on the real line. For every fixed quasi-Bernoulli probability measure on the symbolic space, we prove that the dimension of its push-forward under the coding map is lower semicontinuous in the $C^{1+θ}$ topology, without any separation assumption or shift-invariance requirement on the symbolic measure. The proof combines bounded distortion and finite-scale entropy estimates with uniform control of the entropy dimension over measures whose densities are bounded above and below. For invariant Gibbs measures associated with Hölder continuous potentials, we also prove joint lower semicontinuity with respect to the defining system and the potential. As an application, we obtain a generic dimension formula: for each fixed shift-invariant quasi-Bernoulli measure, a dense $G_δ$ set of systems with derivative moduli strictly less than 1/2 has projected dimension equal to the minimum of one and the entropy-to-Lyapunov-exponent ratio.
Rank-One Sutured Instanton Homology Detects Homology Products

We prove that a balanced sutured manifold $(M,γ)$ satisfying $\dim_{\mathbb C} SHI(M,γ)=1$ is an integral homology product; that is, $H_*(M,R_-(γ);\mathbb Z)=H_*(M,R_+(γ);\mathbb Z)=0$. Consequently, for every taut balanced sutured manifold $(M,γ)$, $SHI(M,γ)\cong\mathbb C$ if and only if $(M,γ)$ is a product sutured manifold. The proof uses the enhanced Euler characteristic of $SHI$ and a specialization formula for sutured torsion.
Minimality of the Double Kite among Strict Two-Pole Configurations of Unit Triangles

A strict unit-triangle configuration is a finite connected family of closed equilateral unit triangles in which distinct triangles are disjoint or meet at a common vertex, and no vertex belongs to more than two triangles. A vertex belonging to exactly one triangle is a pole. We prove that every strict configuration with one or two poles contains at least fourteen triangles, a sharp bound for two poles attained by the double kite and the reverse double kite. A strict four-regular configuration whose contact graph has an edge cut of size at most two contains at least twenty-eight triangles. A decomposition into three strict two-pole components requires forty-two triangles; both known ring constructions attain the bound. The proof reduces minimal counterexamples to two-connected contact graphs, applies area bounds to complementary unit-sided polygons, and excludes the remaining cases by exact angle certificates. The supplement contains 13,668 stored marked records, 233 exclusion certificates, a standard-library verifier, and independent checks of the complete enumeration.
Two-Sided Projection-Based Model Reduction of Parametric Generalized Algebraic Riccati Equations via Grassmann-Manifold Optimization
Xuelian Wen; Qiuqi Li; Juan Zhang

Parametric generalized algebraic Riccati equations arise in many-query problems in optimal control, state estimation, and filtering, where repeated full-order solutions may become computationally prohibitive for large-scale systems. In this paper, within a projection-based model reduction framework, we propose a two-sided projection approach that constructs reduced bases by minimizing the aggregate relative two-sided projection error of Riccati solution snapshots. Under suitable dissipativity assumptions, the resulting Galerkin-projected PGARE admits a unique symmetric positive semidefinite stabilizing solution. For error assessment, we employ an existing residual-based a posteriori error estimator for the full-order Riccati residual. A projection-based error decomposition developed in this work provides the theoretical motivation for the proposed basis construction. To accommodate clustered solution manifolds, we extend the framework to localized model reduction by combining parameter-space proximity and solution-space correlation for clustering, with classifier-based online basis selection. Numerical experiments on parameterized heat-conduction problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed global and localized approaches in terms of approximation accuracy and computational efficiency.
Support recovery of diffusion models under the manifold hypothesis
Ayya Alieva; Gautam Iyer; Alexei Novikov; Lenya Ryzhik

We study diffusion models under the manifold hypothesis with possibly large score estimation and discretization errors, and show that while they may not exactly recover the data distribution, they will exactly recover the support (or data manifold). In continuous time, we use a Lyapunov function to show that even if the relative score estimation error is fixed (and not necessarily vanishing), then the rate at which the process approaches the support is $O(\sqrt{(T-t)|\log(T-t)|})$ as $t \to T$, where $T$ is the final time. In discrete time, we use geometric time steps with a fixed (non-vanishing) ratio and show that with a fixed (also not small) relative score estimation error, the process approaches the data manifold exponentially with the number of iterations. The proof relies on controlling a Gaussian measure of a neighborhood of the cut-locus of the data manifold, using a polynomial approximation argument combined with quantitative semi-algebraic estimates.
TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints

We construct pathological TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints (SECs) in the sense that, if a smaller collection of SECs is imposed, then the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson model returns a disconnected solution costing less than an optimal tour. For asymmetric instances on $n$ vertices, we prove a growth rate of \(Ω(ϕ^n)\), where \(ϕ\approx 1.618\) is the golden ratio. A node-splitting reduction gives metric instances with \(Ω(ϕ^{n/2})\) growth. We also give instances in the plane under the Euclidean, Rectilinear, and Maximum metrics that require exponentially many SECs. Concorde struggles on them, with solve times growing exponentially despite tiny integrality gaps.
Remarks on Souriau's Geometric Thermodynamics for Weak Two-Dimensional Euler Flows

We examine infinitesimal symmetries of relative entropy on low-regularity vorticity spaces and compare them with symmetries of stationary laws of weak two-dimensional Euler trajectories. Relative-entropy invariance under sample-space transformations is equivalent to preservation of the reference law; the corresponding weak infinitesimal condition is a vanishing reference-divergence identity. White-noise vorticity has an infinite-dimensional family of such symmetries, generated by smooth area-preserving transport. At the level of path laws, however, marginal entropy symmetries need not preserve temporal correlations. We first give a continuous Gaussian counterexample, including its infinitesimal form. We then establish a counterexample directly for stationary white-noise weak Euler path laws: explicit non-isometric area-preserving shears preserve the white-noise marginal but cannot preserve an Euler path law satisfying the standard symmetrized weak vorticity equation. We also examine the reduction of guaranteed entropy symmetries under conditioning by renormalized energy. These observations distinguish thermodynamic symmetry, Hamiltonian covariance, and statistical path dynamics without asserting a selection principle for nonunique weak solutions.
Erratum to Power boundedness and related properties for weighted composition operators on $\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, Journal of Functional Analysis 288 (2025), 110745
Vicente Asensio; Enrique Jordá; Thomas Kalmes

As was kindly pointed out to us by S. Li, the proofs of Theorem 2.11 and Lemma 3.1 in our original paper contain errors that require modifications of the corresponding statements. We also correct a gap in the proof of Lemma 2.1, whose statement remains valid. Furthermore, we explain the consequences for several subsequent results and provide the necessary corrections to their statements and proofs.
Toward a Holographic Representation Theory of the Bosonic de Sitter Discrete Series
Maryam Bajalan; Jean-Pierre Gazeau; Hamed Pejhan

We propose a program toward a holographic representation theory of the non-scalar bosonic discrete series $Π^\pm_{p,q}$, $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$, $1\leqslant q\leqslant p$, of the de Sitter ($\mathrm{dS}_{4}$) group $G=\mathrm{SO}_0(1,4)$. The proposal exploits two complementary realizations of the same unitary irreducible representation (UIR): a bounded-domain realization on an open ball $\mathbb{B}$ modeling the hyperbolic space $G/\mathrm{SO}(4)$, with $\partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, and a covariant spacetime realization on $\mathrm{dS}_{4}$, with conformal boundaries $\mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, in which the physical UIR is obtained through the corresponding gauge reduction. This leads to two boundary constructions and an explicit compatibility problem, \begin{align*} \mathbb{B} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \quad\overset{?}{\simeq}\quad \mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \mathrm{dS}_{4} \,. \end{align*} The two outer problems seek explicit intertwiners between the bulk and boundary realizations, with their invariant norms, constraints, and physical quotients properly identified. The middle problem asks how to construct and normalize a unitary intertwiner between the two boundary realizations once both have been shown to carry the same UIR. The bounded picture exposes the unitary and harmonic structure of the representation, while the spacetime picture makes its covariant and gauge-theoretic structure manifest, allowing the two constructions to constrain and illuminate one another. The established scalar family $Π_{p,0}$, $p\in\mathbb{N}$, with its spherical realization on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$, provides the guiding prototype. Particular attention is given to ...
Region Coloring of Spatial Graphs using Knot-theoretic Ternary Quasigroups

We construct coloring conditions around vertices for region colorings of unoriented spatial graph diagrams by knot-theoretic ternary quasigroups. These conditions require cyclic products of left and right operators around each vertex to be the identity. We prove that the resulting coloring sets are preserved under the generalized Reidemeister moves and relate our construction to the palette framework. We show that the vertex coloring conditions are automatic for Dehn tribrackets and determine the associated palettes for unoriented Alexander tribrackets. We also introduce an additional restriction on vertex colorings that is preserved under the fifth Reidemeister move for every unoriented knot-theoretic ternary quasigroup. This restriction gives rise to further coloring invariants for Dehn tribrackets and unoriented Alexander tribrackets.
A $19/5$ lower bound for the four-dimensional Erdős box problem

For every power $q\ge2$ of~$2$, we construct a box-free subset of $[q^5]^4$ with $q^{19}$ points, improving the lower-bound exponent in the four-dimensional Erdős box problem from $15/4$ to $19/5$. In fact, $[q^5]^4$ partitions into $q$ isomorphic box-free sets. The proof uses a finite-field rectangle lemma and orthogonality in a four-dimensional bilinear space. We also deduce a uniform bound $f_4(n)\ge2^{-19/20}n^{19/5}$ and a lower bound for grid-coloring numbers.
Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends

We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.
Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy

Let $G=F\rtimes_ϕ\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $ϕ$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece. Otherwise, the distortion of $H$ is quadratic if all dilation homomorphisms are trivial, and exponential if one of them is nontrivial. Along the way, we show that the distortion of $H$ is determined, up to superadditive closure, by the distortions of the stabilizers of its horizontal components.
Machine learning and high accuracy: Neural preconditioners for computational gravity

Machine learning (ML) developments have empowered valuable calculations in many areas of theoretical physics. Certain topics involving moderate-to-low accuracy requirements have been particularly fortunate because many ML techniques, such as neural networks, introduce a noise floor that would be difficult to penetrate with stricter tolerances. For this reason, topics requiring high accuracy can be hesitant to pursue ML. One prominent example is gravitational wave modeling, which relies on traditional methods that accommodate the high sensitivities of detectors such as LISA. However, recent progress in applied mathematics has identified hybrid methods where fast-but-noisy ML mechanisms are inserted into otherwise traditional numerical schemes to accelerate convergence in a way that ultimately meets or exceeds the accuracy of standard methods. We develop an optimized hybrid ML method to tackle a class of challenging PDEs; specifically, we demonstrate ML implementations for gravitational waves from asymmetric-mass black hole binaries and elastic waves. These require solving sparse linear algebra systems with Helmholtz features that are especially difficult for traditional iterative methods. Our new approach is to train a graph neural network (GNN) as a significantly faster preconditioner using a novel loss function based on the true residual of the iterative algorithm. For the most difficult regions of parameter space, our neural preconditioner decreases iteration counts by 2-15x compared to traditional preconditioners. Because the GNN operates directly on the sparse matrix and needs only modest physical context, it generalizes beyond its training domain and can be adapted to new problems across physics by retraining rather than redesign. Hybrid ML methods such as this offer a new and compelling avenue to handle high accuracy and speed requirements in gravitational wave modeling and beyond.
Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain

We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$. At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques. Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.
Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"

In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,α): x\in U, α\in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),α(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).
Convergence rates for truncated and discretised signature expansions
Eduardo Abi Jaber; Dorinel Bastide; Ronan Pécheul; Clément Rey

Linear expansions in Brownian Stratonovich signatures, which originate in stochastic Taylor expansions, are increasingly used to represent and model processes with memory. Their numerical use requires truncating the signature at a level $M$ and discretising the driving path along $N$ steps. Under a simple growth condition on the coefficients of the linear expansion, we establish strong and weak convergence rates for both approximations, uniformly in time. The strong truncation error decays like $(B^M/(M!)^\varepsilon)^a$ for some constant $B$, uniformly in $N$, where $\varepsilon$ measures the growth of the coefficients and $a$ the regularity of the test function; the weak error does not improve on it. The discretisation error is of order $N^{-a/2}$ in $L^p$, and $N^{-1}$ weakly for polynomial test functions, uniformly in $M$. All these rates are sharp for polynomial test functions, and $M$, $N$ can be chosen independently. We extend the estimates to errors in probability, on distribution functions and on risk measures, and illustrate them on stochastic delay equations, Volterra processes and option pricing in signature volatility models.
Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
A. N. Abyzov; O. V. Lyubimtsev; A. A. Tuganbaev

A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.
An Optimized Expansion Auction Integrating Energy, Flexibility, and Network Constraints
Rafael Benchimol Klausner; Alexandre Street; Joaquim Dias Garcia; Luiz Barroso

Auction mechanisms are widely used to support generation investments. In the US, capacity auctions serve as supply-adequacy instruments to address the missing-money problem, whereas in Latin America, energy and capacity auctions procure long-term contracts to support generation expansion. In both settings, accreditation metrics, such as Firm Energy (FE) and Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), are used to approximate the reliability contribution of selected units and winning projects are selected based on a financial offer. This approach fails to recognize the actual contribution of winners to the multiple services they provide to the system. This limitation becomes more significant with high shares of renewables, as the value of each resource increasingly depends on network and technological constraints, as well as on complementarities within the generation portfolio. Inspired by short-term auctions, such as day-ahead markets, this paper proposes a joint optimization-based auction for generation and transmission investments that internalizes these interactions, capturing the intrinsic value of generation candidates without requiring the computation of FE or ELCC metrics. The auctioneer determines the winning portfolio through an expansion-planning model that explicitly represents network constraints, operational interactions, reliability standards, and multiple scenarios. A case study of the Brazilian system indicates lower system costs, lower risk, and a more diverse portfolio relative to the stylized decoupled procurement approaches currently deployed in many systems.
Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted étale groupoid model
Nikolay A. Ivanov; Ali I. Raad

We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal étale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.
Jonah Gaster; Didac Martinez-Granado; Christopher-Lloyd Simon

We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=Γ(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{π^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $λ$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $λ$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT). We indicate several avenues for further investigation.
Holographic Wilsonian RG of Yang-Mills theory in AdS

In this work, we extend the equilibrium-evolution duality between stochastic quantization and Wilsonian renormalization to non-abelian gauge theories in anti-de Sitter space, for which the radial coordinate of AdS plays the role of the stochastic time. We show, to all orders in the fields for bulk theories without explicit radial dependence, that the Langevin distribution at time $t$ is the product of the ultraviolet and infrared radial wavefunctions at the cutoff $ε=t$. We therefore identify this Langevin process as the ground-state (Doob) transform of the radial evolution. By explicit calculation, we also extend the existing dictionary in the stochastic-renormalization duality: the radial component of the bulk field is Zwanziger's stochastic gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization; and the bulk gauge $A_z=α^{-1}\partial_iA_i$ is Zwanziger's gauge. We also obtain the expressions for the triple-trace and quadruple-trace couplings of the holographic Wilsonian action at finite cutoff in closed form; in the infrared, they reduce to the known gluon correlators and, at the total-energy pole, to flat-space Yang-Mills amplitudes as expected. Although our explicit results are provided at tree-level and derived in AdS$_4$, we also comment on the de Sitter counterpart of these statements and on the loop corrections.
On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
Milena Brockhof; Giovane Galindo; Ludmil Katzarkov; Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins

Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.
Optimal Additive Integer Masks for One-Guess Vulnerability under an Absolute-Moment Budget

We study the average one-guess success probability of an adversary who observes the ordinary integer sum of a finite-support secret and an independent integer-valued mask, subject to an absolute-moment budget on the mask. For a uniform secret on an interval the exact optimum and an explicit optimiser are obtained. For a biased bit the masks that achieve no increase over the prior baseline are characterised, and the entire cost--vulnerability frontier is determined. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks. It has infinitely many affine pieces, which accumulate at the critical cost, where the frontier meets the prior baseline with zero slope. The proof rests on a layer-cake decomposition of an arbitrary mask into truncated geometrics, along which both the vulnerability and the cost are exactly additive. The results give exact design guidance for additive integer noise under the average one-guess metric.
Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications

Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(α)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. Utilizing the higher order Fourier analysis machinery of Green and Sawhney in their breakthrough work on the Gaussian prime conjecture, we show that if there are no local obstructions, then there are infinitely many $(x,y)\in \mathbb Z$ such that $L_1(x,y),\dots,L_k(x,y),$ and $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(x+yα)$ are simultaneously prime. We further establish an asymptotic formula which matches the prediction by the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture. We present two arithmetic applications of this prime counting result. First, we show that the Brauer--Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to weak approximation on a new family of varieties, including diagonal conic bundles all of whose degenerate fibres are defined over $\mathbb Q$ except one fibre that may be defined over an imaginary quadratic field. Second, we construct elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with infinitely many quadratic twists of rank exactly two.
Triply conservative schemes for degenerate convection-dispersion equations
Kaichang Yu; Juan Cheng; Chi-Wang Shu

It is well known that for numerically solving hyperbolic conservation laws, even a convergent numerical scheme still may not always converge to a weak solution. The remedy is the famous Lax-Wendroff theorem. In a recent work on degenerate convection-diffusion equations, an analogous phenomenon was identified and doubly conservative schemes were introduced. In this paper, we address the same issue for solving the following nonlinear degenerate dispersive or convection-dispersion equations: \begin{equation*} u_t+f(u)_x+A(u)_{xxx}=0. \end{equation*} The resulting equation is regarded as degenerate if $A'(u)$ is allowed to vanish. An important example is the Rosenau-Hyman $K(m,n)$ equation. In contrast to classical KdV solitons possessing exponentially decaying tails, $K(m,n)$ equations can admit compactly supported solitary waves, known as compactons, whose regularity can deteriorate at the boundary of their support. We first give an example in which both a classical conservative and doubly conservative scheme converges to a limit that fails to satisfy the ultra-weak formulation. To address this issue, we introduce the notion of a triply conservative (TriC) scheme and prove a Lax-Wendroff type theorem for consistent TriC schemes. Under suitable assumptions, a convergent sequence generated by a consistent TriC scheme will converge to an ultra-weak solution. Several existing high-order schemes are shown to have a TriC structure. We further introduce a new high-order TriC finite volume scheme based on a connection between triple cell averages and quadratic B-splines. The theory and the scheme are also suited for two-dimensional anisotropic problems and non-uniform meshes. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions confirm the high-order accuracy on smooth solutions and illustrate the behavior of the schemes for compactons and traveling fronts.

An edge map $f:E(G)\to E(H)$ between graphs is called an $FT_M$ map if the pullback of every $M$-tension on $H$ is an $M$-flow on $G$; equivalently, the pullback of every $M$-valued 1-coboundary is an $M$-valued 1-cycle. The correspondence between restricted tensions and homomorphisms to Cayley graphs motivates two flow analogues. An $(M,B)$-flow (or tension), is an $M$-flow (resp. $M$-tension) taking values in $B$. For subsets $B=-B\subseteq M$ with $M$ an abelian group, Šámal conjectured that a graph admits an $(M,B)$-flow if and only if it admits an $FT_M$ map to the Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)$. DeVos conjectured that, whenever there is a graph homomorphism $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)\to\operatorname{Cay}(M',B')$, every graph admitting an $(M,B)$-flow also admits an $(M',B')$-flow. We prove that these conjectures are equivalent and give a counterexample using the Petersen graph.
Floating Body Asymptotics via Fractal Strings

Schütt and Werner associated an almost polygonal planar convex body with a decreasing convex sequence and obtained two-sided estimates for the area removed by its floating body. We reinterpret the gaps of the defining sequence as the lengths of a normalized fractal string. Our main result shows that the area deficit, that is, the difference between the area of the set and its floating body, is comparable to an integral transform of the inner tubular volume of this string. As a consequence, if the string has Minkowski dimension $D$, then the principal power exponent of the area deficit is $1-D/3$. We also derive refinements for regularly varying tube functions, establish a realization criterion extending the almost polygonal case of the theorem of Schütt and Werner, and discuss several examples. As an application, we obtain corresponding asymptotic rates for the expectations and variances of the missed area and the number of vertices of random polygons, including new intermediate behaviors between the classical polygonal and smooth cases.
Your PID Is Already a Neural Network: Learning Its Gains with Only Three Weights and No Teacher
Felipe de Jesús Félix-Arredondo; Nezih Nieto-Gutiérrez; Carlos Astengo-Noguez; Alejandro Ucan-Puc

A discrete PID controller is exactly a recurrent neural network, a classical state-space fact: a fixed linear memory of the running integral and the last error, read out by three trainable weights that map one-to-one to the PID gains. Networks with bounded hidden states, such as LSTMs of any width, only approximate it. Trained only on a one-step physical cost (the expected cost of one transition from a fixed state distribution), with no demonstrations, teacher controller, or known gains, the network solves a strongly convex least-squares problem, so gradient descent converges from any initialization to the unique one-step optimal PID gains; the limit network is that PID, with the same action on every error sequence. Partitioned regression then shows what extra capacity buys. Orthogonal residual features keep these gains and improve on the PID if and only if they correlate with the part of the optimal action outside the PID span. On a nonlinear second-order example the gap is 5.88% of the optimal PID cost, and 4.00% against PID with a bias; no controller can improve on PID by more on this objective. A residual started at a tuned PID begins exactly at that PID; at the one-step optimal PID, a fixed-feature residual's first gradient step lowers the cost if and only if its features can improve on the PID. Experiments confirm the realization, recovery, and gap results to numerical precision. On held-out plants of three families, under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, a residual warm-started at a heavily tuned PID and trained with it lowers the long-horizon cost by 3.5%, 3.5%, and 1.9%, with family-wise 95% bounds excluding zero, also under distribution shift; a post hoc comparison with the PID tuned alone suggests that most of it comes from the recurrent part in two families. The primary endpoint, a gain of at least 5% from a generic PID start, is not met in any family.
The Wasserstein cost of the Girsanov Theorem

This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for Itô diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem. More precisely, let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the law of the solution of a stochastic differential equation with a bounded Lipschitz drift. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ be independent Brownian paths, and let $Z_i$ be their Girsanov weights for $\mathbb{Q}$. The reweighted empirical measure $$\widehatμ_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_iδ_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i}$$ approximates $\mathbb{Q}$ when $n$ is large. We prove that the Wasserstein cost $W_p^p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is of order $(\log n)^{-p/2}$, in expectation and almost surely, for every fixed $p\geqslant1$. In the Brownian case where $Z_i=1$ these results show that $\sqrt{\log n}W_p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is asymptotically sandwiched between $\sqrt{2λ_d}$ and $4\sqrt{2λ_d}$, where $λ_d$ is the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in the unit ball. We provide numerical experiments to estimate the (conjectured) limiting constant in dimension $d=1$.
MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to stay positive in the expanding regime

We study MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to remain positive for a long time when $|θ|>1$, where $θ$ denotes the coupling parameter. We show that, for a fixed starting point, the finite-dimensional distributions of the conditioned process converge and identify the limiting process as a Doob $h$-transform with explicit function $h$. We also obtain precise asymptotics for the corresponding persistence probabilities. The limiting process exhibits qualitatively different behaviour depending on $θ$ and on the support of the innovation distribution. We also determine stationary distributions of the limiting conditioned processes for all $θ\ne 1$.
Tautological generation of preprojective BPS cohomology

Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mathbf{d}$ be a dimension vector. We prove that the affinized BPS cohomology of the stack of $\mathbf{d}$-dimensional representations of the preprojective algebra $Π_Q$ is generated by its reduced virtual fundamental class under the action of tautological classes. This is a generalisation to singular quiver varieties of the Kirwan surjectivity statement of McGerty-Nevins for smooth framed quiver varieties. We prove that the statement holds for every King stability condition. To prove this, we attach legs to vertices of $Q$ and construct a correspondence with a smooth quiver variety for the extended quiver. This correspondence sends the reduced virtual fundamental class of the singular preprojective quiver stack to the Vandermonde determinant capped with the fundamental class of the smooth preprojective quiver stack for the leg-extended quiver. We construct the Weyl group action by the simultaneous Springer resolution of Dobrovolska-Ginzburg-Travkin, providing a comparison of the cohomology of fibres. This comparison preserves the tautological Chern classes. The sign-isotypic formula involving Kac polynomials of Hausel-Letellier-Rodriguez-Villegas, combined with Kirwan surjectivity for smooth framed quiver varieties of McGerty-Nevins, then implies the tautological generation theorem. We also describe the sign isotypic component of the cohomology of quiver varieties using the real-root subalgebras of the BPS Lie algebra. The tautological generation result can be extended via similar methods to deformed preprojective algebras of Crawley-Boevey-Holland at central parameters.
Comparing grade restriction windows to Cox windows
David Favero; Mykola Sapronov; Dash Stevanovich

We introduce a new class of toric varieties which admit an HKKN stratification compatible with the combinatorics of the GKZ fan. This class includes all smooth projective toric varieties of Picard ranks 1 and 2. We show that the grade restriction windows due to Halpern-Leistner and Ballard--Favero--Katzarkov arising from our HKKN stratifications agree with the intrinsic window categories appearing in work of Ballard--Berkesch--Brown--Cranton Heller--Erman--Favero--Ganatra--Hanlon--Huang. On the other hand, we provide an example of a smooth projective toric DM stack where this intrinsic window is never a grade restriction window despite the many possible choices. As an application, we demonstrate that reordering and/or taking a subset of an HKKN stratification sometimes changes the grade restriction window and sometimes does not.
Formal completions and decompositions of matrix factorization categories of Fano mirrors

We study the derived categories of matrix factorizations for certain toric Landau--Ginzburg models that are mirror dual to del Pezzo surfaces and Fano threefolds. Some of these models have non-isolated singularities: their critical loci may contain curves and surfaces, possibly with intersecting irreducible components. We handle these cases by studying the potential in the formal neighborhood of each irreducible component of the critical locus. Away from $\operatorname{Sing}(\operatorname{CritLoc}(W)_{\mathrm{red}})$, we construct global formal coordinates and determine the local normal form of the singularity. Near the singular or intersection strata, we analyze how the pieces of the whole connected formal neighborhood are related by localization. This gives explicit decompositions of the derived categories of matrix factorizations after idempotent completion. For the five rank-one pairs $(B_d,V_{4d+2})$, we also compare projective compactifications. The isolated sectors and central-component counts agree for $d=2,3,4,5$ and differ for $d=1$. Equivalence of the distinguished compactified contributions for the remaining matched pairs requires compatible global gluing data or compactified Homological Mirror Symmetry.
Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras

We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius. This settles a question of Hernandez--Walton--Yadav and unifies a wealth of results in the literature. We conclude with applications to topological quantum field theories and Poincaré duality algebras.
Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection for Embedded Hypercubes and Beta--Gaussian Mixtures
Ali Darijani; Emadedin Soufian; Jürgen Beyerer

We derive closed-form Gaussian information projections of Beta--Gaussian distributions whose tangential components are supported on affine embedded hypercubes and whose normal components are Gaussian. The optimal Gaussian is uniquely characterized by moment matching, and the corresponding minimum Kullback--Leibler divergence admits an explicit expression depending only on the intrinsic Beta parameters, independently of the embedding geometry, ambient dimension, and normal Gaussian parameters. In the uniform case, this divergence reduces to a linear function of the intrinsic dimension. We further extend this construction to finite, pure embedded cubical complexes by considering mixtures of the componentwise Gaussian projections. Using the joint convexity of the Kullback--Leibler divergence, we establish an explicit upper bound on the approximation error of the resulting Gaussian Mixture. For uniform tangential distributions and volume-based mixture weights, the bound is linear in the intrinsic dimension and independent of the geometry of the complex, its embedding, and the normal Gaussian parameters.
Fréchet structure over AF algebras I: The compact case

This is the first of two papers devoted to spatial Fréchet structures on AF algebras and their derivations. Here, we study the simplest example of such a structure: the Fréchet algebra of almost-local compact operators associated with a fixed orthonormal basis. We revisit the characterization of its continuous derivations in terms of infinite matrices and their operator-theoretic implementation on rapidly decreasing vectors. Reformulating this description in the language of 0-chains, borrowed from the theory of quantum many-body systems, we establish a sufficient condition for continuity in terms of spatial growth. Finally, we construct a Fréchet-continuous symmetric derivation that does not generate a one-parameter group of automorphisms of this algebra that is strongly continuous with respect to its Fréchet topology.
On the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups

The goal of this paper is to start proving the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.
Generic unipotent representations of finite reductive groups

Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a generic reductive group in the sense of Broué--Malle--Michel. We construct a category over $\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}]$ which interpolates between the various categories of unipotent representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ as we specialize $t$ to $q$. We use this category to show two properties of the unipotent decomposition matrix of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ mod $\ell$ (not dividing $q$): that, uniformly in $(q,\ell)$, there are finitely many such matrices and that for $\ell$ large enough, depending only on $\mathbb{G}$, this decomposition matrix depends only on the root of unity corresponding to $q$ mod $\ell$. We also prove that for $q$ and $q'$ two prime powers that are $\ell$-adically close enough, the categories of unipotent mod $\ell$ representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(q')$ are equivalent.
Zero detection via Cox random measures

Using point process theory we propose and investigate a probabilistic identification of zeros of a deterministic real valued function. We construct a random atomic driving measure for a Cox point process whose mass at a candidate location depends explicitly on the value of the function at that location. We study the properties of the constructed random measure, including its exact asymptotic properties, its Laplace functional and related random processes. We also give an important application involving zero detection for Riemann's ξ function.
Invariant random compacts for $\times p, \times q$ on the circle

We prove that for multiplicatively independent natural numbers $p,q \ge 2$, if $μ$ is a Borel probability measure on the space $\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{T})$ of nonempty compact subsets of the circle $\mathbb{T}$ which is invariant under the induced actions of both multiplication by $p$ and $q$, and $μ$-a.e. $Y$ has positive Hausdorff dimension, then $μ$-a.e. $Y$ is equal to $\mathbb{T}$.
Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures

We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(σ)$ to $L^q(ω)$ for the operator $H_σg(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,dσ$, where $σ$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $ω$ is a $σ$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $κ_{p,q}$ in $C_*\leκ_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $ω$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Osękowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms.
